author: sm06224
body:
…undary design

Adds a design draft that fixes terminology, compares candidate orphan definitions, compares UX strategies, and records a recommended direction for a future v3 implementation. No implementation in this PR.

Goal: before broadening "orphan" to span both relations-based and markdown-reference connectedness, lock down the terminology and the boundary so a future v3 implementation cannot reintroduce the "Backlinks"-style ambiguity this codebase has already fought off once.

Draft content (8 sections):
- §0 TL;DR
- §1 Current state — what v1 orphan means and does NOT mean, and why link-index is excluded today (5 reasons)
- §2 Terminology — explicit table with canonical vs provisional names; `unified orphan` and bare `orphan` are banned; existing code names (`pkc-orphan-marker`, `buildConnectedLidSet`, `data-pkc-orphan`) are never renamed (addition-only)
- §3 Possible definitions — 5 candidates (D1 relations-only / D2 strict union / D3 D1 + broken parallel marker / D4 structural-only / D5 inbound-only) with pros/cons and 5 traps to resolve in contract
- §4 UX options — 5 options (U1 sidebar marker / U2 summary integration / U3 dedicated filter / U4 per-type markers / U5 U1+U3 hybrid) with UI-label rules that keep `orphan` out of user-visible text
- §5 Data/model implications — existing helpers suffice; optional new pure helper `buildConnectednessSets` in `features/connectedness/`; zero AppState / reducer / persistence touch; performance piggy-backs on existing link-index pass
- §6 Recommended direction — adopt D2 (fully-unconnected) with U5 (marker + filter). Explicit "won't adopt" list includes unified label, D4, D5, graph viz. Staged rollout plan S1–S5.
- §7 Explicit non-goals — no code / no graph / no semantic merge / no permanent orphan state
- §8 Related docs — parents (v1 orphan, unified-backlinks v0/v1, summary row v2), link-index specs, data model, and the follow-up contract document that should be written before implementation

Scope: docs-only. No code, tests, dist, or build artifacts changed. Validation (tests / build) intentionally skipped since no code changed.

## Summary

Worker 에서 모든 이미지 생성이 HTTP 500 으로 실패. Cloudflare Observability 로그:
```
Gemini API 400: { "error": { "code": 400,
  "message": "User location is not supported for the API use.", ... } }
```

Google Generative Language API 가 한국 발신 요청을 차단. Cloudflare Worker 가 한국(ICN) 엣지에서 Google 로 나가고 있던 것이 원인.

## 변경

`wrangler.toml` 에 `[placement] mode = "smart"` 추가 (6줄):
```toml
[placement]
mode = "smart"
```

Cloudflare Smart Placement 는 Worker 실행 위치를 백엔드 서비스 (이 경우 Google AI, US) 근처로 이동시켜 egress IP 를 US 데이터센터로 만든다. geo-restriction 우회.

- 배포 후 Cloudflare 가 트래픽 패턴 학습 (수 분 ~ 10분)
- Observability 로그에서 `User location is not supported` 사라짐
- Gemini API 호출 성공 → 이미지 생성 정상화

## Fallback

Smart Placement 는 확률적 — 항상 US 엣지로 가는 것은 보장 안 됨. 만약 실패율이 여전히 높으면 AI Gateway (US 경유 프록시 확정) 로 전환 필요.

body:
## Summary

- Stands up a full **Droplet + docker-compose** deployment: Caddy fronts the API with automatic Let's Encrypt TLS, SQLite persists on a DO Block Storage volume, and `docker compose pull && up -d` is the whole deploy loop. Bootstrap instructions live in `deploy/README.md`.
- Wires a `publish-image` workflow that builds the image and pushes to GHCR on every push to `main` and every `stable-*` tag (existing `tag-stable` workflow provides the tags).
- Rewrites the stale `Dockerfile` as a multi-stage build from `projects/api/` — the old one copied 4 of 11 required components and `CMD`-ed `clojure -M:build`, which only compiles. Image runs as pinned UID 10001 on a slim Temurin 21 JRE (~400 MB).

## Fixes uncovered along the way

- `db.clj` now honors `RTS_DB_CONNECTION_URI` (matching the migrations CLI). Previously the path was hardcoded, so the container couldn't be pointed at a volume.
- Production `system.clj` now calls `integrant.core/expand` before `init`. Without it, `::configuration/openid-url` never materialised as a top-level key and the prod profile couldn't boot. The dev workspace already did this.
- `projects/api/deps.edn` + `projects/deploy-data/deps.edn` bumped `org.clojure/tools.build 0.9.4` (doesn't exist on Maven Central or Clojars) to git-based `io.github.clojure/tools.build v0.10.13`. `build.clj` couldn't resolve its own classpath before.

## Test plan

author: legalmanagerai
body:
## Resumen

Cumplimiento completo del **Art. 539 Ley 2445/2025** + **inciso 7 corregido por Dec 1136/2025** en el wizard de insolvencia del portal de partes, más flujo obligatorio **PDF → firma electrónica → radicar**.

### Compliance (10 numerales Art. 539)
- **Paso 5 Acreedores**: tasa mensual, fechas otorgamiento/vencimiento, documento soporte, otros conceptos (leasing), postergado (572A), garantía mobiliaria economía solidaria con monto, info desconocida y codeudores/fiadores/avalistas (JSONB).
- **Paso 6 Bienes**: medidas cautelares, exterior, patrimonio de familia inembargable, documento idóneo.
- **Paso 9 Ingresos**: tipo de fuente (empleado/pensionado/independiente/mixto) + empleador/fondo + anexo obligatorio condicional.
- **Paso 10 Sociedad conyugal**: estado explícito + flujo liquidación <2 años con escritura + valor bienes.
- **Paso 1**: fija automáticamente la fecha de corte (último día del mes anterior — Parágrafo 2).
- **Validators**: revisan los campos nuevos + anexos condicionales.

### Flujo PDF + firma + radicar (Paso 13 rediseñado)
1. **Generar documento** → PDF a nombre del deudor estructurado por los 10 numerales + juramento (pdf-lib).
2. **Firmar electrónicamente** → reusa /firmar/[token] existente (OTP email, certificado Ley 527/1999 + Dec 2364/2012).
3. **Radicar** → bloqueado hasta que exista firma.

### Nuevos endpoints
- `POST /api/partes/solicitudes/[id]/preparar-firma`: valida, genera PDF, sube a Storage, crea documento + firmante con token.
- `GET /api/partes/solicitudes/[id]/firma-estado`: polling, sincroniza draft cuando firma se completa.
- `POST /api/partes/solicitudes/[id]/radicar`: guard de firma antes del RPC.

### Migración SQL
`supabase/migrations/021_ley_2445_compliance.sql` (**ya aplicada** en Supabase vciifcfppebjpqdawwzh):
- Extiende sgcc_case_creditors, sgcc_case_assets, sgcc_cases, sgcc_solicitudes_draft.
- Agrega draft_id a sgcc_firma_documentos.
- Reemplaza RPC radicar_solicitud para validar firma y copiar campos nuevos al caso.

## Test plan

- [ ] Paso 1: verificar que aparece fecha de corte automática.
- [ ] Paso 5: llenar acreedor completo (tasa, fechas, doc, otros conceptos, codeudor).
- [ ] Paso 5: marcar garantía mobiliaria solidaria y verificar que exige monto aportes.
- [ ] Paso 6: marcar bien en exterior / cautelar / patrimonio inembargable.
- [ ] Paso 9: cambiar tipo de fuente y verificar que aparece empleador/fondo correspondiente.

- [ ] Paso 12: verificar que aparecen los anexos según la fuente elegida.
- [ ] Paso 13: generar PDF → abrir firma → firmar con OTP → radicar.

body:
💡 What: Replaced array map operations that iterate over binary buffers for serialization with native chunked string operations.
🎯 Why: Converting large binaries to strings (and vice versa) using `Array.from` or `.split('').map(...)` creates millions of intermediate objects, leading to major processing bottlenecks and memory spikes for large PDF streams.
📊 Impact: Reduces array iteration and intermediate garbage collection significantly. In mock local tests for 1MB string chunk encoding, mapping took ~800ms vs ~14ms.
🔬 Measurement: Verified with local JS benchmark scripts; ensured functionality correctness by passing all 14 unit regression tests via `node --test`.

author: kamalshafei1990
body:
## Summary
Adds richer intent analysis, response-format hints in the prompt, and a small offline glossary that answers common commercial definitions WITHOUT calling any AI provider.

## Detected intents
`analyzeIntent(query): { type, complexity, expectedFormat }`

| Query | Type | Complexity | Format | Local |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `What is margin?` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `Explain margin` | explanation | simple | structured | miss |
| `Translate this to Chinese` | translation | simple | short | miss |
| `Hello` | chat | simple | short | miss |
| `Pricing strategy for distributors` | business | deep | detailed | miss |
| `What is the price of product ABC?` | business | simple | structured | miss |
| `Compare FOB vs CIF` | business | deep | detailed | miss |
| `How do I create a quotation?` | explanation | simple | structured | miss |
| `ما معنى الهامش؟` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `بص عايز اعرف يعني ايه margin` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `define RFQ` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `what does FOB mean?` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `meaning of landed cost` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `margin definition` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `what does EXW stand for` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |
| `ما هو الهامش؟` | definition | simple | short | **HIT** |

## Response templates (via `formatHint` in prompt builder)
| format | Shape instruction |
|---|---|
| short (definition) | one short paragraph (≤3 sentences) — definition + one concrete example |
| short (translation) | output the translation directly, no preamble |
| short (chat) | 1–2 sentences, plain prose |
| structured (explanation) | one-sentence summary + 2–4 short numbered/bulleted steps, no headers |
| structured (business) | summary sentence + 2–4 concise actionable bullets, no fluff |
| detailed | thorough — summary + 3–5 key points + example, plain prose |

## Local knowledge
15 core commercial terms × 4 languages (EN / AR / EGY / ZH):
`margin · profit · gross margin · net margin · markup · RFQ · quotation · invoice · discount · commission · landed cost · FOB · CIF · EXW · COGS`

Subject extraction handles: `what is X`, `what does X mean`, `define X`, `meaning of X`, `X definition`, `what does X stand for`, `ما معنى X`, `ما هو X`, Egyptian `يعني ايه X`.

Franco (`بص عايز اعرف يعني ايه margin`) → reply pulls the EGY variant per Phase 4 rules (reply in Arabic script, not Franco).

## Fallback behaviour (before/after)
**Before** (Phase 3): when all providers failed, synthetic fallback said generic intent-shaped "try again" text.

**After** (Phase 5):
1. If query is a definition we know → lead with a short honest preamble and serve the REAL glossary answer.
2. If not → fall through to the Phase 3 intent-aware "try again" shape.
3. Never returns a generic "I couldn't complete that request" from anywhere.

Preamble wording (language-aware):
- EN: *"The AI service is temporarily slow, but here's a quick take:"*
- AR: *"خدمة الذكاء الاصطناعي بطيئة مؤقتًا، ولكن إليك شرحًا مختصرًا:"*
- EGY: *"بص، حصل بطء بسيط في الخدمة دلوقتي، بس خليني أشرحلك الموضوع:"*
- ZH: *"AI 服务暂时较慢,不过这里先给你一个简短说明:"*

## Examples before/after (chat route)
| Query | Before (provider) | After (provider, local path) |
|---|---|---|
| `What is margin?` | Groq/DeepSeek call (~800 ms) | `local` (~450 ms, no provider) |
| `What is FOB?` | Groq/DeepSeek call | `local` streaming start/delta/end |
| `ما معنى الهامش؟` | Groq/DeepSeek call | `local` Arabic answer |
| `بص عايز اعرف يعني ايه margin` | Franco, Groq/DeepSeek | `local` Egyptian answer |
| `what is the capital of France` | Provider | Provider (no glossary hit) |

## Integration flow
```
preprocess → detectLanguage → analyzeIntent → enrichedCtx → buildLanePrompt
                                                             ↓
chat route: local-knowledge short-circuit runs BEFORE streamRouteAi
            (also bypasses the provider-config guard — local answers
             work even when no provider key is set)
```

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- Browser preview: 4 local definition hits served in 428–1210 ms with no provider configured; 1 non-glossary query (capital of France) correctly 503s; streaming SSE start/delta/end contract works for both `stream:true` and plain JSON requests.
- Prompt sizes still in budget (FAST ≤1.1 KB, SMART ≤2.7 KB across every language × format combination).

## Rules respected
- ✅ No speed regression (local path is faster than any provider)
- ✅ Lanes untouched
- ✅ No AI calls in the new layer
- ✅ Deterministic — same query always serves same local answer
- ✅ Additive context fields only
- ✅ Generic "I couldn't complete that request" removed everywhere

author: bemusedvermin
body:
Closes #81

## Summary

`body_map.rs` previously collapsed same-site duplicate regions via pair-wise `merge_two`, which is non-associative for `Mean` across 3+ regions: `((a+b)/2 + c)/2 ≠ (a+b+c)/3`. This PR replaces the `Mean` path with a two-pass `(sum, count)` accumulator so `Mean` is now a true arithmetic mean.

### Changes (`crates/beast-interpreter/src/body_map.rs`)

- `per_site_channel_values` splits strategies: `Max` / `Sum` keep the associative pair-wise fold via `merge_two`; `Mean` uses a `BTreeMap<BodySite, (Q3232, u32)>` accumulator and finalises `sum.saturating_div(count)` per site.
- `merge_two`'s `Mean` arm is retained with a `debug_assert!(false, …)` guard so accidental future callers trip in dev.
- Docstrings updated — pair-wise caveat removed from `per_site_channel_values`; `aggregate_channel_globally` `Mean` section reworked (still a mean-of-means across sites).

### New regression test

`per_site_channel_values_three_same_site_mean_is_true_arithmetic_mean` — 3 regions at `BodySite::LimbLeft` with `[2, 4, 12]` yield `6`, not the old pair-wise `7.5`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked` — pass (85 beast-interpreter tests, +1)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --doc --locked` — pass

## Rust-reviewer verdict

**APPROVE.** 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH. Two LOW notes accepted (u32 saturation unreachable in practice; `merge_two` dead-arm guarded with `debug_assert!` to keep PR focused). Determinism invariants verified: `BTreeMap` iteration, saturating Q32.32, no floats, no PRNG or `HashMap` changes.

author: kha-kis
body:
Bundle of three independent maintenance changes (one commit each).

## 1. `chore(api)`: delete unused `HTTPAPIServer` class
The in-process `HTTPAPIServer` in `mole_pkg/services/api.py` was exported but instantiated nowhere — the running API server is `HTTPAPIServerStandalone` in `api_main.py`. Keeping the dead class is a future trap: PR #4 added a new `/v1/dns` shape only to this unused class and it shipped operationally invisible until #5 added the IPC bridge. Removes the file entirely + the export from `services/__init__.py` + the corresponding tests in `tests/test_services.py`.

## 2. `fix(qbittorrent)`: tolerant timeout + retry on `/transfer/info` polling
The hardcoded `timeout=5` against qBit's WebUI was generating spurious hourly ERROR-level entries on high-torrent-count clients (10k+) where qBit's single-threaded WebUI occasionally pauses for several seconds during internal sweeps. The errors auto-recovered without action but diluted the log signal of real outages.

- New `QB_API_TIMEOUT` config (default `15`, was hardcoded `5`).
- `get_connection_status()` retries once on socket timeout with 1s backoff. Single transient timeout now logs at WARNING; two consecutive timeouts (or any non-timeout exception) still ERROR.
- `_is_timeout()` helper distinguishes raw `socket.timeout`/`TimeoutError` from `URLError`-wrapped variants.
- 2 new IsolatedAsyncioTestCase covering both the retry-success and give-up paths.

Other call sites pick up the larger default timeout but don't get retry — they're either mutations (idempotency-sensitive) or already non-noisy.

## 3. `feat(install)`: `--upgrade` mode for in-place upgrades
`install.sh`'s interactive `mole init` at the end made it unsuitable for upgrading a configured host. `sudo ./install.sh --upgrade`:
- Skips dependency installation (already present)
- Skips `systemctl enable mole` (already enabled)
- Skips `mole init` (config exists)
- Prints restart instructions instead of starting the service (operator-controlled cutover)

`--help` prints usage. Unknown args exit 2. Default behavior unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 211 passed (was 215; -6 deleted dead-class tests, +2 new retry tests)
- [x] `bash -n install.sh` — syntax OK
- [x] `bash install.sh --help` — prints usage
- [x] `bash install.sh --notarealarg` — exits 2 with message
- [x] `bash install.sh --upgrade` (non-root) — banner shows "Upgrade Mode", root check fires

author: squevlav
body:
Este feature implementa un flujo completo de creación de órdenes y procesamiento de pagos utilizando Mercado Pago.

En primer lugar, el caso de uso calcula el monto total esperado a partir de los productos incluidos en la orden (detalleOrden). Luego compara este valor con el monto enviado en los datos del pago. Si existe una diferencia mayor a un margen permitido (0.01), se lanza una excepción para evitar inconsistencias o posibles manipulaciones desde el frontend.

Después de validar el monto, el sistema procede a crear la orden de pago en Mercado Pago mediante un servicio dedicado. En este paso se envían datos como el monto, el correo del usuario, el token de la tarjeta, el método de pago y las cuotas. La respuesta incluye identificadores y el estado del pago.

Posteriormente, el sistema crea la orden en la base de datos, registrando la información del usuario y los productos adquiridos. Una vez creada la orden, se guarda también el pago en el sistema, incluyendo tanto los datos enviados como la respuesta recibida desde Mercado Pago, estableciendo la relación entre la orden y el pago.

Sin embargo, no fue posible realizar las pruebas del flujo. Esto se debe a que la integración con Mercado Pago requiere un token generado desde el frontend a partir de la información del método de pago, con el fin de evitar que la aplicación backend tenga contacto directo con datos sensibles de los clientes.

Inicialmente, se intentó utilizar un valor generado de manera aleatoria como token, pero la plataforma respondió indicando que no cumplía con la estructura requerida. Posteriormente, se probó con un token simulado que respetaba las condiciones esperadas (32 caracteres alfanuméricos); no obstante, la respuesta de Mercado Pago fue nuevamente de rechazo, indicando que el token no era válido.

En consecuencia, la validación completa del feature queda pendiente hasta contar con un token legítimo generado correctamente desde el frontend.

author: bemusedvermin
body:
Closes #76

## Summary

Pure refactor of the `parameter_map` hotspot in `beast-interpreter` — no behavioural change. The ~408-LOC monolith is now a module directory with responsibilities separated along the pipeline boundary (parse → resolve → evaluate).

### Sub-module layout (`crates/beast-interpreter/src/parameter_map/`)

| File              | Total LOC | Production LOC |
|-------------------|-----------|----------------|
| `mod.rs`          | 53        | ~46            |
| `ast.rs`          | 84        | 84             |
| `parser.rs`       | 459       | ~298           |
| `literal.rs`      | 70        | ~45            |
| `eval.rs`         | 163       | ~40            |
| `analysis.rs`     | 48        | ~34            |
| `test_support.rs` | 52        | 52 (cfg-test)  |

`parser.rs` runs ~298 production LOC because the recursive-descent grammar rules are tightly coupled; further splitting would hurt readability, and the issue explicitly forbids swapping the parser (that's #61).

### `CompiledExpr` newtype

`ExprNode` is `pub(crate)` with `pub(crate)` variants. `CompiledExpr { pub(crate) node: ExprNode }` is constructible only via `pub(crate) fn from_node` from the parser, so "channel symbols resolved at parse time" is a compiler-enforced invariant rather than a convention. `pub type Expr = CompiledExpr` keeps downstream callers (`composition.rs`, `emission.rs`, integration tests) compiling unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked` — 335 tests pass (beast-interpreter: 88 unit, +4 literal-helper tests)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --doc --locked` — pass

## Rust-reviewer verdict

**APPROVE.** 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH. One pre-existing LOW observation (unchecked `self.pos + 3` usize add in `parse_factor`) — out of pure-refactor scope; will open a follow-up tracker.

## Out of scope

- New operators (`sqrt`, ranges, `clamp`, `div`, `sub`) — see #61.
- Parser rewrite (pratt / `nom` / `winnow`).

author: sami-ben-grine
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `GatewayProvider` that speaks OpenAI chat-completions wire format to an [`andy-models`](https://github.com/rivoli-ai/andy-models) gateway instead of talking to vendors directly. Satisfies the andy-llm side of [rivoli-ai/andy-models#11](https://github.com/rivoli-ai/andy-models/issues/11) (Phase 7 — GatewayProvider).

- Consumers present a single tenant bearer token; the gateway owns per-vendor API keys, routing to the real upstream (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Ollama / OpenRouter), pricing snapshots, and the usage ledger.
- Direct vendor providers remain available for offline / Conductor-embedded modes — both can coexist.
- Model references change from vendor-native ids (`gpt-4o-mini`) to catalog slugs (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`).

### What the provider does

- **`CompleteAsync`** — `POST /v1/chat/completions`, parses `choices[0].message` (including `tool_calls`), surfaces `Usage` + `FinishReason`
- **`StreamCompleteAsync`** — reads SSE line-by-line, yields content deltas, accumulates partial tool-call arguments across chunks, emits a terminal `LlmStreamResponse` with `IsComplete`, `FinishReason`, and final `Usage`
- **`IsAvailableAsync`** — `GET /v1/models` health check
- **`ListModelsAsync`** — returns the catalog entries visible under the gateway's RBAC scope

### Factory wiring

- `LlmProviderFactory` recognises `gateway` (and `andy-models` alias) as a provider type.
- Env fallbacks: `ANDY_MODELS_API_KEY`, `ANDY_MODELS_API_BASE`, `ANDY_MODELS_MODEL`.

### Migration note

`docs/gateway-provider.md` covers the step-by-step migration for consumer services (add config → feature-flag verify → flip `Llm:DefaultProvider` → stop setting vendor keys → update model ids to catalog slugs), env-var reference, and the follow-up plan for per-user token forwarding.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — 0 errors, pre-existing warnings unchanged
- [x] `dotnet test` — **222 passing / 2 skipped** (11 new `GatewayProviderTests`)
  - Constructor validation (missing key / base / model)
  - `IsAvailableAsync` for 200 OK and network error
  - Non-streaming `CompleteAsync` with Bearer auth header assertion and usage parsing
  - Default-model fallback when request has none
  - `tool_calls` parsing from non-streaming response
  - Streaming SSE — content accumulated across deltas, final `Usage` / `FinishReason` on the terminal chunk
  - `stream:true` is set on the outgoing request
  - `ListModelsAsync` parses the `data` array and surfaces `owned_by` as `Provider`
- [ ] Manual smoke against a live `andy-models` API with a real provider key on the gateway side — not in CI yet; documented procedure in `docs/gateway-provider.md`.

## Explicitly deferred

- **Per-user token forwarding** — today uses a single service-level bearer token. A pluggable `IGatewayTokenProvider` (to forward the caller's JWT unchanged when the gateway enforces per-user RBAC) is flagged in the migration note as a follow-up.
- **Consumer-side config flips** — changing each downstream service's `Llm:DefaultProvider` to `"gateway"` is in those repos, not this one.
- **`AddSingleton<GatewayProvider>()`** DI registration — current provider doesn't have an `IOptions<LlmOptions>` fallback constructor, so direct DI injection isn't supported. Consumers use `ILlmProviderFactory.CreateProvider("gateway")`. Adding the fallback constructor is trivial follow-up if direct injection is ever needed.

author: seeburtoh
body:
## What this adds

A notebook in `1_foundations/1_lab1.ipynb` demonstrating the **orchestrator-worker**
workflow pattern applied to multi-company competitive analysis.

## How it works

- **Orchestrator** (Claude) reads a natural-language query, identifies 2–5 companies
  to analyze, and selects 3–4 relevant analysis dimensions.
- **Workers** run in parallel via `asyncio.gather`, each specializing in a different
  lens:
  - OpenAI GPT-4o — market positioning
  - Gemini 2.5 Flash — product features
  - Groq (Llama 3.2) — pricing & business model
  - DeepSeek — technical architecture
- **Synthesis step** sends all worker findings back to the orchestrator for a
  final comparison report.

## Why this pattern

Competitive analysis is a good fit for orchestrator-worker because the subtasks
aren't known up front — the number of companies and relevant dimensions depend
on the query. A 3-company query fires 12 parallel worker calls; a 5-company
query fires 20, all coordinated by a single planning call.

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the `lastFMConstructor` function in `core/agents/lastfm.go` so that the Last.FM integration works out-of-the-box without requiring manual user configuration. Three files are modified with surgical, backward-compatible changes:

1. **`consts/consts.go`** — Added `LastFMApiKey` built-in shared API key constant (`c2918986bf01b6ba353c0bc1bdd27bea`).
2. **`core/agents/lastfm.go`** — Added fallback logic so the constructor uses the built-in key when `conf.Server.LastFM.ApiKey` is empty, and `"en"` when `conf.Server.LastFM.Language` is empty. Removed the `if conf.Server.LastFM.ApiKey != ""` registration guard in `init()` so the agent is always registered.
3. **`server/initial_setup.go`** — Updated the `checkExternalCredentials()` diagnostic message from "Last.FM integration not available: missing ApiKey/Secret" to "Last.FM integration is ENABLED, using default ApiKey" to accurately reflect the new fallback behavior.

## Scope & Constraints

- **Function signatures preserved**: `lastFMConstructor(ctx context.Context) Interface` is byte-for-byte unchanged in signature.
- **Backward compatible**: User-provided `LastFM.ApiKey` and `LastFM.Language` continue to take precedence over fallbacks.
- **No new interfaces**: Zero new exported types or public APIs.
- **No i18n changes**: Only Go-side constants and log messages modified; no user-facing strings.
- **No dependency changes**: `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged.

## Key Accomplishments & Critical Fix

During validation, a security regression was detected and fixed (commit `32f745f5`): the initial implementation passed the built-in key as a structured log field (`log.Info(msg, "key", consts.LastFMApiKey)`), which bypassed the existing redaction patterns in `log/log.go` (those patterns match Go `%+v` struct format, not logrus `key=VALUE` fields). This would have leaked the key in plaintext into every INFO-level startup log whenever the fallback engaged. The fix removes the structured field and preserves only the informational message; the exact key value remains inspectable via `consts.LastFMApiKey` in source. An explanatory comment was added to prevent regression.

## Validation Gates — ALL PASSED

- `go build -tags=netgo ./...` — clean
- `go vet ./...` — no findings
- `gofmt -d` on modified files — no diffs
- `go test -count=1 ./...` — 19 packages PASS, 458 Ginkgo specs PASS (plus 1 pre-existing `XContext` pending spec in `scanner/metadata/ffmpeg_test.go`, out of scope per AAP §0.6.2)
- `CI=true npm test -- --watchAll=false --ci` — 10 suites / 34 tests PASS
- `cd ui && npm run check-formatting` / `npm run lint` — both clean
- Runtime verified in 3 scenarios: no key configured (fallback), user key configured (precedence), debug mode (redaction). HTTP `/ping` returns 200 in all cases. Built-in key value does not appear in any log output.

## Remaining Work for Human Developers

- **[HIGH]** Code review and PR approval
- **[MEDIUM]** Manual integration smoke test against the real Last.fm API using the built-in key
- **[MEDIUM]** Production deployment and observability check

- `d6691dc4` — Add LastFMApiKey built-in shared constant
- `8140f900` — lastFMConstructor default fallbacks and unconditional registration
- `034976d5` — Align checkExternalCredentials() log message
- `32f745f5` — Remove plaintext LastFM built-in key from checkExternalCredentials log

author: copilot
body:
labwc failed to run due to a missing `timerfd` kernel module (compile blocker), absent Wayland environment variables, missing `/run/user/0` directory, broken VT ioctl stubs, and incorrect DRM UAPI values.

## timerfd.rs (new)
The kernel declared `mod timerfd` in `lib.rs`/`main.rs` but the file didn't exist — nothing compiled. Created a full Linux-compatible implementation:
- `Itimerspec`/`Timespec` structs matching the Linux x86_64 ABI
- `TimerFdScheme` implementing `Scheme` (open/read/write/close/fstat/lseek/poll)
- `settime()` / `gettime()` called directly from syscall handlers
- `read()` returns little-endian 8-byte expiry count; `EAGAIN` if not yet expired; `POLLIN` in poll when fired

## elf_loader.rs — Wayland environment
Every spawned process (including labwc) lacked the Wayland socket env vars. Added to `MINIMAL_ENVP`:
```
WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/0
XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland
```

## main.rs — /run/user/0 pre-creation
labwc creates its socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wayland-0`. Added pre-creation of `/run`, `/run/user`, `/run/user/0` in the virtual run overlay after `filesystem::init()`.

## filesystem.rs — VT ioctl stubs
seatd and libinput issue VT/keyboard ioctls during seat init; most returned `ENOSYS` causing seat management to abort. Added stubs for:
- `VT_OPENQRY` (reports VT 1), `VT_GETMODE` (VT_AUTO), `VT_SETMODE`, `VT_RELDISP`, `VT_RESIZE/RESIZEX`
- `KDSKBMUTE`, `KDSKBENT`, `KDGKBENT`, `KDGKBLED`

## drm_scheme.rs — DRM UAPI correctness
- **Encoder `crtc_id`**: `2000` → `0` (CRTC 2000 doesn't exist; only CRTC 200 is exposed)
- **`DRM_CAP_CURSOR_WIDTH/HEIGHT`**: was returning screen dimensions → fixed to `64`
- **`DRM_IOCTL_MODE_GETPLANE`**: was reporting 0 formats → now returns `XRGB8888` + `ARGB8888`

## sys_scheme.rs — sysfs completeness
- Non-empty `/sys/dev/char/226:*/device/drm/` directories listing `card0` and `renderD128` — required by `drmGetPrimaryDeviceNameFromFd`
- PCI attribute files (`uevent`, `vendor`, `device`, `class`, `revision`, `subsystem_vendor`, `subsystem_device`) under `/sys/dev/char/226:*/device/` — required by `drmGetDeviceFromFd`
- `readlink` target for `/sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:02.0/subsystem` → `../../../../bus/pci`

author: coolaj86
body:
Fixes #15

The OpenRC init script was written to a temp file named `${name}` (no extension) in the current working directory. If the user ran `serviceman add` from a directory containing a binary with the same name as the service (e.g. `./payd-vault`), serviceman would silently overwrite it.

systemd uses `${name}.service` and launchd uses `${name}.plist` — neither clashes with a bare binary name. The OpenRC path now uses `${name}.openrc.tmp` for the same safety.

The dryrun path also now removes the temp file after printing it.

- **Premise:** The [HTML-AAM spec §2 Documentation conformance](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#docconformance) enumerates elements that must not carry ARIA attributes. `aria-query` encodes this list in `dom[tag].reserved`.
- **Problem:** Our rule hand-maintained a shorter set (8 elements) and silently accepted ARIA attributes on `<col>`, `<colgroup>`, `<noembed>`, `<noscript>`, `<param>`, `<picture>`, `<source>`, and `<track>`.

Fix: derive the set from `aria-query`'s `dom` map by filtering `def.reserved`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Elements flagged | `meta, html, script, style, title, base, head, link` (8) | same + `col, colgroup, noembed, noscript, param, picture, source, track` (16) |

`aria-query` is already a dependency used elsewhere for role/attribute validation — no new packages. Six new invalid tests cover the previously-missing elements.

Note: HTML-AAM reserves `map`, `slot`, and `template` as well, but these are absent from aria-query's `.reserved` set, so this PR does not flag them. Closing that gap would require either a hand-maintained supplement or a change upstream in aria-query.

## Prior art

| Plugin | Rule | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| [jsx-a11y](https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/blob/main/src/rules/aria-unsupported-elements.js) | `aria-unsupported-elements` | Uses `aria-query`'s `dom` map filtered by `.reserved`. |
| [vuejs-accessibility](https://github.com/vue-a11y/eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility/blob/main/src/rules/aria-unsupported-elements.ts) | `aria-unsupported-elements` | Same. |
| [lit-a11y](https://github.com/open-wc/open-wc/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin-lit-a11y/lib/rules/aria-unsupported-elements.js) | `aria-unsupported-elements` | Hardcoded list `['meta', 'script', 'style']`; does not consult aria-query. |

Upstream `ember-template-lint@7.9.3` has the same narrower coverage.

author: blitzy[bot]
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes an incorrect percentage-to-integer scaling of the hue component in HSV/HSVA color strings within the `QtColor` configuration type parser, as specified in the Agent Action Plan (AAP).

## Problem

The `_parse_value` helper method in `qutebrowser/config/configtypes.py` unconditionally scaled all percentage values using a maximum of 255, which is correct for saturation, value, and alpha channels but wrong for the hue channel, whose valid range per Qt's `QColor.fromHsv()` API is 0–359.

- **Before:** `hsv(100%,100%,100%)` → `QColor.fromHsv(255, 255, 255)` (hue capped at 255)
- **After:** `hsv(100%,100%,100%)` → `QColor.fromHsv(359, 255, 255)` (hue scaled to full range)

This was originally a deliberate workaround for an older Qt CSS parser bug (`QTBUG-70897`) that is no longer applicable.

## Changes

All three AAP-specified files modified on this branch:

1. **`qutebrowser/config/configtypes.py`** — `QtColor._parse_value` now accepts a `maxval: int = 255` keyword parameter; `QtColor.to_py` passes `maxval=359` when parsing the hue component of `hsv(...)` / `hsva(...)` strings. Defensive overflow/SIGSEGV protection added via existing `qtutils.check_overflow` (prevents PyQt5 sip binding crashes on malformed input like `hsv(inf%,0%,0%)` or astronomical integers).
2. **`tests/unit/config/test_configtypes.py`** — Updated `TestQtColor.test_valid` expected values for `hsv(10%,10%,10%)` → `QColor.fromHsv(35, 25, 25)` and `hsva(10%,20%,30%,40%)` → `QColor.fromHsv(35, 51, 76, 102)`. Removed obsolete `QTBUG-70897` comments. Added 8 new `test_invalid` cases covering overflow/NaN inputs.
3. **`doc/changelog.asciidoc`** — Added two "Fixed" bullets under v1.6.0 (unreleased) documenting the hue percentage fix and the companion overflow/SIGSEGV hardening.

## Test Results

- `TestQtColor` (AAP primary target): **32/32 passed** (10 valid + 22 invalid)
- `TestQssColor` (regression): **19/19 passed**
- `flake8` on both modified Python files: exit 0 (zero violations)
- `py_compile` on both modified Python files: clean
- All 8 AAP manual trace scenarios verified

## Scope Compliance

- ✅ Only the three files explicitly listed in AAP §0.5.1 were modified
- ✅ `configdata.yml`, `settings.asciidoc`, `proxy.py`, `QssColor`, and all CI/CD files remain untouched per AAP §0.5.2
- ✅ The `_parse_value` signature change is backward-compatible (default `maxval=255` preserves legacy behavior)
- ✅ All existing `TestQssColor`, hex, named-color, and integer-HSV test cases continue to pass unchanged

## Branch Commits

1. `40a4f7514` — Fix HSV/HSVA hue percentage scaling in QtColor
2. `8d541572b` — Document HSV/HSVA hue percentage scaling fix in changelog
3. `464b63a75` — Update TestQtColor HSV/HSVA expected values for hue-359 scaling fix
4. `299d80a76` — Harden QtColor._parse_value against overflow and SIGSEGV

## Remaining Work (path-to-production, ~3 hours)

- Human code review of the 3-file diff
- Merge to main and resolve any rebase conflicts
- Confirm the changelog renders correctly in published documentation
- (Optional, out-of-scope per AAP) Resolve pre-existing PyYAML 3.13 + Python 3.7 `collections.Hashable` deprecation-warning compatibility that affects other unrelated test classes in the broader config test suite

author: kbuci
body:
### Describe the issue this Pull Request addresses

Ensure the Flink Parquet schema converter correctly attaches the `VARIANT` logical type annotation when converting Variant columns, and fails fast when the annotation is unavailable.

Previously, `ParquetSchemaConverter.convertVariantToParquetType()` produced a Parquet group with `metadata` and `value` binary fields but did not attach the `VARIANT` annotation. Without the annotation, readers cannot distinguish a Variant column from an ordinary `ROW<metadata BINARY, value BINARY>`, risking silent data-correctness issues.

This PR:
- Resolves the VARIANT annotation via reflection in `DataTypeAdapter` (Flink 2.1.x) to maintain backward compatibility with parquet-java < 1.16.0.
- Attaches the annotation to the Parquet group on write schema conversion.
- Fails fast if the annotation is unavailable (parquet-java < 1.16.0 or Flink < 2.1), preventing writes of variant columns that cannot be identified by readers.
- Improves error messages across all pre-2.1 Flink adapter shims.
- Adds unit tests for schema conversion paths (annotation detection, fail-fast, shredded rejection).

**Note:** This PR covers schema conversion and annotation enforcement only. Actual variant data writing (adding a `VariantWriter` to `ParquetRowDataWriter`) and corresponding Flink-write IT tests will be addressed in a follow-up PR.

### Summary and Changelog

* **VARIANT annotation on write schema (`ParquetSchemaConverter`)**: `convertVariantToParquetType()` resolves the Parquet VARIANT annotation via `DataTypeAdapter.variantParquetAnnotation()` and attaches it with `.as(annotation)`. If unavailable, throws `UnsupportedOperationException` with a clear error message.
* **Reflection-based annotation detection (`DataTypeAdapter` for Flink 2.1.x)**: Resolves `LogicalTypeAnnotation.variantType(byte)` via reflection at class-load time and caches the result. Returns `Option.empty()` on parquet-java < 1.16.0, `Option.of(annotation)` on 1.16.0+. A named constant `VARIANT_SPEC_VERSION = 1` documents the Parquet Variant binary spec version.
* **Pre-2.1 Flink adapters (1.17.x–2.0.x)**: Added `variantParquetAnnotation()` that throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. All variant methods updated to use a shared error message constant.
* **Unit tests (`TestParquetSchemaConverter`)**: Unannotated groups treated as ROW, write produces correct annotated layout (on parquet 1.16.0+), fail-fast on older parquet.
* **Unit tests (`TestHoodieSchemaConverter`)**: Variant in arrays/maps, shredded variant rejection.

### Impact

* Schema conversion for Variant columns now produces properly annotated Parquet types.
* Attempting to convert a Variant schema on unsupported configurations fails immediately with a clear error.
* No regression risk: changes are additive and only activate for Variant LogicalType.
* No public API changes.

### Risk Level

Low. Changes are additive and scoped to Variant schema conversion. Non-Variant schemas are completely unaffected. The reflection-based detection falls back gracefully.

### Documentation Update

None.

### Contributor's checklist

- [x] Read through contributor's guide
- [x] Enough context is provided in the sections above
- [x] Adequate tests were added if applicable

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Three fixes on top of the 4-PR scheduler series: **1. "No feasible slots" on every day — now explains why** The week picker was silently dropping the algorithm's `warnings`, so if your home address or the lead's address was missing it'd render 14 days of "No feasible slots" with no hint what was wrong. `/api/schedule/week` now checks both up front and returns a 400 with an actionable message, which the modal already surfaces at the top in its amber callout. - Missing home → "Set your starting address in Settings before using the AI scheduler." - Missing lead address → "This lead has no address yet — add one to rank days by drive time." **2. Timezone: pin all scheduler dates to America/New_York** Vercel runs UTC, so `new Date().getDate()` on the server was jumping to tomorrow every evening after ~8 PM ET. Three endpoints were affected: - `/api/schedule/today` — queried tomorrow's leads between 8 PM–midnight ET, so the Today's route card looked empty. - `/api/schedule/week` — horizon dates and work-day lookup used UTC; on Sundays after 7 PM ET it'd flip "Sunday = day off" onto Saturday. - `/api/schedule/suggest` — past-date guard used UTC, which refused to book anything for "today" between 8 PM and midnight. All three now go through a shared `src/lib/date.ts` that matches the ingest pipeline's existing America/New_York pattern. **3. "Estimate Added to Calendar" toast was hidden behind the modal** The booking flow now keeps the modal open for the SMS confirmation step, so the toast was painting behind the modal overlay and auto-clearing before the user ever closed it. Moved the toast to fire on modal close instead. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Open the AI scheduler on a lead that has no address — top of the week picker should show the amber "lead has no address yet" message instead of 14 rows of "No feasible slots" - [ ] If Settings home address is empty, the picker should show the "set your starting address in Settings" message - [ ] Fill in both addresses on a lead with a valid home — confirm feasible days actually rank with drive-time badges - [ ] Book a lead — after closing the success view with Done, you should see the "Estimate Added to Calendar" toast at the bottom of `/leads` - [ ] If you're testing in the evening (after 8 PM ET), the Today's route card should still show today's jobs, not tomorrow's ### Notes - Addresses Devin Review's two findings on PR #26 plus the empty-week issue David hit on the Amy Chesson lead. - No SQL, no env vars. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/8f3a19bb9de54f4aa71bb0972e5abac9 Requested by: @arborstarjax-bot ---

author: madmax983
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored string formatting in the Scholar tool (`src/tools/scholar.rs`) to eliminate intermediate heap allocations. Replaced the `format!()` macro + `.push_str()` pattern and an inefficient `.collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")` chain with direct use of `std::fmt::Write` macros (`writeln!` and `write!`).

🎯 **Why**: Generating markdown dynamically previously required making many temporary string allocations on the heap and moving data into a vector just to join it for function signatures. This creates unnecessary work for the allocator and reduces performance, especially on larger programs. 

📊 **Impact**: Reduces heap allocations significantly during API documentation generation (O(n) intermediate arrays/strings completely removed). Ensures zero-cost formatting directly into a pre-allocated `String::with_capacity(4096)` buffer.

🔬 **Measurement**: Run `cargo test` and `cargo run -- doc examples/api.gl` (assuming a target). Or, review the source in `src/tools/scholar.rs` to observe the absence of intermediate `String` or `Vec` collections on the hot path.

body:
### Motivation
- Separar la navegación del bloque de acciones (carrito/usuario) para mejorar jerarquía visual y claridad en mobile/desktop según el requerimiento UX. 
- Mantener el acceso a contacto por WhatsApp sin bloquear contenido, permitiendo que el usuario lo pueda mover si estorba.

### Description
- Se reestructuró `SiteShell` para dividir el header en dos filas: `header-primary-row` (marca + menú hamburguesa) y `header-secondary-row` (carrito + usuario), y se movió la navegación colapsable (`nav-links`) entre ambas filas; cambios en `src/components/site-shell.tsx`.
- Se eliminó el botón de WhatsApp del header y se añadió `DraggableWhatsAppButton`, un anchor flotante que reutiliza la URL de contacto mediante `getWhatsAppHref`, soporta arrastre por `pointer` events, respeta límites del viewport y evita la navegación cuando el usuario mueve el botón accidentalmente (detección `movedDuringDrag`).
- Ajustes en estilos globales (`src/app/globals.css`) para soportar: `header-primary-row`/`header-secondary-row`, nuevo comportamiento de `nav-links` colapsable, y estilos del botón flotante `.whatsapp-floating` (posición fija, tamaño, z-index y cursor de arrastre).
- Actualización de documentación y trazabilidad: `README.md` y `AGENTS.md` registran el cambio y la evidencia de pruebas automatizadas.

### Testing
- Ejecuté `npm run lint` y no se reportaron errores (`✔ No ESLint warnings or errors`).
- Ejecuté `npx tsc --noEmit` para comprobación de tipos y pasó sin errores.

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ vite (7.3.2 → 8.0.9) · [Repo](https://github.com/vitejs/vite) · [Changelog](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Vite Vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read via Vite Dev Server WebSocket

Summary

server.fs check was not enforced to the fetchModule method that is exposed in Vite dev server's WebSocket.

Impact

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

  • explicitly exposes the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option)
  • WebSocket is not disabled by server.ws: false

Arbitrary files on the server (development machine, CI environment, container, etc.) can be exposed.

Details

If it is possible to connect to the Vite dev server’s WebSocket without an Origin header, an attacker can invoke fetchModule via the custom WebSocket event vite:invoke and combine file://... with ?raw (or ?inline) to retrieve the contents of arbitrary files on the server as a JavaScript string (e.g., export default "...").

The access control enforced in the HTTP request path (such as server.fs.allow) is not applied to this WebSocket-based execution path.

PoC

  1. Start the dev server on the target
    Example (used during validation with this repository):

    pnpm -C playground/alias exec vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173

  2. Confirm that access is blocked via the HTTP path (example: arbitrary file)

    curl -i 'http://localhost:5173/@fs/etc/passwd?raw'

    Result: 403 Restricted (outside the allow list)

  3. Confirm that the same file can be retrieved via the WebSocket path
    By connecting to the HMR WebSocket without an Origin header and sending a vite:invoke request that calls fetchModule with a file://... URL and ?raw, the file contents are returned as a JavaScript module.

author: lag-ceo[bot]
body:
## Summary

ADR-only PR. Graduation criterion #2 of `design/adr-code-author-blast-radius-fence.md`. No implementation; ships the design shape so the follow-up implementation PR is mechanical.

## Naming ambiguity surfaced + resolved (per `dev-flag-structural-concerns`)

Reading for context on this PR, I noticed that the fence ADR and the principal-bootstrap ADR (#59) both cite `"D13"` as the medium-tier kill switch. But `DECISIONS.md` D13 is a DIFFERENT decision — `"Telegram-as-operator, tools auto-fire on TG-originated prompts"`. Following that shorthand would either overwrite a real decision or produce a dangling reference.

This ADR names the decision cleanly: `arch-medium-tier-kill-switch`. The ADR also explicitly calls out which design docs still use the ambiguous "D13" shorthand so follow-up PRs can migrate citations.

## Shape (key design choices)

**Three tiers documented** (soft / medium / hard). Soft = what's shipped (file sentinel, iteration-boundary poll). Hard = out of scope (OS-level kill). Medium = this ADR, needed because a code-author can push commits mid-loop and a soft halt that waits for `git push` to finish is an unacceptable blast radius.

**`KillSwitchController`** — `AbortController`-backed; subscribes to `fs.watch` on `.lag/STOP` AND a poll fallback (network shares / Windows / Docker bind mounts drop watch events silently). Composable with parent signals via `AbortSignal.any` so process-level SIGTERM propagates in.

**`runActor`** gains `killSwitchSignal?: AbortSignal`. Back-compat: existing `killSwitch` callback predicate unchanged; either tripping halts the loop. In-flight `observe`/`classify`/`apply` receive the signal via `ActorContext.abortSignal`; adapters thread it into `fetch` + `execa cancelSignal` so halts catch in-flight HTTP + child processes — not just loop boundaries.

**`kill-switch-tripped` atom** — `type: 'observation' + metadata.kind: 'kill-switch-tripped'` discriminator. No AtomType widening (same pattern as `pr-observation`). Written by the runner, not the framework.

**Revocation semantics** (close in-flight draft PR, write `code-author-revoked`) live in the code-author actor's halt handler, NOT in the kill-switch primitive. Framework stays mechanism-only.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Does NOT implement `src/kill-switch/`.
- Does NOT modify `runActor`, adapters, or `ActorContext`.
- Does NOT seed any canon atom.

## Open questions deliberately deferred

1. Halt-latency target (target ~1s from STOP file appearing; benched at implementation time)
2. SIGTERM-ignoring child behavior (that's the hard-tier use case, not medium)
3. Atom-write best-effort when AtomStore is wedged (stderr log + non-zero exit)

## Graduation criteria for the implementation PR

Listed in the ADR. Summary: unit tests for `createKillSwitch` + integration test showing `runActor` halts within 1s + adapter `AbortError` propagation + CPU-overhead bench < 1% idle.

## Canon

- `inv-kill-switch-first` — the invariant this operationalizes.
- `design/adr-code-author-blast-radius-fence.md` — downstream ADR requiring this tier.
- `design/adr-code-author-principal-bootstrap.md` — also cites the medium tier (as "D13").
- `dev-forward-thinking-no-regrets` — ADR-frozen shape means impl is mechanical.
- `dev-flag-structural-concerns` — the reason this ADR exists (D13 shorthand was ambiguous).
- `dev-substrate-not-prescription` — revocation semantics live in actor modules, not framework.

## Context

Opened under `lag-ceo[bot]` attribution via `scripts/gh-as.mjs`.

body:
## Summary

Supersedes PR #139. Addresses all 12 issues flagged by multi-LLM post-implementation review (Gemini 2.5 Pro + Codex gpt-5.4 xhigh + DeepSeek-Reasoner + NotebookLM NB-2) + 1 CI-discovered schema-type bug + 1 SAST finding.

**180 backend tests passing (was 128 before review).**

## What was wrong and what changed

### 🔴 Catastrophic

| # | Commit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| CATA-1 | `e513ea327` | Rename `process_id` → `practice_id` across migration/models/repo/service/engine/events/router/frontend. Prior code read payload.process_id but migration 075's trigger emits practice_id — **accrual never fired in production**. |
| CATA-2 | `c6d9a2f63` | Add `_require_team_or_admin` + `_partner_to_list_dict` DTO. GET /api/partners had no router role check + returned SELECT * → any authenticated user (incl. partner-role) enumerated every partner's NPWP, NIK, bank account, IBAN, fiscal address. |
| CATA-3 | `af0933f12` | Block partner-role on POST /referrals; verify team member owns both the partner AND the practice's client. Previously a partner could POST to their own /referrals with any practice_id → fraud. |
| CATA-4 | `9872af3ce` | **Discovered by CI typecheck.** Migration 119 declared `practice_id UUID` but production `practices.id` is INTEGER (migrations 031/041b/068). FK would have failed on Fly Postgres. Change to INTEGER across schema/models/repo/engine/router/frontend. |

### 🟠 Critical

| # | Commit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| CRIT-1 | `cdc87bc82` | Wrap commission offset + approve transition in `async with conn.transaction()`; add `WHERE status = old_status` guard to prevent concurrent double-offset. |
| CRIT-2 | `43ce6c05a` + `4ad8db253` | Migration 120: `partner_email_outbox` table. activate/mark-paid now enqueue atomically; `POST /api/partners/outbox/flush` sends with backoff + DLQ. Closes the "commission stuck in paid with email lost" gap. |
| CRIT-3 | `7af8e3ae7` | Remove admin fallback in `_require_finance`. Spec required separate perm; prior code let any admin act. |
| CRIT-4 | `4553a6e24` | Remove hardcoded production URL + `"zantara-secret-2024"` fallback in emails.py. Dev/CI without env vars would silently send through prod. |
| CRIT-5 | `8c92d8223` | Block `entity_type='foreign'` at service layer + hide in UI dropdown. NB-2: foreign partners on standard KITAS (E23/E33E/F/G) violate KITAS income restrictions. |
| CRIT-6 | `637320068` | `_sterilize_service_type_for_partner` maps raw "KITAS E33G" to "Visa / KITAS service" in /me/referrals (UU PDP data minimization). |
| CRIT-7 | `928186e95` | Move PPh rates to `system_settings` + add no-NPWP surcharge (+20% Indonesian default). Asya can change rates without code deploy. |
| CRIT-8 | `951c8ad27` + `a131bcb3d` + `76ab379cc` | Align FE/BE contract: GET list returns `{partners,total,page,page_size}`; IDs are UUID strings everywhere; fix wrong endpoint paths; align field names (tax_id→npwp, bank_account_name→bank_account_holder); remove phantom enums; tighten mark-paid prompt validation. |

### 🟡 SAST

| # | Commit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Bandit B701 | `271de2d19` | `jinja2 autoescape=False` → `jinja2.select_autoescape([])`. Bandit's allowlist recognizes the explicit form. Behavior unchanged (markdown templates, no HTML escaping). |

## Companion docs landed

Under `docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-04-21-partners-v1/`:
- `99-synthesis.md` — council triage and 3 path-forward options.
- `ASYA-withholding-rates-runbook.md` — Asya-facing guide for adjusting PPh rates via `system_settings` (no code deploy needed) + 4 open questions before first real payout.
- `POST-MERGE-deploy-runbook.md` — step-by-step migration 119+120 application on Fly, schema verification, smoke endpoints, first accrual E2E.

- \`src-tauri/src/app_runtime_launch.rs\` — 1068 code LoC, zero tests, orchestrates 20+ subsystems. Proposed 3-phase extraction (\`health_probe_phase\`, \`web_server_phase\`, \`scheduler_phase\`). ~1 day.
- \`frontend/src/pages/hooks/useSettingsForm.ts\` — 984 LoC, 10+ concern groups in one hook. Split by concern group. ~1 day.

**🟡 maybe-split (2, watch-items):**
- \`src-tauri/src/updater/install.rs\` (964 code)
- \`crates/oneshim-storage/src/sqlite/web_storage_impl.rs\` (946 code)

- Rust: \`sqlite/maintenance.rs\`, \`frame_storage.rs\`, \`accessibility/windows.rs\`, \`privacy.rs\`, \`local_llm_session.rs\`, \`models/intent.rs\`, \`coaching_engine/mod.rs\`, \`update_coordinator.rs\`, \`monitor.rs\`, handler-per-domain files

1. \`wc -l\` filtered to >500 LOC

Decision document only. **No refactoring in this PR.** Each must-split moves to its own PR if/when executed.

## Summary

When Phase 1b's \`BitVec.ult rhatUn1 (q1c * dLo)\` check fires (Knuth's multiplication-check correction triggers), the post-Phase-1a quotient \`q1c\` must be at least 1.

## Proof

By contradiction: if \`q1c = 0\`, then \`qDlo = 0 * dLo = 0\` and \`rhatUn1 < 0\` is impossible at the Nat level. So \`q1c ≥ 1\`.

## Status

This guarantees the upcoming \`q1' = q1c + signExtend12 4095\` (= \`q1c - 1\`) decrement won't underflow, parallel to how \`div128Quot_first_round_correction\` (#834) needed \`q1.toNat ≥ 2^32 ≥ 1\` to safely decrement after the Phase 1a hi1-correction.

**Stacked on #845.** Next iteration: assemble the Phase 1b correction case theorem (Euclidean preservation when the check fires).

author: parallax1s
body:
## Summary

Doc-only proposal landing the "Path A" groundwork from [PR #8](https://github.com/parallax1s/opsin-pipeline/pull/8)'s §Implications for Stage 4. **No data or code changes.**

Proposes ~40-entry expanded literature calibration (up from current 22) with concrete entries per scaffold, curation ownership, and acceptance criteria.

## The core problem

PR #8 showed PLM delta alone doesn't discriminate useful vs disruptive on the current calibration because both classes cluster at retinal-pocket positions with overlapping PLM plausibility distributions. To test any chemistry-aware scorer (Stage 4), we need a calibration that contains entries *distinguished by substitution chemistry at the same position* — which the current set largely doesn't.

## What this doc proposes

- **Target**: ≥40 entries, ≥10 disruptive, ≥6 neutral.
- **Chemistry-flip pairs** at counterion positions: `D85R/K` (currently only `D85A/V/N/T/S`), `E123K/R` on ChR2, `R82D/E` inverse reversals.
- **Non-pocket neutral controls** (currently absent): surface Lys/Arg, cytoplasmic-domain residues.
- **Conservative variants** (`D85E`, `C128F/W`) at positions where the existing set has only non-conservative substitutions.
- Per-scaffold curation target with PMID/DOI flags marked "verify".

## Acceptance criteria for Path A (explicit)

Before Stage 4 scoring is unblocked:

- [ ] ≥40 total entries with required class balance
- [ ] ≥1 charge-reversal pair per scaffold
- [ ] ≥3 non-pocket neutral controls
- [ ] `cli run` still matches 100% of entries (no stale IDs)
- [ ] At least one scorer variant moves AUROC above 0.5 on the expanded set — otherwise finding is "no discriminative signal, Stage 4 merges flag-off-by-default."

## Ownership

- **Codex** — BR/ChR2 curation (familiar with existing literature source set)
- **User** — CaRhGC entries (Hegemann-lab RhGC spectral tuning context)
- **Me** — rerun ESM2 + calibration pipeline once literature JSON lands; AUROC writeup

## Not a commitment

If you decide Path B instead (ship Stage 4 off-by-default, defer curation), this doc stays as a reference for the follow-up chunk. Nothing here prejudges the direction decision that's still pending on PR #8.

author: pulumi[bot]
body:
## Problems
1. **500 error on registration** -- matrix-js-sdk registerRequest had inconsistent error handling. The SDK threw errors with unexpected structure, causing unhandled exceptions that showed as 500.
2. **Slow connection** -- startClient waited indefinitely for initial sync. On slow servers or with many rooms this could hang forever.

## Fixes
- **Registration rewritten with raw fetch** -- bypasses SDK entirely for register/login. Direct HTTP calls are more reliable and predictable.
- **Login rewritten with raw fetch** -- same approach for consistency.
- **15s sync timeout** -- if initial sync takes longer than 15 seconds, the app loads anyway (rooms will appear as they sync).
- **Reduced sync limit** -- from 20 to 10 messages per room for faster initial load.
- **setDisplayName uses raw fetch** -- never throws, non-critical operation.

body:
Closes #421

## Summary
`global/settings.windows.json` declared `version: "1.12.2"` (parity with
the Linux/macOS `settings.json`) but four hook registrations were
missing, so Windows sessions silently skipped:

| Event | Hook | Status pre-PR |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `PreToolUse: Bash` | `conflict-guard.ps1` | script missing + unregistered |
| `PostCompact` | `post-compact-restore.ps1` | script present, unregistered |
| `InstructionsLoaded` | `instructions-loaded-reinforcer.ps1` | script present, unregistered |
| `TaskCreated` | `task-created-validator.ps1` | script present, unregistered |

The issue body claimed all four `.ps1` scripts existed; in reality
`conflict-guard.ps1` had no PowerShell counterpart. This PR ports it
from `conflict-guard.sh` using the same `CommonHelpers.psm1` response
pattern as `dangerous-command-guard.ps1`.

## Changes
- `global/hooks/conflict-guard.ps1` — new PowerShell port of `conflict-guard.sh` (fail-open, MERGE_HEAD/REBASE_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD detection, porcelain dirty-tree check)
- `global/settings.windows.json` — four hook entries added in matcher/event positions matching settings.json
- `tests/scripts/test-windows-hooks-parity.sh` — compares `(event, matcher, hook-script-basename)` tuples between the two settings files

## Deviation from Issue AC
The issue AC asks for `async: true` on `post-compact-restore` and `task-created-validator`, citing Linux/macOS behavior. In practice, `settings.json` does **not** have `async: true` for those hooks (lines 285, 307). Keeping OS parity took precedence over the AC's premise. A separate PR can enable async on both sides if desired.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `conflict-guard.ps1` registered under `PreToolUse: Bash`
- [x] `post-compact-restore.ps1` registered under `PostCompact` (sync, matches settings.json)
- [x] `instructions-loaded-reinforcer.ps1` registered under `InstructionsLoaded`
- [x] `task-created-validator.ps1` registered under `TaskCreated` (sync, matches settings.json)
- [x] Parity test passes: hook event sets equal between the two files
- [ ] Manual Windows 11 smoke test (deferred to reviewer — no Windows host available in this session)

## Test Plan
```bash
bash tests/scripts/test-windows-hooks-parity.sh
# -> PASS: hook parity between settings.json and settings.windows.json

python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('global/settings.windows.json'))"
# -> JSON valid
```

## Summary

Completes the registry migration foundation laid in #579. Two tag-driven publish workflows, cloned from the working \`publish-test-harness.yml\` pattern, plus the missing \`publishConfig\`/\`repository\` fields on \`crane-mcp/package.json\`.

**Tag conventions** match the harness:

| Tag | Publishes | Dist-tag |
|-----|-----------|----------|
| \`crane-contracts-v0.1.0\` | \`@venturecrane/crane-contracts@0.1.0\` | \`latest\` |
| \`crane-contracts-v0.1.0-rc.1\` | \`@venturecrane/crane-contracts@0.1.0-rc.1\` | \`rc\` |
| \`crane-mcp-v0.2.0\` | \`@venturecrane/crane-mcp@0.2.0\` | \`latest\` |
| \`crane-mcp-v0.2.0-rc.1\` | \`@venturecrane/crane-mcp@0.2.0-rc.1\` | \`rc\` |

Workflows use \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` with \`packages: write\` permission — no separate PAT needed. Post-publish smoke check retries \`npm view\` up to 5 times to handle registry propagation lag.

## Why

Dependabot's \`/packages/crane-mcp\` runs have been failing because \`@venturecrane/crane-mcp\` references \`@venturecrane/crane-contracts\` as a registry semver dep (\`^0.1.0\`), but neither package was actually published to \`npm.pkg.github.com\`. Dependabot's workspace resolver hits the registry, gets 404, aborts with \`security_update_not_possible\`. The other 7 Dependabot directories already went green after #583 + #613; this is the last loose end.

## Publish order after merge

1. Push tag \`crane-contracts-v0.1.0\` → wait for workflow → registry smoke check
2. Push tag \`crane-mcp-v0.2.0\` → wait for workflow → registry smoke check

Order matters: \`crane-mcp\`'s published \`package.json\` declares \`crane-contracts\` as a registry dep, so consumers installing \`crane-mcp\` need \`crane-contracts\` on the registry first.

## Test plan

- [x] \`publishConfig\` + \`repository\` added to \`crane-mcp/package.json\` mirroring the harness/contracts pattern
- [x] Workflows mirror the proven \`publish-test-harness.yml\` reference

- [ ] \`crane-contracts-v0.1.0\` tagged, workflow green, \`npm view\` returns 0.1.0
- [ ] \`crane-mcp-v0.2.0\` tagged, workflow green, \`npm view\` returns 0.2.0
- [ ] Next Dependabot run on \`/packages/crane-mcp\` returns success

## Refs

- #579 (NODE_AUTH_TOKEN foundation)
- #583 (Dependabot registry auth)
- #613 (root \`.npmrc\` scope mapping)
- \`.github/workflows/publish-test-harness.yml\` (cloned pattern)

## Summary

This PR addresses a UX parity gap in Element Web: the Thread list panel's root tiles and latest-reply summaries were rendering message previews as plain text without the message-type prefix (e.g., "Image:", "Audio:", "Video:", "File:", "Poll:") that the Pinned Message Banner already displayed. The prefix-generating logic existed as private functions inside `PinnedMessageBanner.tsx` and was unreachable from thread rendering paths.

This refactor extracts the preview logic into a new shared module `src/components/views/rooms/EventPreview.tsx`, which is now consumed by the Pinned Message Banner, the Thread-list root tile (`EventTile` in `TimelineRenderingType.ThreadsList`), and the Thread Summary reply preview (`ThreadMessagePreview`).

## Key Accomplishments

- **New shared component** `EventPreview.tsx` (244 lines) exporting `EventPreview`, `EventPreviewTile`, and `useEventPreview` with an internal `getPreviewPrefix` helper. Uses `useAsyncMemo` + `useTypedEventEmitter` to handle edit (`Replaced`) and decryption (`Decrypted`) events consistently across all consumers.
- **New shared stylesheet** `_EventPreview.pcss` with `.mx_EventPreview` (ellipsis) and `.mx_EventPreview_prefix` (semibold) — imported alphabetically in `_components.pcss`.
- **PinnedMessageBanner refactored** — local `EventPreview`, `useEventPreview`, `getPreviewPrefix` deleted; unused imports (`M_POLL_START`, `MsgType`, `useMemo`, `MessagePreviewStore`) removed; shared component used at line 108-112 with `mxEvent`, `className`, and `data-testid` props.
- **EventTile ThreadsList path updated** — replaced direct `MessagePreviewStore.instance.generatePreviewForEvent()` call with `<EventPreview mxEvent={this.props.mxEvent} />` at line 1344.
- **ThreadSummary refactored** — `ThreadMessagePreview` now uses the shared hook and `EventPreviewTile`; local state/listeners removed. Includes a regression-safeguard guard matching the pre-refactor short-circuit semantics.
- **i18n keys added** — `event_preview|prefix|{audio,file,image,poll,video}` and `event_preview|preview`; legacy `room|pinned_message_banner|prefix|*` keys retained for backward-compat.
- **Tests updated** — 15 `findByText`/`findByTestId` calls added to accommodate async first-render-null pattern; snapshot regenerated with new `mx_EventPreview_prefix` class names.

## Validation

- **238/238 tests pass** across 11 related suites (PinnedMessageBanner, EventTile, ThreadPanel, ThreadView, TimelinePanel, RoomTile, MessagePreviewStore, RoomHeader, RoomViewStore, i18n-helpers, languageHandler).
- **ESLint, Prettier, and Stylelint all exit 0** on the 10 in-scope files.
- **TypeScript**: in-scope files compile cleanly; the lint script runs the full-repo `tsc --noEmit` which is timeboxed in the build pipeline.
- **6 agent commits** all in-scope; zero out-of-scope modifications (verified via `git log --author="agent@blitzy.com" --name-only`).

## Known Regression Fix (commit 7b66125842)

During initial validation, an async-pattern mismatch caused `MemberAvatar` to render during `TimelinePanel.onLoaded`'s setState flush with a transient incomplete `RoomMember`, triggering `useIdColorHash` to crash. Four targeted fixes resolved it: switched from `useMemo` → `useAsyncMemo` (first render null), normalized empty preview strings to `null`, added an explicit guard in `ThreadMessagePreview`, and migrated tests to async queries.

## Out-of-Scope Pre-Existing Issues (not caused by AAP work)

Two pre-existing issues documented and forensically verified as unrelated to this AAP: (1) `StopGapWidgetDriver` TS errors due to upstream matrix-js-sdk renaming `encryptToDeviceMessages`; (2) `ReadReceiptGroup-test.tsx` snapshot failure due to a hardcoded 2024 date in time-dependent assertions. Both are out of the AAP's 10-file scope.

## Remaining Work Before Production

- Playwright E2E test exercising thread-panel preview prefix rendering (3.0 h)
- Manual QA against a live Matrix homeserver with real encrypted events (2.0 h)
- Translation coordination for new `event_preview|prefix|*` keys (2.0 h)
- Visual-regression (Percy/Chromatic) review (1.5 h)
- Fix pre-existing `ReadReceiptGroup` snapshot regression (out-of-scope, 1.0 h)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Hotfix for a live-data regression introduced by #13. **Observed production symptom**: `broker=zerodha`, `websocket.connected=true`, **but `tokens_subscribed=0`** → dashboard silent, `/api/forecast` stuck on `source="synthetic"` even during market hours. **Cause**: #13 moved the historical-REST seed call to run *before* `ws.set_tokens(tokens)`. That ordering is correct for candle-series monotonicity, but it couples subscription liveness to the health of the historical-data endpoint. If Kite's historical REST is slow, rate-limited, or the account doesn't have the historical-data entitlement, the seed blocks the watchlist thread, `set_tokens` never runs, and the ticker stays connected with zero subscriptions. **Fix**: 1. Restore `ws.set_tokens(tokens)` **before** the seed call in `app.py`. Live ticks now start flowing the instant the watchlist resolves, independent of REST health. 2. Rewrite `CandleBuilder.seed_history()` to **merge + sort by timestamp** (with dedupe, live candles winning on ties) rather than naive-append. This preserves the monotonic-series guarantee that #13's reordering was enforcing, without coupling it to call-site ordering. Trade-off considered: the original reordering in #13 was pushed by Devin Review to prevent a race where a minute-rollover during the ~10-30 s of seed HTTP calls could let a live tick-built candle land in the deque before historical bars, producing a non-monotonic series. Merge-sort in `seed_history()` handles that race at the data-structure level — stronger guarantee, no call-site coupling, zero risk of blocking subscription again. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Pull, restart uvicorn during market hours, verify `curl /api/health` reports **`tokens_subscribed > 0`** within a few seconds of boot. - [ ] Verify startup log order: `Subscribed KiteTicker to N tokens` now appears **before** `History seed: ...`. (It was the other way in #13.) - [ ] Wait ~1-2 min after boot, then `curl /api/forecast?symbol=NIFTY` — `"source"` should be `"live"` once at least 20 completed bars exist (seeded + fresh ticks combined). - [ ] If the historical-data entitlement is missing on your Kite plan, seed will log `errors=N` but the ticker still subscribes — regression would have blocked subscription entirely. ### Notes - 54/54 unit tests pass, ruff clean. - 2 new tests: - `test_seed_history_merges_with_live_ticks_in_chronological_order` — proves the deque stays sorted when seed arrives after live ticks. - `test_seed_history_live_candle_wins_on_timestamp_collision` — pins the tie-breaking rule. - No API surface changes, no frontend changes. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ffb935b1841f4ae3bb43a24b92a10935 Requested by: @Vishalbalupatil ---

## Summary

Single cleanup PR addressing the four out-of-the-box deploy failures filed in #1-#4. Each bullet maps 1:1 to an issue:

- **#1 — PyPI build**: switches the build backend from setuptools to hatchling and bumps `version` to `0.0.3`, so the broken `0.0.2.2` sdist on PyPI can be superseded. `packages = [\"merle\"]` under `tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel` pulls in `merle/templates/` automatically — no more `package_data` format.
- **#2 — Ollama tarball 404**: `merle/templates/Dockerfile.template` now pulls `ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst` and extracts with `tar --zstd`; `zstd` is added to the `dnf`/`microdnf` install line.
- **#3 — prepare copies consumer's pyproject.toml + zappa pinned**: adds `merle/templates/pyproject.toml.template` — a minimal manifest with a single `merle @ git+https://github.com/zappa/zappa-merle.git` dep — and generates it into the model cache dir instead of copying the consumer's `pyproject.toml`. Dockerfile's `uv sync` gets `--no-install-project` so the stub manifest doesn't need a backend. Zappa pin relaxed to `>=0.61.2,<0.63`.
- **#4 — zappa PATH + authorizer cache**: `merle.managers._subprocess_env_with_venv_bin()` prepends `Path(sys.executable).parent` onto `PATH` for both `zappa deploy` and `zappa undeploy`, so zappa resolves when merle is launched via its fully-qualified venv path. `authorizer.py` now returns `arn:aws:execute-api:region:account:api-id/*/*/*` for both Allow and Deny so API Gateway's token-keyed `result_ttl` cache covers every path under the same token rather than wedging on the first method.

Also includes housekeeping already on the branch: CI Python 3.14, pre-commit ruff bump.

body:
# Issue #8: Rename content.md to SKILL.md and support references/ subdirectory

Closes #8

## Summary

Adopt the agentskills.io open standard across all three build targets.

- Source skill body filename: `content.md` -> `SKILL.md`
- New optional `references/` subdirectory per skill, recursively copied into every target's skill directory
- Claude target migrated to directory format (`.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`) with YAML frontmatter, matching the official Claude Code skills spec

## Changes

### Source layout

```
templates/skills/<id>/
  skill.yaml
  graph.yaml
  SKILL.md            # was content.md
  references/         # optional, any files/subdirs
```

### Build output per target

| Target | Skill location | references/ copied to |
|--------|----------------|-----------------------|
| GHCP | `.github/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` + `skills/<id>/SKILL.md` | both locations |
| Claude | `.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` (**new dir format**) | `.claude/skills/<id>/references/` |
| Codex | `.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` + `skills/<id>/SKILL.md` | both locations |

### Breaking change (Claude)

Previously the Claude build wrote single files at `.claude/skills/<id>.md` (legacy `.claude/commands/` compat). The new layout matches the official Claude Code Skills spec (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) and agentskills.io standard. Users re-running `afs setup --agent claude` will have their Claude skill files replaced with the new directory layout.

`CLAUDE.md` itself is unchanged, so inline skill content is backward compatible.
