author: mkhomutov
body:
## Summary

Transitions [RFC 0017 — Persona Memory Injection Token Budget](../blob/feature/v022-rfc-0017-acceptance/docs/rfcs/0017-persona-memory-injection-budget.md) from `📋 Proposed` → `👍 Accepted` for v0.2.2, commits answers to the resolvable open questions, and folds in a directly cost-saving design addition: an empty-context TICK short-circuit that closes a real budget-drain bug in the persona tick loop.

No code changes. Docs only. Implementation begins under `0017-pr-plan.md` (Phase 3 of the dev workflow), tracked separately.

## Open question resolutions (committed at acceptance)

| OQ | Status | Resolution |
|----|--------|------------|
| **OQ1** — `_MEMORY_BUDGET_TOKENS` default | ✅ Resolved | **1500 tokens** for Phase 1. ~6× the current 300-char relationship cap and ~3× the 500-char note cap at ~4 chars/token. Phase 1 smoke test may retune as a one-line constant change without re-acceptance. |
| **OQ2** — `min_score` default value | ⏳ Deferred to Phase 2 | Empirical task — calibration script against a populated FTS5 DB. Acceptance does not gate on this; the API contract (`min_score: float \| None` in `[0, 1]`, `None` = current behaviour) is what's stable. |
| **OQ3** — per-tier vs global `min_score` | ✅ Resolved | **Per-tier.** Episodic and notes get separate calibrated defaults (`_DEFAULT_EPISODIC_MIN_SCORE`, `_DEFAULT_NOTES_MIN_SCORE`) because their BM25 distributions differ enough that a single threshold would either over-filter notes or under-filter episodes. |
| **OQ4** — allocator fairness mode | ✅ Resolved | **No fairness.** Greedy in priority order. Tier priorities (relationship=8, episodic=7, notes=6) already encode the right ordering. Revisit only if Phase 2 telemetry shows persistent low-tier starvation; that would be a future RFC, not v0.2.2. |
| **OQ5** — per-event vs per-turn budget | ⏳ Out of scope | Deferred to RFC 0008 (scheduler-level). The per-event allocator composes under it (Section E forward-compatibility). |

## New: empty-context TICK short-circuit (Section F)

The user flagged a real budget bug: **agents loaded into memory but contextually idle still drain budget on every tick**. Investigation confirmed the mechanism — [`TickScheduler`](../blob/feature/v022-rfc-0017-acceptance/agents/tick.py) only suppresses LLM calls after `idle_after_ticks` (default 10) consecutive `DO_NOTHING` actions, so a freshly-loaded persona issues up to **10 full LLM calls over ~10 minutes** before idle suppression engages, even if it has nothing to think about.

With the budget allocator (Section B) and `min_score` threshold (Section C) from this RFC, those calls now provably carry **zero memory tokens** (the boilerplate tick query falls below the threshold; relationship and notes contribute nothing without an interlocutor). Issuing an LLM call whose entire memory contribution is empty is a budget bug — the model has nothing to reason about beyond the static persona prompt.

**Fix (folded into Phase 2):** `_inject_memory_context` exposes `memory_admitted_tokens`. The persona runtime's TICK handler skips the LLM call when:

```
event.type == TICK
AND memory_admitted_tokens == 0
AND no active goal payload
AND no pending conversation turn
```

The skipped tick records `DO_NOTHING` (advances `idle_count` immediately on cold-start instead of after 10 minutes) and logs at `DEBUG` with reason `empty_context_tick`. Goal #8 added to the Goals list; Section F added to the design (with mermaid flow); Phase 2 deliverables and Files Touched table updated.

**Why this belongs in RFC 0017 and not a separate RFC:** the safety signal that makes the short-circuit non-regressive — *zero items admitted at the budget layer* — only exists once Sections B–C land. Implementing it independently would have to re-derive that signal by inspecting tier outputs separately, duplicating logic the allocator already centralises. Atomic with Phase 2.

## Files changed

- [docs/rfcs/0017-persona-memory-injection-budget.md](../blob/feature/v022-rfc-0017-acceptance/docs/rfcs/0017-persona-memory-injection-budget.md) — header status → Accepted, ToC entry for Section F, Goal 8, Section F design, Phase 2 deliverable additions, Files Touched additions, OQ resolutions, Decision/Next Steps rewritten for post-acceptance.
- [ROADMAP.md](../blob/feature/v022-rfc-0017-acceptance/ROADMAP.md) — RFC tracker row → 👍 Accepted; current-milestone line: "RFC 0017 authoring" → "RFC 0017 PR plan"; last-updated note refreshed.

## Out of scope for this PR

- `docs/rfcs/0017-pr-plan.md` — created as the next PR, per [development-workflow.md](../blob/feature/v022-rfc-0017-acceptance/docs/development-workflow.md) Phase 3.
- Any code under `agents/persona_runtime/` or `agents/memory/` — implementation lands per the PR plan.

## Status hygiene

- [x] RFC header status updated (Proposed → Accepted, Accepted date added)
- [x] ROADMAP RFC tracker updated
- [x] ROADMAP current-milestone updated
- [x] No stale Decision/Next Steps text
- [x] No references to PR review reports (per `.github/copilot-instructions.md`)

author: ianlintner
body:
## Summary

- Opens Phase 6 of `docs/oauth2-spec-audit.md` with an explicit RFC 9700 section-by-section compliance matrix, a 14-item chunked plan, and a 13-point conformance-vector checklist.
- Threads RFC 8707 `resource` through the refresh-token grant so rotated access tokens honor audience narrowing (§2.3). Prior code only wired this on the initial authorize and client_credentials paths.
- Switches login-submit redirects from HTTP 302 Found to 303 See Other across both success and failure branches so user-agents cannot forward the form body to the redirect target (§4.11).
- Adds `tests/rfc9700_compliance.rs` — 3 new integration tests that verify audience wiring, the 303 post-credential redirect, and discovery-document exclusions (no `password`, no `token`, no `plain`; advertises `S256` and RFC 9207 `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported=true`).

## Scope / non-goals

Phase 6 has 14 items total; this PR delivers the three that can land without schema migrations. The remaining items are captured in `docs/oauth2-spec-audit.md` §9.2 and will ship as independent PRs:

- 6.1 Revoke token family on authorization-code replay (requires migration V15 adding `token_family` to `authorization_codes` + Storage trait changes across SQLite/Postgres/Mongo).
- 6.2 Full DPoP / mTLS proof validation on token use.
- 6.5 JWT client-assertion `jti` replay store.
- 6.3 (complete schema-level): storing `resource` on the `tokens` row so refresh without an explicit `resource` inherits the original audience.
- 6.4, 6.6, 6.7 (completed here), 6.8–6.14.

## Files touched

| `crates/oauth2-actix/src/handlers/oauth.rs` | Refresh grant forwards `req.resource` into `CreateToken` |

- RFC 8707 — Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0

### Motivation

- Provide realtime message push to web clients (STOMP over WebSocket) and a full IM workflow that links WhatsApp webhook → AI auto-reply → CRM records → agent handover.
- Centralize CRM integration and admin APIs so frontend and operators can manage agents, levels, assignments and leads.
- Improve robustness for media, scheduling (auto-offline), reconnect/resend and JSON time handling.

### Description

- Added documentation files under `docs/` describing WebSocket usage, product design, technical design and project status.
- Enabled WebSocket/STOMP endpoint `/ws` and simple broker `/topic` via `WebSocketConfig`, and added `spring-boot-starter-websocket` dependency in `pom.xml`.
- Global app configuration improvements: global `CorsConfig`, `JacksonConfig` (register time modules / disable timestamps), `CrmConfig` for CRM properties and `application.properties` sample entries.
- Implemented a comprehensive set of REST controllers for IM/CRM operations: `AuthController`, `ChatController`, `AgentController`, `AgentAccountController`, `AgentLevelController`, `AgentStatusController`, `ClueController`, and `GlobalExceptionHandler`.
- Introduced domain DTOs and webhook models for WhatsApp messages and parser enhancements in `WhatsAppMessageParser` and webhook request/value classes to support context/referral/status fields.
- Implemented services and interfaces for core functionality: `CrmOpenApiService`, `AgentDispatchService`, `ChatHistoryService`, `AgentPushService`, `CacheSyncService`, `SendMessageService`, and AI service improvements; plus substantial CRM adapter `CrmOpenApiServiceImpl` to map CRM worksheet interactions.
- Added in-memory runtime implementations for dispatch and history: `InMemoryAgentDispatchService` and `InMemoryChatHistoryService` and a WebSocket push implementation `WebSocketAgentPushServiceImpl` using `SimpMessagingTemplate` with failure buffering and `ws/reconnected` support.
- Enhanced WhatsApp handling and AI flow in `WhatsAppWebhookServiceImpl`: better message parsing, local history write, CRM recording, assignment logic, 24h/30d rules, AI fallback, and push to assigned agent when online.
- Media and messaging improvements in `SendMessageServiceImpl`: media upload to Meta (`uploadMedia`), unified `sendMediaMessage` (supporting mediaId/link), additional convenience methods and mime-type resolution; async send with logging.
- Agent presence and inactivity handling: `AgentSessionActivityService`, `AgentWebSocketPresenceListener`, `AgentInactiveScheduler` and `ConversationTimeoutScheduler` to auto-offline inactive agents and trigger AI fallback where appropriate; `CacheSyncService` to sync CRM → local state on startup/login.
- Miscellaneous: enable scheduling (`@EnableScheduling`), added many request/response model classes, improved Dify AI client logging, and added multipart max file size properties.

### Testing

- No automated tests were added or modified as part of this change.

Agencies can set a custom logo, site name, and favicon for the admin panel, separate from public site settings.

### Patch Changes

-   [#680](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/680) [`2e4b205`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/2e4b205b1df30bdb6bb96259f223b85610de5e78) Thanks [@CacheMeOwside](https://github.com/CacheMeOwside)! - Fixes dark mode toggle having no effect with the classic theme.

-   [#732](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/732) [`e3e18aa`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/e3e18aae92d31cf22efd11a0ba06110de24a076a) Thanks [@jcheese1](https://github.com/jcheese1)! - Fixes select dropdown appearing behind dialog by removing explicit z-index values and adding `isolate` to the admin body for proper stacking context.

-   [#647](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/647) [`743b080`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/743b0807f1a37fdedbcd37632058b557f493f3be) Thanks [@arashackdev](https://github.com/arashackdev)! - Adds Persian (Farsi) locale with full admin translations.
    Adds Vazirmatn as the default font family for Farsi.

-   [#689](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/689) [`fa8d753`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/fa8d7533e8ba7e02599372d580399dae88ecd891) Thanks [@edrpls](https://github.com/edrpls)! - Fixes the taxonomy term picker to match across diacritic boundaries.

    Typing `Mexico` in the admin picker now surfaces a term labeled `México` instead of prompting a duplicate create. Input and term labels are folded via NFD decomposition + lowercase before substring-matching, so editors who type without diacritics — or with locale keyboards that produce precomposed vs. combining forms — still see the canonical term.

    Before this fix, `"mexico"` and `"méxico"` were treated as distinct strings, so the picker showed zero suggestions and the editor had no way to find the existing term except to create a duplicate. Duplicate terms then split the taxonomy and broke public-facing filter pages that group content by slug.

    The exact-match check that gates the "Create new term" button uses the same fold, so typing `Mexico` when `México` exists also suppresses Create — closing the duplicate-creation loop.

-   Updated dependencies \[]:
    -   @emdash-cms/blocks@0.7.0

## emdash@0.7.0

### Minor Changes

-   [#705](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/705) [`8ebdf1a`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/8ebdf1af65764cc4b72624e7758c4a666817aade) Thanks [@eba8](https://github.com/eba8)! - Adds admin white-labeling support via `admin` config in `astro.config.mjs`. Agencies can set a custom logo, site name, and favicon for the admin panel, separate from public site settings.

-   [#742](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/742) [`c26442b`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/c26442be9887f1e3d3df37db5ccda6b260820a77) Thanks [@ascorbic](https://github.com/ascorbic)! - Adds `trustedProxyHeaders` config option so self-hosted deployments behind a reverse proxy can declare which client-IP headers to trust. Used by auth rate limits (magic-link, signup, passkey, OAuth device flow) and the public comment endpoint — without it, every request on a non-Cloudflare deployment was treated as "unknown" and rate limits were effectively disabled.

    Set the option in `astro.config.mjs`:

    ```js
    emdash({
    	trustedProxyHeaders: ["x-real-ip"], // nginx, Caddy, Traefik
    });
    ```

    or via the `EMDASH_TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADERS` env var (comma-separated). Headers are tried in order; values ending in `forwarded-for` are parsed as comma-separated lists.

    Also removes the user-agent-hash fallback on the comment endpoint. The fallback was meant to give anonymous commenters on non-Cloudflare deployments something approximating per-user rate limiting, but the UA is trivially rotatable; requests with no trusted IP now share a stricter "unknown" bucket. Operators behind a reverse proxy should set `trustedProxyHeaders` to restore per-IP bucketing.

    **Only set `trustedProxyHeaders` when you control the reverse proxy.** Trusting a forwarded-IP header from the open internet lets any client spoof their IP and defeats rate limiting.

### Patch Changes

-   [#745](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/745) [`7186961`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/7186961d3cbf706c1248e9e40b14b1a545ce8586) Thanks [@ascorbic](https://github.com/ascorbic)! - Fixes an unauthenticated denial-of-service via the 404 log. Every 404 response previously inserted a new row into `_emdash_404_log`, so an attacker could grow the database without bound by requesting unique nonexistent URLs. Repeat hits to the same path now dedup into a single row with a `hits` counter and `last_seen_at` timestamp, referrer and user-agent headers are truncated to bounded lengths, and the log is capped at 10,000 rows with oldest-first eviction.

-   [#739](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/739) [`e9ecec2`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/e9ecec2d2dfb20ab4c413fb593a09a9f6d0fb27e) Thanks [@MohamedH1998](https://github.com/MohamedH1998)! - Fixes the REST content API silently stripping `publishedAt` on create/update and `createdAt` on create. Importers can now preserve original publish and creation dates on migrated content. Gated behind `content:publish_any` (EDITOR+) so regular contributors cannot backdate posts. `createdAt` is intentionally not accepted on update — `created_at` is treated as immutable.

-   [#732](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/732) [`e3e18aa`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/e3e18aae92d31cf22efd11a0ba06110de24a076a) Thanks [@jcheese1](https://github.com/jcheese1)! - Fixes select dropdown appearing behind dialog by removing explicit z-index values and adding `isolate` to the admin body for proper stacking context.

-   [#695](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/695) [`fae63bd`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/fae63bdae8ff798a420379c36d3d05e54ea3628a) Thanks [@ascorbic](https://github.com/ascorbic)! - Fixes `emdash seed` so entries declared with `"status": "published"` are actually published. Previously the seed wrote the content row with `status: "published"` and a `published_at` timestamp but never created a live revision, so the admin UI showed "Save & Publish" instead of "Unpublish" and `live_revision_id` stayed null. The seed now promotes published entries to a live revision on both create and update paths.

-   [#744](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/pull/744) [`30d8fe0`](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/commit/30d8fe00025e058c71c8bfcd296946bb2042c4a7) Thanks [@ascorbic](https://github.com/ascorbic)! - Fixes a setup-window admin hijack by binding `/setup/admin` and `/setup/admin/verify` to a per-session nonce cookie. Previously an unauthenticated attacker who could reach a site during first-time setup could POST to `/setup/admin` between the legitimate admin's email submission and passkey verification, overwriting the stored email — the admin account would then be created with the attacker's address. The admin route now mints a cryptographically random nonce, stores it in setup state, and sets it as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, `/_emdash/`-scoped cookie; the verify route rejects any request whose cookie does not match in constant time.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent unnecessary sensor SPI initialisation and avoid false hardware detection when modules are not compiled in or required pins are unavailable.
- Make module detection decisions use compiled feature flags and explicit pin-count checks to more accurately reflect available hardware.

### Description
- Replace the generic `hal_esp32_requires_sensor_spi()` usage with explicit availability checks that combine `feat::...()` and `FEAT_PINS_*` counts and only initialize the sensor SPI when at least one SPI-capable module is actually available.
- Update sensor bus init logging to report availability using the derived booleans `imu_available`, `ads_available`, and `act_available` instead of raw `feat::` queries.
- In `hal_esp32_init_all()` use the same availability booleans to decide whether to call `hal_imu_begin()`, `hal_steer_angle_begin()`, and `hal_actuator_begin()` and improve log messages to indicate module unavailability or inactive capability.
- In `modulesInit()` replace `feat::...()` checks with module-level compiled flags (`g_features[MOD_*].compiled`) for Ethernet/ADS/IMU/Actuator/Safety detection paths so detection is skipped when the module is not compiled in.
- Minor whitespace/format tweaks in `hal_bno085.cpp`.

### Testing
- Built the ESP32 firmware (full project compile) after the changes; the compile succeeded. 
- Ran static compile-time checks (build-time warnings/errors); no new errors were introduced.

author: copilot
body:
Introduces the foundational Platform Abstraction Layer (PAL) enabling dual-runtime deployment: Power Apps / Dataverse as primary host, SQLite as fallback, and in-memory for local dev.

## Domain model
- `src/domain/correspondence.ts` — `Correspondence` entity with `CorrespondenceDirection` and `CorrespondenceStatus` enums (canonical domain model, separate from existing UI types in `mocks/uiData.ts`)

## Platform contracts (`src/platform/contracts/`)
Six typed interfaces defining the host-agnostic service boundary:
- `ICorrespondenceRepository` — CRUD + branch filter
- `IUserRepository`, `IBranchRepository`, `IDepartmentRepository`
- `IReferenceConfigRepository`
- `INotificationService` + `NotificationPayload`

## Host adapter interface
`IHostAdapter` aggregates all contracts into a single injection point:
```ts
export interface IHostAdapter {
  correspondences: ICorrespondenceRepository;
  users: IUserRepository;
  branches: IBranchRepository;
  departments: IDepartmentRepository;
  referenceConfigs: IReferenceConfigRepository;
  notifications: INotificationService;
  sequenceStore: SequenceStore;
}
```

## Adapter implementations
- **`inMemory/`** — fully wired, backed by existing seed data; default for local dev
- **`dataverse/`** — stub; all methods throw `not yet implemented`
- **`sqlite/`** — stub; same pattern, ready for driver wiring

## Factory + config
- `hostAdapterFactory.ts` — `createHostAdapter(target: PlatformTarget): IHostAdapter`
- `systemConfig.ts` extended with `PlatformTarget` (`"IN_MEMORY" | "DATAVERSE" | "SQLITE"`), `PlatformConfig`, and `platformConfig` (defaults to `IN_MEMORY`)

### Motivation
- Replace heavyweight Plotly bar charts with a lightweight, consistent HTML/CSS response-scale widget to improve layout density and visual consistency.
- Surface respondent metadata (filtered N and per-item response counts) alongside mean responses in a compact format.
- Improve readability of item descriptions and tighten header spacing and overview copy to match updated UI styling.

### Description
- Add `render_response_scale_bar` to render a compact custom 1–7 response bar with HTML/CSS and embedded mean and anchors, including a minimum visible fill for low scores.
- Replace Plotly-based charts in `render_overview_question_blocks` and `render_item_question_bar` with calls to `render_response_scale_bar`, and thread `respondent_n` through `render_item_blocks`/`render_item_question_bar` so per-item metadata is shown.
- Replace the DataFrame display in `render_item_description_expander` with a custom HTML table via `st.markdown` for improved styling and fixed layout, and add expanders showing all Table 1 and Table 2 item descriptions in the overview.
- Adjust header CSS padding in `render_top_bar_title` and update overview text to include an inline DOI link and revised section headings.

### Testing

author: ysmolski
body:
This PR supports cost weights on the arguments of the directives. When a customer applies such a directive with the specific non-null argument to a field, then its cost will be added to the cost of the field.

Composition now tracks weights for arguments of directives for each field. This is a static data so it goes into the config of a schema. It is needed for the engine to understand where directives' arguments with costs were used. 
Router/engine uses it to take those weights into costs accounting.

If such directive was applied to the implementing type of some interface, and if the interface type is being used in the operation, then all the implementing types are taken into an account and maximum weight is picked among them.

I have added just a simple e2e test to verify that feature is working. More extended tests are implemented in the corresponding [engine PR](https://github.com/wundergraph/graphql-go-tools/pull/1465).

Example how cost from the directive could be added to the `employees' field of the `Engineer` type:
```graphql
directive @expensiveOp(applied: Boolean = true @cost(weight: 22)) on FIELD_DEFINITION

type Engineer implements RoleType {
  departments: [Department!]!
  title: [String!]!
  employees: [Employee!]! @goField(forceResolver: true) @expensiveOp
  engineerType: EngineerType!
}
```

See [documentation preview](https://wundergraphinc-yury-eng-8700-router-support-cost-on-the-arg.mintlify.app/router/security/cost-control#weights-on-directive-arguments) for more.

author: tmchow
body:
## Summary

Skills across the plugin instructed agents to use the platform's blocking question tool (`AskUserQuestion` / `request_user_input` / `ask_user`) with a fallback when "the tool is unavailable." Two bugs fell through that phrasing, both manifesting as silent skips of required questions:

1. **Codex edit modes** — `request_user_input` is only exposed in Plan mode ‼️. In file-editing modes the call fails, and agents skipped the question instead of falling back.
2. **Claude Code** — `AskUserQuestion` is a deferred tool whose schema isn't loaded at session start. Agents read "unavailable" as "not yet loaded" and jumped straight to the text fallback instead of calling `ToolSearch` to load the schema.

Fixes #612

## Change

Tighten the canonical sentence in `AGENTS.md` and every skill site:

- Name the tool for each platform.
- Instruct Claude Code to call `ToolSearch` with `select:AskUserQuestion` first if the schema isn't loaded. A pending schema load is explicitly *not* a fallback trigger.
- Narrow the fallback condition to "no blocking tool exists in the harness or the call errors," with Codex edit modes called out as a concrete example.
- When the fallback does apply, require numbered options in chat with no silent skipping.

37 skill `SKILL.md` and reference files receive the unified sentence; `AGENTS.md` gets the canonical checklist. Existing preload rules in `ce-code-review` and `ce-doc-review` tighten the fallback trigger from the loose "unavailable" to the explicit "`ToolSearch` returns no match, the tool call explicitly fails, or the runtime mode does not expose it."

## Forward compatibility

`AGENTS.md` notes that these constraints reflect platform behavior as of April 2026. If Anthropic un-defers `AskUserQuestion` or Codex exposes `request_user_input` in edit modes, revisit the guidance rather than carry the workaround forward indefinitely.

author: victorpurmar
body:
## Summary
Three small follow-ups surfaced during reviews of the previous lifecycle/terminal PRs (#254, #255, #256, #257). Each has its own commit and independent tests.

### 1. I2 — filter `_cc` JSON markers from `run.log`
The xterm pane in the dashboard was showing raw JSON like `{"_cc": "analyzing", "dimension": "security"}` mixed into the human-readable stderr stream. These are structured IPC markers (emitted by `emit_marker` to update `phase` / `current_dimension` on the job) — they should never reach the terminal view.

**Fix:** `_consume_stream` now skips `_tee_run_log` for lines starting with `{"_cc`. `_append_log` still parses the marker to keep the IPC role intact — only the literal JSON string is kept out of `run.log`.

### 2. Task 1 race — `RunLogWriter.write` vs `close`
The pre-lock `if self._fh is None` check was racy: thread A could pass the check (file still open), queue on the lock, wait while thread B ran `close()` under the lock and nulled `_fh`, then acquire the lock and call `self._fh.write(text)` — AttributeError on NoneType, escaping the `except OSError` clause and contradicting the module's "silent-by-design, diagnostic-only" contract.

**Fix:** moved the None-check INSIDE the lock, using a local ref (`fh = self._fh`). Also added `__enter__`/`__exit__` so callers can `with RunLogWriter(d) as w:` for guaranteed cleanup on any exit path. New tests include a stress test that actually exercises the race and a serial regression guard.

### 3. I3 — LiveTerminal infinite reconnect on 404
When a pre-feature run (no `run.log`) was opened in the dashboard, the SSE endpoint returned 404. `EventSource` auto-reconnects on `error` events indefinitely, so the browser hammered the endpoint and the user saw an empty terminal with no explanation.

**Fix:** the component now probes `/api/jobs/<id>/logs?since=0` (plain JSON, no streaming) first. On 404 / 410 / network error / any non-`ok` response, it renders a muted placeholder (`No terminal output captured for this run.` / `Run artifacts removed.` / `Log unavailable (HTTP N).`) and skips `EventSource` entirely. A `cancelled` flag ensures unmounting before the probe resolves prevents a stray connection from opening after teardown.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest` — 2048 passing (+3 from baseline 2045)
- [x] `npx vitest run LiveTerminal.test.jsx` — 7 passing (probe, 404, 410, network, unmount, done, cancelled-before-probe)
- [x] `npx vitest run EvaluationStatus.test.jsx` — 6 passing (no regressions; LiveTerminal is mocked there)
- [x] `npm run build` — exits 0
- [x] Manual: open a pre-feature run in the dashboard → placeholder text appears, no network-tab spam
- [x] Manual: open a Plan-A run → terminal streams live as before
- [x] Manual: inspect `run.log` of a dashboard-spawned run → no `_cc` JSON lines

## Non-blocking follow-ups (not in this PR)
- `sync_index` walks the full evaluations tree on every list request. Profile at scale; if it becomes a hot path, memoize walks via a TTL or cache invalidation on `status_mtime`.
- Plan B1 reviewer flagged a minor path duplication between `_score_completed_evidence` in `cancel_evaluation` (mixed skip-for-ext-) and the status-poll path — worth reconciling.

body:
The volatile support does not have test coverage, and dates back to when this transform was originally introduced 20 years ago, so it does not appear that volatile support was specifically added -- it was just naively implemented to start with, and then received bug fixes.

The current implementation is still buggy, e.g. it allows sinking volatile past inaccessiblemem calls, which is invalid (as those may contain volatile accesses on allocas).

After https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/192992, there would be another constraint that all the instructions after the volatile load are speculatable.

This wouldn't be hard to fix, but I'd rather remove volatile support here entirely.

author: scrambled2
body:
## Problem

Running the command suggested in the README:

```
/plugin marketplace add pixeltable/pixeltable-skill
```

…currently fails with:

```
Error: Failed to parse marketplace file at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json:
Invalid schema: ... owner: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined,
plugins: Invalid input: expected array, received undefined
```

The shipped `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` contains plugin-manifest fields (`name`, `display_name`, `description`, `categories`, `tags`, `homepage`) rather than a marketplace manifest. Claude Code distinguishes these two files: a **marketplace** describes a *catalog* of plugins (requires `owner` object + `plugins` array), while a **plugin** (already correctly defined in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) describes a single plugin.

Because of this, `/plugin marketplace add` rejects the file before any plugin can be discovered, and `/plugin install pixeltable-skill@pixeltable-skill` subsequently fails with *"Plugin not found in any marketplace"*. Today the skill can only be installed via the `install.sh` script (direct skill copy), bypassing the `/plugin` management system entirely.

## Fix

Replace `marketplace.json` with a proper marketplace manifest that catalogs the single plugin already defined at the repo root:

- `owner` object with name + url
- `metadata` with description and version
- `plugins` array containing one entry pointing at `source: "."` (the existing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`)
- Descriptive fields (category, tags, homepage) preserved on the plugin entry

Schema reference: <https://anthropic.com/claude-code/marketplace.schema.json>

The schema shape mirrors other working Claude Code marketplaces (the official `anthropics/claude-code` marketplace and `huggingface/skills`).

## Result

After this change:

```
/plugin marketplace add pixeltable/pixeltable-skill      # succeeds
/plugin install pixeltable-skill@pixeltable-skill        # succeeds
```

Users get `/plugin`-managed install/update/uninstall for free. The `install.sh` path still works unchanged for users who prefer direct skill copy (Cursor, air-gapped, etc.).

## Test plan

- [x] JSON is valid
- [x] Schema shape matches the official Anthropic marketplace and `huggingface/skills`
- [ ] Maintainer: verify `/plugin marketplace add pixeltable/pixeltable-skill` resolves on a branch build before merging

Long-press speed boost was fixed at 2x; this change makes long-press speed directional and continuous via horizontal drag. While holding, dragging right increases speed up to 4x and dragging left reduces speed down to 0.25x, without applying cursed-speed ranges.

    - `->` increases speed

  - Temporary long-press speed is clamped to `0.25x..4x`.

- **Runtime polish**
  - Added drag update sensitivity constant and small delta threshold to avoid redundant playback-speed writes during move events.
  - Standardized speed label formatting to fixed precision for stable display.

```kotlin
val targetSpeed = clamp(

    0.25f,

if (abs(targetSpeed - lastFastForwardSpeed) >= minSpeedUpdateDelta) {

}
```

body:
## Summary

Three targeted library adoptions picked out of a research pass over LRU, widgets, mapping, pub/sub, FSM, and testing options. Each replaces hand-rolled code that had no active value left to protect.

**R1 — `hashicorp/golang-lru/v2`**
\`internal/game/cache.go\` dropped \`container/list\` + \`sync.Mutex\` + hand-rolled eviction for a thin wrapper around the generic LRU. Public API identical. **100 → 58 lines**.

**R2 — `charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput`**
\`internal/ui/state.go\` dropped the hand-rolled \`textInput\` struct (8 methods) for \`textinput.Model\`. Non-Enter keys route through \`m.nameInput.Update(msg)\`; \`view.go\` uses \`View()\` directly. Gains cursor blink, word-jumps, paste, and every keybind bubbles ships.

**R3 — `google/go-cmp`**
\`internal/server/mapper_test.go\` proto assertions rewritten with \`cmp.Diff\` + \`protocmp.Transform\`. Failure output now reads \`(-want +got)\` instead of field-by-field \`GetX()/GetY()\` chains.

## Rejected (for the record)

- \`connectrpc/connect-go\` — better ergonomics than raw gRPC, but migration cost exceeds benefit until we add a second client type (web, mobile).
- \`asaskevich/EventBus\` / \`cskr/pubsub\` — reflection-based dispatch, trade compile safety for runtime panics; our typed Hub is strictly better.
- \`looplab/fsm\` / \`qmuntal/stateless\` — dependency overhead for a 3-state turn machine that is 40 lines of idiomatic Go.
- \`jmattheis/goverter\` — codegen setup cost exceeds maintenance burden at our ~200-line mapping layer.
- \`stretchr/testify\` — pulls yaml + difflib + spew + objx; stdlib \`testing\` + go-cmp covers every case.

- Adds `EAI_TENANT_ID` to the generated `.env.local` so the Vertical-Template's server-side tenant resolver (`page.tsx:12-15`, `api/eai/[[...rest]]/route.ts:20`) actually honors the binding — closes a pre-existing mismatch between the CLI's `TENANT_<KEY>_ID` scheme and the template's `EAI_TENANT_ID` fallback chain

## Behavior changes

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| "Tenant structure: single/dual/multi" | "Which platform tenant should this vertical bind to?" |
| Silent use of active tenant for Entra provisioning | Explicit tenant choice, Entra provisioning runs against *that* tenant |
| `TENANT_<KEY>_ID` only (template never read it) | `EAI_TENANT_ID` + `TENANT_<KEY>_ID` kept in sync |
| (no non-interactive tenant control) | `--tenant <id>` flag for scripted runs |

## Child-tenant branch: intentionally stubbed

The "Create a child tenant under the default" option is shown in the menu labeled `[not implemented]` and hard-fails on selection. The underlying `createTenant({ parent })` + `bootstrapChildTenantAdmin` sequence has a known live admin-assignment failure, so `init` refuses to leave a half-provisioned child tenant bound to a fresh vertical. The implementation sketch is left as a commented block in `promptTenantBinding` for when the backend path is stable. Use `eai tenant create --parent <id>` + `eai init --tenant <child-id>` in the interim.

## Q5/Q6/Q7 (AI chat / docs / auth provider)

Retained, relabeled `[not implemented]` / `[default, implemented]`. None of these toggles drive scaffold branching today — the labels make the placebo visible until someone wires them up.

author: iankressin
body:
## Summary
- On a normally-completing bounded stream, `PortalSource.stop()` ran **twice**: once at the tail of `read()`, and again from the outer `finally` in `pipeTo()` / `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` (which run `stop()` on every exit path). Non-idempotent user cleanup (`pg.end`, `sqlite.close`, `redis.quit`, `server.close`) would throw on the second call.
- **Root cause fix:** `read()`'s tail `stop()` is redundant because the callers own cleanup, so it's removed.
- **Safety net:** an idempotency guard remains in `stop()`, and the stream is now marked started *before* running start hooks so a partial start failure still cleans up via the outer `finally` (rather than being skipped by the guard).

### Review feedback addressed
- Dropped the unrelated transformer-ID de-duplication change.
- Fixed the partial-start-failure cleanup gap (cleanup was being skipped when a transformer `start` hook rejected) + added a regression test.

body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only git diff viewer to the GPUI desktop client plus agent-routed review comments. Users can browse diffs between any two refs/commits/working-tree in a project, toggle unified ↔ side-by-side view, see syntect-powered syntax highlighting, annotate individual lines with review comments, and ship a batch to an active agent session as a CSI-sanitised markdown prompt.

Implements RFC [`docs/rfc/rfc-git-diff-ui.md`](../blob/rfc-git-diff-ui/docs/rfc/rfc-git-diff-ui.md), phases P0–P5. P6 (keyboard shortcut `C`, stale-diff re-anchoring, ViewMode persistence) explicitly deferred.

## Highlights

- **Protocol** (`zremote-protocol`) — new `DiffFile`, `DiffSource`, `ReviewComment`, `ReviewCommentBatch` wire types with `#[serde(tag = "type")]` tagged enums + back-compat tests.
- **Agent** (`zremote-agent`) — git diff layer via `git diff -U3 --word-diff=none` shelling; unified diff parser (GNU-format); `/api/projects/:id/diff` and `/api/projects/:id/diff/sources` local endpoints; `/api/projects/:id/review/send` handler with batch/body size limits, cross-project session authorization, and C0+C1 control-byte sanitisation; rendered markdown prompt injected into an active PTY session.
- **Server** (`zremote-server`) — diff stream and review batch dispatch over existing agent WebSocket; NDJSON hunk streaming.
- **Client SDK** (`zremote-client`) — `stream_diff`, `get_diff_sources`, `send_review`.
- **GUI** (`zremote-gui`) — `DiffView` with source picker, file tree, diff pane, inline review composer, bottom drawer panel, command-palette action; `HighlightEngine` (syntect + in-code theme), cache keyed by `(content, syntax, side)`; `Alt+S` toggles view mode, `Esc` closes.

## Security

Independent security review was mandatory; all findings fixed before merge:

- **CWE-116**: C0+C1 control-byte (`0x00-0x1f`, `0x7f`, `0x80-0x9f`) stripping in `sanitize_body` blocks terminal-escape and 8-bit CSI/OSC hijacks.
- **CWE-862**: `post_send_review` verifies target session's `project_id` matches the URL's project; cross-project injection returns 403.
- **CWE-400**: per-batch cap (100 comments) + per-body cap (64 KiB) reject oversize payloads at the HTTP layer.
- **CWE-209**: rendered prompt removed from `SendReviewResponse` — no echo to logged channels.

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p zremote-gui --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p zremote-agent --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`

- [x] `cargo test -p zremote-gui --test review_pure` — 8 passed

- [x] `cargo test -p zremote-agent --lib local::routes::projects::diff` — 11 passed (incl. cross-project reject + size-limit)
- [x] `cargo test -p zremote-agent --test review_integration` — 2 passed (full PTY round-trip + end-to-end CSI/C1 strip)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --exclude zremote-gui` — 2541 passed, 0 failed
- [ ] Manual: launch standalone, open a project with git history, select Diff, toggle view modes, add review comments across files, dispatch to an active session, verify prompt renders in the target terminal.

```
cb035df refactor(gui): P4 review fixups — extract highlight cache + side pane
```

author: tocyuki
body:
## Summary

Replaces the `rdq ask` stub with a working one-shot CLI that turns a
natural-language prompt into SQL via Amazon Bedrock and runs it through
the same downstream pipeline `rdq exec` uses (read-only gate,
destructive confirmation, Data API, per-profile history, table / json /
csv rendering). Exit codes 0-5 match exec so CI pipelines can share
failure-handling logic.

Highlights:

- **Default is generate-and-execute** for CI / scripting. `--dry-run` /
  `-n` prints the bare SQL to stdout so `rdq ask -n ... | rdq exec --file -`
  is a clean pipe.
- **Generated SQL is echoed to stderr** (`-- Generated SQL:\n<sql>`) in
  execute mode so stdout stays a pure result stream. `--quiet` / `-q`
  suppresses the echo while keeping error messages and
  `(N rows affected)` visible on stderr.
- **Schema context is cached-only.** Blocking first-run ask on a 30s
  live `information_schema` fetch would hurt UX; the prompt template
  already handles a nil snapshot, and the cache is populated by
  `rdq tui`. When Bedrock cannot resolve the request it emits an
  SQL-comment block per the system prompt — detected up-front and
  surfaced as exit 1 instead of executing a comment-only payload.
- **Shared read-only gate.** `isReadOnlyProfile` is lifted from a method
  on `ExecCmd` to package scope so exec and ask agree on the policy
  stored in `state.json` (which the TUI `F8` toggle and the GUI
  Settings switch also write).
- **Fully unit-tested.** Every AWS boundary (Bedrock, Data API, schema
  cache, state) goes through unexported seams; 17 table-driven tests in
  `command/ask_test.go` cover every branch without hitting AWS. `make
  check` (fmt + vet + ` go test -race -count=1 ./...`) passes across
  all packages.

## Changes

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `command/ask.go` | Stub → full implementation. Adds `runAsk`, `setDefaultSeams`, `isAllSQLComments`, `defaultAskBedrock`. Flags: `--output/-o`, `--dry-run/-n`, `--quiet/-q`, `--yes/-y`. |
| `command/ask_test.go` | New. 17 table-driven tests covering happy path, JSON / CSV / table rendering, empty prompt, missing Bedrock model, all-comment reply, `--dry-run`, `--quiet` + errors-still-shown, read-only block, destructive confirmation (TTY + non-TTY), Bedrock / execute timeouts and errors, ephemeral-mode history skip, history recorded on success, plus a 9-case unit test on `isAllSQLComments`. |
| `command/exec.go` | Extracts `isReadOnlyProfile` from `(c *ExecCmd)` method to package-level function taking a state loader. No behavioural change for exec. |
| `README.md` | Adds an `### ask subcommand` section (usage, flag table, exit-code table, schema-cache guidance). Flips the implementation-status row to ✅ Implemented and rewords the overview so the stub-placeholder wording is gone. |

Deliberate non-goals for v1 (noted in the plan doc):

- Multi-turn chat (TUI keeps that role).
- Live schema fetch — revisit later with `--refresh-schema` if needed.
- No `--focus` / `--print-sql` / `--no-schema` flags; keep the surface
  small.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check` (fmt + vet + `go test -race -count=1 ./...`) — all
      packages pass, including 35 tests in `command/` (17 new ask + 18
      existing exec).
- [x] `./rdq ask --help` shows `-n/-o/-q/-y` with correct help text.
- [x] Dry-run smoke test against `studypocket-stg` returned a valid
      `SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata ORDER BY
      schema_name;` on stdout (exit 0) and no stderr output.
- [x] Execute-mode smoke test against the same cluster returned the
      table of 15 schemas on stdout with the generated SQL echoed to
      stderr; `-q` suppressed the echo while keeping the table output.
- [ ] Manual verification of the pipe workflow:
      `rdq ask -n "..." | rdq exec --file -`.
- [ ] Manual verification of the read-only block (exit 3) and the
      destructive confirmation flow (TTY + `-y` in a non-TTY shell).

## Notes / follow-ups

- Observed pre-existing: `(0 rows affected)` is printed to stderr for
  some SELECT queries because `runner.ConvertResult` sets `Updated = 0`
  instead of `-1`. Affects both exec and ask; out of scope here, worth
  a separate fix in `internal/runner/`.

author: productdevbook
body:
## Summary

Four correctness issues from audit round #15:

- **HIGH — MSSQL emitted `TRUE`/`FALSE`** (`src/printer/mssql.ts`): SQL Server has no boolean type — TRUE/FALSE are identifiers, not literals. Any `lit(true)` in a WHERE, CASE, or DEFAULT clause hit the base printer's literal path and produced SQL the driver rejected. Override `printLiteral` to emit `1`/`0`.
- **HIGH — AuditTimestampPlugin emitted `NOW()`** (`src/plugin/audit-timestamp.ts`): `NOW()` is not a function on SQL Server or SQLite. Every audited INSERT/UPDATE/MERGE on those dialects failed at runtime. Switched to `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (SQL:92 niladic keyword, portable across all four dialects).
- **MEDIUM — `parseTableRef` silently misparsed quoted identifiers** (`src/utils/table-ref.ts`): `parseTableRef('\"my.table\"')` split on the inner dot and produced `{ schema: '\"my', name: 'table\"' }`. Without dialect context the helper can't decide whether a dot is a literal or a separator — reject with a clear error.
- **MEDIUM — Constant folding broke SQL integer division** (`src/normalize/expression.ts`): `5 / 2` folded to `2.5` (JS float division). Every DB does `2` (integer division). `WHERE col = 5/2` silently changed row set. Refuse to fold `/` and `%` when both operands are integers.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm fmt && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — 1158 pass (+13 new)
- [x] Reproducers confirmed each bug pre-fix, verified fix post-patch
- [x] Existing `audit-timestamp` and `merge-combinations` tests updated to expect `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`
- [x] Regression test file: `test/audit15-regressions.test.ts`

body:
## Summary
Refactored the sources panel UI to separate VRS (Virtual Radar Server) networks into a collapsible details section when VRS sources are present, improving organization and reducing clutter.

## Key Changes
- **UI Reorganization**: Moved VRS sources into a collapsible `<details>` element that only appears when VRS networks are available
- **Styling**: Added CSS rules for the new VRS details section (`#vrs-det`, `#vrs-sum`) with custom disclosure triangle styling matching the existing Sources section
- **Data Separation**: Split source entries into physical and VRS-only categories, rendering them separately with a count badge for VRS networks
- **Popup Binding**: Simplified marker click handlers by replacing custom `openDetailPanel` calls with standard Leaflet `bindPopup()` methods:
  - Station circle markers now use `makePopupFn(s)`
  - Detail markers use `getCachedPopup(s)`
  - VRS hit markers use the popup directly
- **Event Handling**: Added click event handler to prevent the VRS global checkbox from toggling the parent `<details>` element open/closed

## Implementation Details
- The VRS section displays as a collapsible details element with a count badge (e.g., "VRS networks (3)") when VRS sources exist
- When no VRS sources are present, falls back to a simple checkbox label for backward compatibility
- Extracted `renderRow()` function to reduce code duplication between physical and VRS row rendering
- Maintained existing styling consistency with the Sources section using shared CSS patterns

author: bboe
body:
## Summary

`edit.c` open-coded the three-line gap-buffer cursor move idiom ten times across Ctrl+A / Ctrl+B / Ctrl+E / Ctrl+F / Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P:

```c
char c = buffer[gap_start - 1];
buffer[gap_end - 1] = c;
gap_start = gap_start - 1;
gap_end = gap_end - 1;
```

(plus the right-moving dual).  Lift `gap_start` / `gap_end` to file-scope globals — they're program-lifetime state — and collapse the copies behind two `regparm(1)` helpers that return the moved character.  `buffer_character_at` and `column_before` lose the `gap_start` / `gap_end` parameters (they read the globals directly).

Call sites shrink from 7-line open-coded blocks to either `gap_move_left();` (when the character isn't needed) or `if (gap_move_left() == '\n') { ... }` (when it is).

## Net

- `edit.c` loses 18 lines of source.
- Binary grows 10 bytes (2228 → 2238, +0.4%) — cc.py generates a small amount of function-call overhead that the inline form didn't have.  Fine trade for the readability.

## Scope

I also looked at `shell.c` / `dns.c` / `ping.c` for cross-program DRY:
- `shell.c` — the line-editor dispatch doesn't have obvious duplication.
- `dns.c` / `ping.c` share a `recvfrom` retry poll (3 sites, 7 lines each), but this codebase builds each program as its own binary, so a helper would have to live in a shared `.h` and get copied into both binaries — net binary growth, no size win. Skipped.

Other `edit.c` candidates (view-line clipping, save-loop byte copy) weren't big enough to justify the helper overhead given the +10-byte cost already seen.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 tests/test_asm.py` — passes (edit.c is userspace, doesn't affect the self-host)
- [x] `python3 tests/test_programs.py` — 27/27 pass
- [x] `python3 tests/test_cc.py` — 31/31 pass

body:
## Summary
레버리지 3건 중 2번 (`osty lint --fix` CLI) 착수. 기존 `--fix` / `--fix-dry-run`은 **단일 파일 경로에서만** 작동했고, `osty lint DIR`이나 workspace 모드에서는 플래그가 조용히 무시되고 있었음 — fixable 진단이 보여도 적용 수단이 없어서 사용자가 파일별로 호출하거나 손으로 고쳐야 했던 갭.

## 구현
`runLintLoadedPackage`가 진단 렌더링 직후 신규 `applyPackageFixes`를 호출:

- `diag.File` 기준으로 lint 진단을 파일별로 버킷팅 (stamp 누락 시 `pkg.Files[0].Path`로 fallback — 쓰기 대상 모호성 제거)
- 파일별 `f.Source`에 `lint.ApplyFixes` 실행
- `--fix` → 파일별 in-place rewrite
- `--fix-dry-run` → 각 변경 파일을 `// ==== path ====` 헤더 아래에 stdout으로 스트리밍. 파일별 diff 가능
- summary line 한 줄로 전체 집계 출력 (applied N, skipped M 또는 would apply N, would skip M)

Workspace 모드(`osty lint`의 dir-of-packages)는 `runLintWorkspace → runLintLoadedPackage`로 동일 경로를 타므로 트리 전체가 한 호출로 고쳐짐.

## 테스트 (cmd/osty/lint_fix_test.go, 4건)
- `TestLintFixSingleFileRewritesUnusedBinding` — 단일 파일 경로 회귀 방지
- `TestLintFixPackageModeRewritesEveryFile` — 2파일 패키지가 한 번에 모두 rewrite
- `TestLintFixDryRunLeavesFilesUnchanged` — dry-run이 디스크에 쓰지 않고 미리보기만
- `TestLintFixPackageDryRunHeadsEachFile` — 다중 파일 dry-run이 파일별 헤더 마커 포함

## Test plan
- [x] `just front` + `go test ./cmd/osty` — 전부 통과
- [x] 새로운 4개 테스트 모두 통과

author: mabry1985
body:
Closes #465.

## Motivation

PR #463 (the v0.7.22 dev→main promotion bundling 17 already-merged PRs) was auto-closed yesterday by `protoquinn[bot]` with this comment:

> **Auto-remediation verdict: decomposable** — closing and proposing a split.
>
> This PR has merge conflicts that cluster into distinct file groups. Rather than attempting a complex merge, the recommended path is to split this PR into smaller, focused PRs — one per file cluster.
>
> **Conflicting file clusters:**
> - `src/services/a2a/agentCard.ts`
> - `src/services/fleet-health/collector.ts`
> - `src/services/ceremonies/loader.ts`
> - `package.json`
>
> **Evidence:** This dev→main promotion PR bundles 3 independent concerns ... Splitting into separate PRs per feature area would isolate the conflicting files and allow each to merge independently.

That's a **structurally wrong policy for a promotion PR**. The work is already split across the 17 PRs being promoted; the conflicts are drift between dev and main, not need-to-decompose. Recovery is `rebasable` (back-merge), not split.

## Two-layer fix

### Layer A — `workspace/agents/ava.yaml` `diagnose_pr_stuck` prompt

Promotion-PR rule is now stated **first**, above the four verdict definitions, in positive framing per the no-negative-reinforcement memory:

> When the PR is a promotion — head branch is `dev` or `staging`, OR base branch is `main` or `staging`, OR title starts with `Promote` / `promote:` — the verdict is always `rebasable`. Drift between branches is fixed with a back-merge of the base into the head. Apply this even when conflicts cluster in a small number of files; splitting wouldn't reduce drift, because the conflict is between branches, not within the PR's commits.

The dispatch payload to Ava also gains a `Head branch:` line so she has the field to apply the rule to.

### Layer B — `lib/plugins/pr-remediator.ts` chokepoint guard

```ts
// before
case "decomposable": {
  // ... post comment, ghClosePr ...
}

// after
case "decomposable": {
  if (isPromotionPr(pr)) {
    console.warn(`PROMOTION GUARD: refusing decomposable verdict on protected PR ${prKey} ` +
                 `(head=${pr.headRef} base=${pr.baseRef} title="${pr.title}"). ` +
                 `Promotion conflicts indicate drift, not need-to-decompose. Escalating to HITL.`);
    this._emitStuckHitlEscalation(pr.repo, pr.number, "update_branch", entry, evidence);
    break;
  }
  // ... existing post comment, ghClosePr ...
}
```

`isPromotionPr()` returns true when `headRef ∈ {dev, staging}` OR `baseRef ∈ {main, staging}` OR title starts `promote:` / `promote `. `PrDomainEntry` gains an optional `headRef` field; `src/api/github.ts` surfaces `pr.head.ref` in the `pr_pipeline` domain so the guard can see it.

This is the same defense-in-depth shape as #437 (cooldown), #444 (target registry), and #459 (synthetic actor filter): invariants belong at the action-site chokepoint, not at the planner. A drifting prompt cannot close a release-pipeline PR.

## Tests

`src/pr-remediator.test.ts` adds 4 new cases inside the `diagnose_pr_stuck` describe block:

- (a) decomposable verdict on a refactor PR (head=`feature/x`, base=`dev`) → still closes (no HITL)
- (b) decomposable verdict on dev→main promotion PR → does NOT close, escalates to HITL with `Promotion-PR guard` reason in the summary
- (c) decomposable verdict on staging→main promotion PR → escalates to HITL
- (d) decomposable verdict on dev→staging promotion PR → escalates to HITL

Full suite: **1047/1047 pass**.

## Verification plan

- [ ] Open a synthetic conflict-bearing dev→main PR (e.g. add a debug commit on main touching a file dev also changed).
- [ ] Wait for `pr-remediator` to dispatch `diagnose_pr_stuck` after 2 update-branch 422s.
- [ ] Expect: `PROMOTION GUARD` warn line in logs, HITL request emitted, **PR remains OPEN**.
- [ ] `gh pr view <id> --json closedBy --jq .closedBy.login` should never be `protoquinn[bot]` for any PR with `base: main`.

author: o6lvl4
body:
## Summary
Aggregates all compiler + runtime work that was staged on the fix branch to make `bonsai-almide` run end-to-end — both native and WASM. Previously unmerged into `develop`.

## What's in here

Compiler / codegen:
- **Recursive import resolution** (`b9c9271`) — transitively-imported bundled stdlib (fs, process, …) now reach `resolved.modules` so their `type_decls` emit. Unblocked FileStat etc. in external packages.
- **LICM nested-loop recursion + unique names** (`28d53c3`) — `try_hoist_expr` now recurses into `ForIn`/`While` bodies and uses `__licm_N` to avoid shadowing. A 248 MB `Bytes` read inside a doubly-nested Q1_0 decode hoisted: 7+ min → 4 s.
- **`int.bits_to_f32` intrinsic** (`5d55902`) — u32 → f32 bit reinterpretation. The existing `bits_to_float` is a u64 intrinsic and silently converted f32 tensor bytes into subnormal `~1e-85` noise (GGUF F32 load produced output == input in bonsai blk.0 until this landed).
- **Codegen + primitive wins** (`312190a`) — range-iter without `Vec` collect, `list.with_capacity`, `matrix.from_q1_0_bytes`, `#[inline(always)]` on hot runtime helpers. Q1_0 decode 4 s → 35 ms (120x).

WASM emitter:
- **i64 memory-grow check** (`3db5bac`) — `__alloc` can now grow past 2 GB. Bonsai's 2.48 GB decoded `token_embd` fits inside the 4 GB cap.
- **Dispatch for `int.bits_to_f32` + `list.with_capacity`** (`8958d1f`).
- **Q1_0 direct-matmul primitives** (`2e0404b`, `857df92`) — `matrix.linear_q1_0_row_no_bias`, `matrix.silu_mul`, `matrix.select_rows`, `matrix.select_rows_q1_0`. Keeps weights packed (5 MB/layer vs 400 MB decoded), which is what lets the full 28-layer forward fit in WASM.

Runtime tweak (this PR):
- **Relax `matrix.select_rows{,_q1_0}` to `&[i64]`** (`5ff28fb`) — rust codegen passes `List[Int]` fn-args as `&[i64]` slices, so `&Vec<i64>` receivers failed compile on any native call-site.

## Why now
`bonsai-almide` just shipped an end-to-end Q1_0 forward (token 26194 ≈ " Tokyo" for "The capital of Japan is") on both native and browser WASM; all of the above are load-bearing for that to work. Keeping them on a side branch was creating drift (see: the signature bug was only discovered when we tried to land a native tok/s benchmark today).

## Test plan
- [ ] `almide test` green
- [ ] `cargo test` green
- [ ] `bonsai-almide` native bench still runs (pp5 ≈ 18.5 s, tg ≈ 24 s/tok; not fast, just correct)
- [ ] `bonsai-almide` WASM bench still runs (pp5 ≈ 8.3 s, tg ≈ 11 s/tok)

### 💡 What:
Improved the accessibility and visual feedback of the next departure prediction display.

### 🎯 Why:
The original design used color alone to distinguish between live and scheduled data, which is inaccessible to many users. Additionally, the original colors failed WCAG AA contrast requirements when paired with white text.

### 📸 Before/After:
- **Before**: Light blue (#3498db) or green (#27ae60) backgrounds with low contrast. No screen reader context for data source.
- **After**: High-contrast blue (#1565c0) and green (#1b5e20) backgrounds. Smooth transition between states. Screen readers now announce updates and the data source (Live vs. Scheduled).

### ♿ Accessibility:
- Background colors now meet WCAG AA contrast standards (>= 4.5:1).
- Added `aria-live="polite"` to the prediction container.
- Added a `.sr-only` span to provide textual context for the data source.

author: jasonhui1
body:
### 💡 What
Added `aria-label` attributes to all icon-only buttons in the Composer sidebars and toolbars. Added `aria-hidden="true"` to decorative SVGs within these buttons, and added `focus-visible` outline classes and `aria-expanded` state properties to sidebar toggle buttons. Also logged critical accessibility learnings in `.Jules/palette.md`.

### 🎯 Why
Screen readers cannot reliably interpret icon-only buttons without `aria-label`s, rendering parts of the interface (like Undo/Redo or toggling sidebars) completely inaccessible to visually impaired users. Furthermore, decorative SVGs without `aria-hidden="true"` can cause screen readers to announce unnecessary elements. This micro-enhancement ensures these controls are both reachable via keyboard and properly announced by assistive technologies.

### 📸 Before/After
* **Before**: Icon-only buttons lacked descriptions (relying only on `title`) and keyboard focus outlines. Screen readers would struggle to convey their purpose.
* **After**: Icon-only buttons are explicitly labeled via `aria-label`. SVGs are hidden from screen readers. Keyboard users receive clear visual focus states on sidebar toggles.

### ♿ Accessibility
* **Added `aria-label`** to Undo, Redo, Delete Canvas, and Left/Right Sidebar toggle buttons.
* **Added `aria-hidden="true"`** to SVGs inside all modified toolbar buttons.
* **Added `aria-expanded`** to sidebar toggle buttons to communicate their state to screen readers.
* **Added `focus-visible` rings** to sidebar toggle buttons for clearer keyboard navigation.

---

author: ajsutton
body:
## Summary

- `just install-mac` produced a Release binary that died silently at launch.
- Root cause: `project.yml` bakes `CLOUDKIT_ENABLED` into Release unconditionally (commit `f72d9fd`), but `scripts/inject-entitlements.sh` only added the matching `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` line to the `Debug:` block. The signed Release app therefore called `CKContainer.default()` on startup without the iCloud capability, and the hardened runtime killed it with an uncatchable `NSException` before any UI rendered. `just run-mac` (Debug) was unaffected because Debug only gets `CLOUDKIT_ENABLED` when entitlements are also injected — flag and capability stay aligned.
- `scripts/inject-entitlements.sh` now also prepends `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` to each target's existing `Release:` config block in place, so there's no duplicate YAML key against the block that already carries `ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME` / `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS`.
- `install-mac` now forces `ENABLE_ENTITLEMENTS=1` for its `just generate` step so the fix applies regardless of the dev's local `.env`.

## Test plan

- [x] `just install-mac` builds & installs without errors
- [x] `codesign -d --entitlements :- /Applications/Moolah.app` shows `com.apple.developer.icloud-container-identifiers` = `iCloud.rocks.moolah.app.v2` and `CloudKit` service
- [x] Installed app launches and stays running (was dying silently before)
- [x] `just format-check` clean
- [ ] `just test` on CI (unchanged — inject script still leaves `Debug-Tests` entitlements-free)

author: leopechnicki
body:
## Security Audit — Crew Leo Agile Dev Team

Full pentest of the mempalace codebase. Found and fixed **8 issues** across 3 files.

---

### Findings & Fixes

#### `mempalace/mcp_server.py` — 6 fixes

| # | Severity | Finding | Fix |
|---|----------|---------|-----|
| 1 | Medium | `tool_search` `limit` parameter had no upper bound — a caller could request unlimited results and exhaust memory (DoS) | Capped at `_SEARCH_LIMIT_MAX = 100` |
| 2 | Low | `tool_kg_query` `direction` parameter passed directly to SQLite query builder without validation — unexpected values silently fall through | Added allowlist check against `{"outgoing", "incoming", "both"}` |
| 3 | Low | `tool_diary_write` `topic` parameter stored in metadata without sanitization — inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which sanitizes all user-controlled metadata | Now runs through `sanitize_name()` |
| 4 | Low | `tool_diary_read` `last_n` had no upper bound — could load thousands of entries into memory | Capped at `_DIARY_READ_MAX = 200` |
| 5 | Low | `tool_add_drawer` `source_file` metadata field accepted arbitrary strings including null bytes and unlimited length | Strip null bytes, truncate to 500 chars |
| 6 | Medium | MCP server main loop swallowed JSON parse errors silently — MCP clients expect a well-formed JSON-RPC `-32700` response to recover; without it the protocol stream desynchronizes | Added inner `try/except json.JSONDecodeError` that returns a proper JSON-RPC parse error |

#### `mempalace/hooks_cli.py` — 1 fix

| # | Severity | Finding | Fix |
|---|----------|---------|-----|
| 7 | Low | `MEMPAL_DIR` env var used directly as a path in `subprocess.Popen`/`subprocess.run` without resolving symlinks — a symlink pointing to a sensitive directory (e.g. `/etc`) would cause mempalace to index it | Resolve via `os.path.realpath()` before use in both async and sync ingest paths |

#### `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — 1 fix

| # | Severity | Finding | Fix |
|---|----------|---------|-----|
| 8 | Medium | `actions/checkout@v6` and `actions/setup-python@v6` reference versions that **do not exist**. If GitHub ever publishes v6 tags (or they're taken over), the CI pipeline would execute attacker-controlled code (supply-chain attack surface). Current stable versions are v4 and v5 respectively. | Updated all 4 jobs to use `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-python@v5` |

---

### What was NOT found
- No hardcoded secrets or API keys
- No SQL injection risks (all queries use parameterized statements)
- No `eval()` or `exec()` on user input
- No path traversal in file-writing operations (sanitize_name already blocks `..`, `/`, `\`)
- No insecure deserialization

---

### Testing
All changes are backward-compatible — no API surface changes, only input validation added. Existing test suite should pass without modification.

---

## Summary

- Public client methods now take **inline kwargs** instead of Pydantic `*Request` objects — matches the JS SDK and standard Python SDK ergonomics (OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe).
- `*Request` classes remain exported for users who want to build payloads manually, but client methods no longer accept them.
- Structured types (`FetchConfig`, format configs, `schema` dicts) are still passed as-is.

## Before / After

```python
# Before
sgai.scrape(ScrapeRequest(url="https://example.com", formats=[MarkdownFormatConfig()]))

# After
sgai.scrape("https://example.com", formats=[MarkdownFormatConfig()])
```

- `ScrapeGraphAI` / `AsyncScrapeGraphAI`: `scrape`, `extract`, `search`

## Resampling stutter

Fixes audio stuttering on players that require resampling (e.g. 44.1kHz/16-bit clients). The drift detection in the standalone resampler was firing on every call with the soxr resampler, rebuilding the graph every time and dropping a significant portion of audio on any resampling target.

- Fix timestamp drift after extended playback (https://github.com/Sendspin/aiosendspin/pull/217)

Adds host-scoped scheduling for background monitoring jobs in the Open Library monitoring subsystem. Introduces a selective registration mechanism, an asyncio-capable scheduler, and a new HAProxy metrics collector that ships session counts, rates, and queue lengths to Graphite via the pickle protocol on port 2004.

## Key Achievements

- **`OlAsyncIOScheduler`** (new) — parallel async scheduler to `OlBlockingScheduler`; inherits from `apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio.AsyncIOScheduler`; shares UTC timezone, `[OL-MONITOR]`-tagged listener, and `id = func.__name__` defaulting.
- **`limit_server(allowed_hosts, scheduler)`** — broadened to accept any `BaseScheduler`; retains environment-driven hostname resolution (`os.environ.get("HOSTNAME")`) and three matching modes (exact, prefix-wildcard, short-to-FQDN).
- **`get_service_ip(image_name)`** — bounded-timeout Docker container IP resolver via `docker inspect`, with registry-prefix and `:tag` normalization.
- **`haproxy_monitor.py`** (new, 399 LOC) — `GraphiteEvent` dataclass, `HaproxyCapture` regex filter, `fetch_events()`, async `main()` dual-frequency loop with four aggregation modes (max/min/sum/None), at-least-once delivery on Graphite outages, bounded socket/HTTP timeouts.
- **`monitor_haproxy()` coroutine** — 60-second interval job host-scoped to `ol-www0`; resolves `web_haproxy` IP then awaits `haproxy_main()` with production settings.
- **Async `main()` entrypoint** — graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM handling via `loop.add_signal_handler`, prevents `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` on shutdown.

## Validation

- **Tests**: 19/19 monitoring tests passing; full regression 2736 passed / 9 skipped / 3 xfailed (zero regressions).
- **Coverage**: monitoring subsystem 90% combined (utils.py 100%, haproxy_monitor.py 84%).
- **Lint**: `ruff check` — all checks passed; `black --check` — all files unchanged; `mypy` — no issues in 6 source files.
- **Runtime**: Verified on all 5 production host profiles (`ol-web0`, `ol-web1`, `ol-web2`, `ol-covers0`, `ol-www0`); host-scoping produces correct job counts (1, 1, 0, 4, 4 respectively); SIGTERM exits cleanly with code 0.
- **Security**: Proactively remediated CVE-2025-43859 (h11 request smuggling, CVSS 9.1) by bumping `httpx` to 0.28.1 with floor pins on `h11>=0.16.0` and `httpcore>=1.0.9` in `scripts/monitoring/requirements.txt`.

## Files Changed

- `scripts/monitoring/utils.py` (UPDATED, +101/-4) — Added `OlAsyncIOScheduler`, `get_service_ip`, broadened `limit_server` type; added `[OL-MONITOR]` prefix to `job_listener`.
- `scripts/monitoring/monitor.py` (UPDATED, +101/-12) — Migrated to `OlAsyncIOScheduler`, added `monitor_haproxy` job, async `main()` with signal handlers.
- `scripts/monitoring/haproxy_monitor.py` (CREATED, +399) — Full async HAProxy metrics pipeline.
- `scripts/monitoring/requirements.txt` (UPDATED, +10/-0) — Added httpx with CVE-safe h11 floor pins.
- `scripts/monitoring/tests/test_utils_py.py` (UPDATED, +206/-2) — 6 new tests for async scheduler, get_service_ip, job_listener prefix.
- `scripts/monitoring/tests/test_haproxy_monitor.py` (CREATED, +370) — 8 new tests with 84% module coverage.

## Remaining Pre-Production Work

None blocking. Three path-to-production items (total 7h) remain for human operators: staging smoke deploy, Graphite dashboard config for the new `stats.ol.haproxy.*` namespace, and production image rebuild + rollout coordination. All AAP-scoped feature work is complete.

## Problem When sorting tasks by Priority, the order was High → Low → Medium (alphabetical) instead of the expected High → Medium → Low or Low → Medium → High. ## Root Cause `frappe.get_list` sorts the `priority` field alphabetically by default. Frappe's query builder does not allow raw SQL expressions like `FIELD()` in `order_by`, so the sort cannot be overridden at the database level. ## Fix When `order_by` contains `priority`, fetch data normally and re-sort in Python using a logical priority order map `{High: 0, Medium: 1, Low: 2}`. ## Testing Tasks sorted by Priority asc: Low → Medium → High ✅ Tasks sorted by Priority desc: High → Medium → Low ✅ Fixes #1882

author: c-sinclair
body:
## Summary

Removes `inherits` from the scope DSL and enables a do-block form for setting `description` (and any future scope option):

```elixir
scope :my_scope_name, expr(...) do
  description "This is important"
end
```

**Breaking change**: `inherits` is gone. The old positional form (`scope :own_draft, [:own], expr(status == :draft)`) and the keyword form (`scope :name, expr(...), inherits: [:parent]`) no longer compile. Write each scope as one expression:

```elixir
# Before
scope :own, expr(author_id == ^actor(:id))
scope :own_draft, [:own], expr(status == :draft)

# After
scope :own, expr(author_id == ^actor(:id))
scope :own_draft, expr(author_id == ^actor(:id) and status == :draft)
```

Why: scope inheritance added hidden coupling (child behaviour depended on parent filters that might live in a different module), interacted awkwardly with `write:` and argument-based scopes, and — because `inherits` was an optional positional arg — blocked `scope` from supporting Spark do-blocks at all. Inlining with `and` is mechanically trivial, reads plainly, and shows up straight in `AshGrant.explain/4`.

Domain-level scope merging is unchanged — a resource still sees scopes defined on its domain. Only scope-to-scope inheritance is removed.

### Net change

Net −191 LoC across lib/. Info's `resolve_scope_filter/3` is now a direct lookup; `AddArgumentResolvers` lost the recursive DSL-state walker.

### Docs

- `usage-rules.md`: scope entity section updated, inheritance rule replaced with "combine inline" DO.
- `README.md`, `guides/scopes.md`, `guides/authorization-patterns.md`, `guides/scope-naming-convention.md`, `guides/getting-started.md`, `guides/advanced-patterns.md`: removed inheritance references, updated examples.
- `guides/migration.md`: new section explaining the removal and migration path.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased): breaking change + added do-block form.

## Test plan

- [x] `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean
- [x] `mix test` — 1045 tests pass (1 pre-existing failure in `default_field_policies_test.exs`, unrelated)
- [x] `mix format --check-formatted` clean
- [x] `mix credo` — only pre-existing non-blocking suggestions
- [x] Test resources and guide examples all compile after inlining combined filters
- [x] Do-block form verified via new tests in `test/ash_grant/scope_dsl_test.exs`

Nettoyage demandé après la livraison strate 0 — suppression de wrappers obsolètes et réécriture des README pour qu'ils reflètent l'état réel du framework.

```

ca38bcc chore(packages): supprime wrappers obsoletes @bonsai/zod et @bonsai/remeda
```

## 📦 Phase 1 + 2 — Suppression wrappers

### `@bonsai/zod`
Wrapper supprimé. Zod a été remplacé par Valibot (cf. [ADR-0022](docs/adr/ADR-0022-entity-schema-validation.md)) et le wrapper n'avait plus aucun consommateur dans le framework — re-export passthrough mort depuis l'introduction de `@bonsai/valibot`.

Wrapper supprimé. `remeda` n'est utilisé que par `tools/` (build-bonsai-package, pug-to-ts-template), jamais par le framework Bonsai. Les tools importent directement `from "remeda"` (devDependency racine), sans passer par le wrapper. Cf. [ADR-0031](docs/adr/ADR-0031-monorepo-package-topology.md) C3 (hors API publique Bonsai).
