### Update [Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django) from **5.1.1** to **6.0.4**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.4
   ```
   ==========================

*April 7, 2026*

Django 6.0.4 fixes one security issue with severity "moderate", four security
issues with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.3.

CVE-2026-3902: ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation
====================================================================

``ASGIRequest`` normalizes header names following WSGI conventions, mapping
hyphens to underscores. As a result, even in configurations where reverse
proxies carefully strip security-sensitive headers named with hyphens, such a
header could be spoofed by supplying a header named with underscores.

Under WSGI, it is the responsibility of the server or proxy to avoid ambiguous
mappings. (Django's :djadmin:`runserver` was patched in :cve:`2015-0219`.) But
under ASGI, there is not the same uniform expectation, even if many proxies
protect against this under default configuration (including ``nginx`` via
``underscores_in_headers off;``).

Headers containing underscores are now ignored by ``ASGIRequest``, matching the
behavior of :pypi:`Daphne <daphne>`, the reference server for ASGI.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4277: Privilege abuse in ``GenericInlineModelAdmin``
=============================================================

Add permissions on inline model instances were not validated on submission of
forged ``POST`` data in
:class:`~django.contrib.contenttypes.admin.GenericInlineModelAdmin`.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4292: Privilege abuse in ``ModelAdmin.list_editable``
==============================================================

Admin changelist forms using
:attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.list_editable` incorrectly allowed new
instances to be created via forged ``POST`` data.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33033: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``MultiPartParser`` via base64-encoded file upload
===============================================================================================================

When using ``django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser``, multipart uploads
with ``Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`` that include excessive whitespace
may trigger repeated memory copying, potentially degrading performance.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33034: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ASGI requests via memory upload limit bypass
=========================================================================================================

ASGI requests with a missing or understated ``Content-Length`` header could
bypass the :setting:`DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` limit when reading
``HttpRequest.body``, potentially loading an unbounded request body into
memory and causing service degradation.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 where :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogin`
  and :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogout` did not respectively set or clear
  ``request.user`` if it had already been materialized (e.g., by sync
  middleware) (:ticket:`37017`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 in admin forms where
  ``RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper`` incorrectly wrapped all widgets in a
  ``<fieldset>`` (:ticket:`36949`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 6.0 where the ``fields.E348`` system check did not
  detect name clashes between model managers and
  :attr:`~django.db.models.ForeignKey.related_name`\s for non-self-referential
  relationships (:ticket:`36973`).

body:
`BuildWritableContact` filtered phones with exact label checks for `work`, `home`, and `mobile` only — every other label (`other`, `main`, `workFax`, `pager`, etc.) was silently dropped on the way to Microsoft Graph.

## Changes

- **`PhoneNumberMapper.cs`** (new) — internal static class encapsulating the bidirectional label ↔ Microsoft Graph field mapping:
  - `other` → `homePhones` (closest personal-number field)
  - all other unrecognised labels → `businessPhones` (fallback; value preserved, label may change on round-trip)
  - `FromMicrosoftField` for the read direction (used for consistency/testability)

- **`MicrosoftContactsConnector.BuildWritableContact`** — replaced hard-coded `OrdinalIgnoreCase` label comparisons with `PhoneNumberMapper.ToMicrosoftField()`:

  ```csharp
  // Before: phones with unrecognised labels were simply omitted
  ["homePhones"] = CreateStringArray(contact.Phones
      .Where(phone => string.Equals(phone.Label, "home", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
      .Select(phone => phone.Number)),

  // After: "other" (and any other label) is routed to the closest available field
  ["homePhones"] = CreateStringArray(contact.Phones
      .Where(phone => PhoneNumberMapper.ToMicrosoftField(phone.Label) == PhoneNumberMapper.HomePhones)
      .Select(phone => phone.Number)),
  ```

- **`PhoneNumberMapperTests.cs`** (new, 31 tests) — covers the `other` case, additional unrecognised labels (`main`, `workFax`, `homeFax`, `pager`, `workMobile`, `googleVoice`), case-insensitivity, null/empty labels, and round-trip semantics.

author: oenzoribas
body:
# Refatoração do componente Carousel

## 💡 Contexto
Este PR refatora o componente `Carousel` para alinhá-lo aos padrões de Clean Code, Separation of Concerns e acessibilidade do projeto.

A implementação inicial possuía gargalos de renderização, acoplamento forte de dados e uso inadequado do ciclo de vida do React com GSAP.

Abaixo estão os problemas resolvidos e as abstrações implementadas.

## 🐛 Correções críticas (bugs e anti-patterns)

- **Falha silenciosa no GSAP corrigida**: o código tentava animar propriedades inexistentes em um `NodeList` (`gsap.fromTo(imagens.alt, ...)`).  
    Agora, o React gerencia estado e atualizações de DOM (`src` das imagens), enquanto o GSAP anima apenas os wrappers (`.slide-img`) na montagem.

- **Uso semântico de hooks**: validação e pré-carregamento das imagens foram movidos de `useGSAP` para `useEffect`.  
    O `useGSAP` passou a gerenciar somente o ciclo de vida das animações, evitando memory leaks e comportamentos inesperados.

- **Desbloqueio de navegação global**: o `e.preventDefault()` em `lidarComTeclado` estava no topo do escopo e bloqueava eventos nativos (como `Tab`).  
    O bloqueio agora ocorre apenas nas condições de `ArrowLeft` e `ArrowRight`.

## 🏗️ Arquitetura e reusabilidade

- **Desacoplamento de dados (dumb component)**: remoção do hardcode de imagens (`imagensOriginais`) dentro do componente.  
    O `Carousel` agora recebe dados por props e se torna reutilizável em toda a aplicação.

- **Estrutura de dados robusta**: a prop de imagens deixou de aceitar `string[]` (URLs) e passou a aceitar `CarouselImage[]`, com `src` e `alt` obrigatórios.

- **Limpeza de estilos inline**: estilos recriados a cada render foram removidos e migrados para uma estrutura de dicionário CSS.

## ♿ Acessibilidade (a11y)

- **Atributos dinâmicos e semânticos**: substituição de `alt="atual"` por descrições reais vindas da estrutura de dados, melhorando SEO e leitores de tela.

- **Gerenciamento de foco**: garantia de foco adequado para navegação por teclado, com controle contido no track visual.

## 🚀 O que foi construído e melhorado

- **Arquitetura headless com custom hook**: regras de negócio (validação de rede, controle de índices, lógica circular e autoplay) foram extraídas para `useCarousel`.

- **Type safety em modo estrito**: tipagem completa com TypeScript e uso de type predicates na filtragem de imagens.

- **Simetria visual com aspect ratio**: inclusão de bounding boxes com `aspect-ratio` fixo e `object-fit: cover` para evitar quebras com imagens de dimensões variadas.

- **Animação premium**: troca do scale básico por slide-fade com `power2.inOut`, profundidade espacial e blur lateral via GSAP.

- **Suíte de testes (100% de cobertura)**:
    - renderização inicial de loading;
    - renderização condicional de empty states;
    - mocks de carregamento estrito com `new Image()`;
    - interação por mouse e navegação por teclado;
    - avanço de tempo com fake timers para `autoPlay`.
    
## O que não foi feito (escopo futuro)

- **Lazy loading e otimização de performance**: embora o pré-carregamento seja implementado, a implementação de lazy loading para imagens fora da viewport ainda é um passo futuro.

- **Suporte a múltiplos carousels**: o componente foi refatorado para ser reutilizável, mas testes e ajustes para múltiplas instâncias na mesma página ainda são necessários.

- **Personalização de animações**: atualmente, a animação é fixa. Permitir personalização via props (tipo de animação, duração, etc.) é um aprimoramento planejado.

author: thadcraft-shopify
body:
A worker whose queue has neither `@index` nor `entry_resolver` set was yielding `UnresolvedEntry` (a `Struct.new(:id, :queue_entry)` with no `.run`) from `Worker#poll`. The Minitest adapter called `example.run` on it, raised `NoMethodError`, `rescue_run_errors` caught it, and the worker exited with code 42. The report step then saw `worker_errors` non-empty and failed the build — cascading into ~150 downstream broken jobs even though 597k tests passed.

Repro: world-shopify-selective-tests #936469, summary job `019dae91-8271-4b54-a31d-2ed49491de24` (ci-queue 0.90.0).

How a worker reaches this state: `runner.rb#run_command`'s `retry? && remaining <= running` "Queue almost empty, exiting early..." branch skips `prepare_queue_for_execution` but falls through to `Minitest.run []`, which invokes `queue.poll` on a queue that was never populated or configured with a resolver. `reserve` can still pick up a lost test (via `reserve_lost`) and return an entry that `resolve_entry` has no way to turn into a runnable.

## Fix

Primary, in `Worker#poll`: when `resolve_entry` returns an `UnresolvedEntry`, acknowledge the entry and `next` instead of yielding it. The test is released so another worker (or the heartbeat reclaimer) can handle it.

Defense in depth, in the Minitest and RSpec adapters: `next unless example.respond_to?(:run)` inside the `queue.poll` block — an unexpected queue state should never crash a worker.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test `test_poll_skips_unresolved_entries_without_crashing` pushes a raw entry onto a worker with no `@index` and no `entry_resolver`, polls, and asserts nothing is yielded and the queue exhausts. Without the `poll` fix this test hangs (entry yielded but never acknowledged → `exhausted?` never true).
- [x] Existing `resolve_entry` and retry-with-entry-resolver tests still pass.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

- `BuildStatusReporter#success?` should not treat a single `worker_errors` entry as build-failing when `error_reports.empty? && queue_exhausted? && !timed_out?` — surface as a warning instead.
- Optional: `runner.rb`'s "Queue almost empty" branch could `exit!(0)` instead of falling through to `Minitest.run []`. The poll-level fix makes this harmless, but it's the cleaner root-level exit.

author: thebtf
body:
## Summary

Two additive fixes. Closes engram #157.

### 1. engine.Config.StdinEOFPolicy passthrough

Engine consumers call `engine.New(Config{...})` — they don't construct `ResilientClientConfig` directly. The engine's `runClient` now propagates `StdinEOFPolicy` from Config to `RunResilientClient`.

**Aimux adoption:**
```go
e, _ := engine.New(engine.Config{
    Name:           "aimux",
    StdinEOFPolicy: owner.StdinEOFWaitForDisconnect,
    // ...
})
```

### 2. upgrade: sameFile identity guard

`go build -o mcp-mux.exe` silently fails when the daemon holds a file lock. The staged binary (`mcp-mux.exe~`) ends up identical to the running one. `upgrade --restart` then swaps the same binary — no-op upgrade that appears successful.

Fix: SHA-256 comparison of staged vs current binary before swap. If identical, exit with diagnostic message explaining the cause and correct workflow.

### Files changed

- `muxcore/engine/engine.go` — `StdinEOFPolicy` field + passthrough (+6 lines)
- `cmd/mcp-mux/main.go` — `sameFile` + `fileHash` helpers + guard in `runUpgrade` (+45 lines)

### Tests

Full muxcore suite: 20/20 PASS. Engine tests: 18/18 PASS.

    val jsonText = AppJson.encodeToString(DummyDto(firstName = "a", lastName = "b"))
    assertEquals("""{"first_name":"a","last_name":"b"}""", jsonText)
}
```

テストランナー出力 (コンパイルエラーではなく期待通りのアサーション失敗):

```
SerializationSnakeCaseTest > serializer converts camelCase kotlin fields to snake_case JSON keys FAILED
    org.junit.ComparisonFailure at SerializationSnakeCaseTest.kt:20
1 test completed, 1 failed
BUILD FAILED in 1s
```

### Green (最小実装)

`Serialization.kt` で以下を実施:

1. テスタビリティのため、Json builder を top-level `val AppJson` に抽出 (Application 全体を起動しなくてもテストから直接利用可能に)。
2. builder に `namingStrategy = JsonNamingStrategy.SnakeCase` を 1 行追加。
3. 他の設定 (`encodeDefaults = true`, `isLenient = true` 等) は変更しない。

実行結果:

```
SerializationSnakeCaseTest > serializer converts camelCase kotlin fields to snake_case JSON keys PASSED
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1s
```

### Refactor

- `./gradlew spotlessApply` 実施 (R5)。
- `@OptIn(ExperimentalSerializationApi::class)` を付与 — `JsonNamingStrategy.SnakeCase` が要求するため、kotlin-style ルール (8) 「`@OptIn` は使用 API が要求する場合のみ」に準拠。
- import は明示 (wildcard なし、`.editorconfig` + ktlint 準拠)。
- 旧 mock-server-base 由来の残骸コメント (`isBeginner` / `isPrimePass` 参照) を別コミットで削除。

## 同時更新したテスト (回帰修正)

Admin API の既存テストは POST body に camelCase キーを送っていた (`ScenarioOverride` / `ScenarioTransitionChain` に deserialize)。SnakeCase 有効化によりワイヤ形式を snake_case に揃える必要があるため同時修正:

- `ScenarioConfigTest` / `ScenarioExecutionTest`: `delayMs` → `delay_ms`、`statusCode` → `status_code` (POST body)
- `AdminTransitionRoutesTest`: レスポンス JSON の `currentIndex` → `current_index`

Kotlin フィールド識別子 (camelCase) は維持。JSON ワイヤ形式のみ変更。`test-conventions.md` の fixture-test 同時更新ルールに従い同一コミットに含める。

## `encodeDefaults = true` の取り扱い (調査済・保持確定)

PR レビュー中に `encodeDefaults = true` の削除可否を調査した。結論: **削除不可、保持する**。

一次証拠 (資料1 `linked-bubbling-sun.md`):

- **L99-L102 空配列・null ポリシー**: 「リスト型は null を使わず `List<T> = emptyList()` に統一。`encodeDefaults = true` により空配列は JSON 上 `[]` として出力される」
- **L176 レスポンス形式**: 「既存 Serialization.kt が `encodeDefaults = true` / `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` で設定済。`List<T> = emptyList()` は JSON 上 `[]`、`T? = null` は JSON 上 `null` として出力される」
- L28 / L242: 型規約の根拠として `encodeDefaults = true` の既存設定を明示参照

削除した場合の Flutter / iOS / Android 動作確認時の不都合:
- default 値を持つ List フィールド (例: `Drug.contraindications = emptyList()`) が JSON から消える
- Flutter freezed 非 nullable List フィールド → parse error
- Swift Codable 非 Optional Array → `keyNotFound` throw
- 現行 `AdminTransitionRoutesTest` も `current_index: 0` の露出に依存

```
./gradlew spotlessCheck detektMain test
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 4s
```

- 既存の `SampleResponse(id, message)` 系テストは回帰なし (1 単語フィールドのため snake_case 変換の影響を受けない)。
- 列挙型に付いた `@SerialName` (Phase 2 以降で定義) は kotlinx.serialization 仕様により `NamingStrategy` より優先される。

## Summary

body:
Another slice of [#654](https://github.com/pggLLC/Housing-Analytics/issues/654) (expand unit + smoke test coverage for Phase 3 modules). Same shape as [#660](https://github.com/pggLLC/Housing-Analytics/pull/660)'s pma-competitive-set coverage — pure-function tests, no DOM, adds to the `test:ci` chain.

## What this locks in

`js/lihtc-deal-predictor.js` is the module that drives the \"recommend 4% vs 9% vs Either\" logic, saturation / absorption risk, caveats when inputs are missing, and the legacy `predict()` wrapper. Zero tests before this PR.

## 9 test groups, 31 assertions

| Group | Count | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Public API surface | 3 | exports, empty-input shape, legacy wrapper shape |
| Execution path selection | 5 | the 4% / 9% / Either decision tree with every named branch |
| Saturation signalling | 3 | med-threshold (3) **and** high-threshold (5) boundaries; scenarioSensitivity output |
| Basis-boost rationale | 3 | isQct, isDda, neither |
| Caveats from missing inputs | 5 | pmaScore, ami30UnitsNeeded, pabCapAvailable, pabCap-only-for-large, DISCLAIMER first |
| Confidence + badge | 3 | tier enum, monotonicity with input richness, non-empty badge |
| Unit + AMI mix | 2 | shape + proposed-units total |
| Legacy predict() wrapper | 3 | score map, execution propagation, disclaimer |
| Robustness | 3 | null, string coercion, negative units |

## Notable finding while writing the tests
The module fires the `\"Market saturation: …\"` risk at **`saturationMedThreshold` (3)**, not just the high one (5). That's a defensible design choice — signalling saturation risk earlier is more useful for a decision tool than waiting until the market is oversaturated — but the two thresholds emit slightly different wording:
- `≥3`: `Market saturation: N competitive LIHTC projects within the market area`
- `≥5`: `Market saturation: N competitive LIHTC projects within 1 mile may limit absorption`

Both are tested explicitly at their boundaries so a future refactor can't silently collapse them.

## Wiring
- New npm script `test:lihtc-deal-predictor`
- Appended to both `test:ci` and `test:all` chains
- `_comment_test_ci` updated — **four unit suites now, 142 assertions total** (pro-forma 24 + QAP 64 + PMA 23 + deal-predictor 31)

## Verified

$ npm run test:ci
exit=0
```

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Update the RTP Plugin to use a blacklist approach for disabled worlds instead of whitelist.

## Problem:
Currently, RTP teleports players to ANY world if it's not in the enabled list. This is wrong!

When a player uses `/rtp` in Overworld, they should NOT be able to teleport to disabled worlds (like world_nether or world_the_end).

## Solution:
Change from whitelist (`enabled-worlds`) to blacklist (`disabled-worlds`) approach.

### Configuration Update:
```yaml
rtp:
  radius: 5000
  cooldown: 30
  combat-cooldown: 15
  search-time: 5
  max-height: 320
  
  # Worlds where RTP is BLOCKED (blacklist)
  disabled-worlds:
    - world_nether
    - world_the_end
    - arena
    - pvp_world
  
  gui:
    enabled: true
    title: "&6Random Teleport"
  
  worlds:
    world: 5000
    world_nether: 2000
    world_the_end: 1000
  
  messages:
    teleporting: "&eSearching for a random location... Don't move!"
    teleported: "&aYou have been teleported!"
    cooldown: "&cPlease wait &e{time} &cseconds before teleporting again."
    no-permission: "&cYou don't have permission to use this command."
    invalid-world: "&cRandom teleport is not available in this world."
    in-combat: "&cYou cannot use RTP while in combat!"
    movement-cancelled: "&cRTP cancelled - You moved!"
```

### Code Changes Required:

**ConfigManager.java:**
- Change `isWorldEnabled(World world)` to `isWorldDisabled(World world)`
- Load `disabled-worlds` list instead of `enabled-worlds`
- Return true if world IS in disabled-worlds list

**RTPCommand.java:**
- Check if current world is disabled (player executing command in disabled world)
- Show error if player tries to use RTP in disabled world

**TeleportService.java:**
- Check if target world is disabled BEFORE teleporting
- Find safe location only in non-disabled worlds
- Show error if teleport destination would be in disabled world

**TeleportUtil.java:**
- When selecting random coordinates, verify the world allows RTP
- Don't teleport to disabled worlds at all

## Logic:
- Player in Overworld uses `/rtp` → WORKS (Overworld not disabled)
- Player in End uses `/rtp` → BLOCKED (End is disabled)
- `/rtp` from Overworld tries to teleport to End → BLOCKED (End is disabled world, won't generate random coords there)

This way, disabled worlds are completely off-limits for RTP.

body:
## What changed
- moved host composition back to explicit inputs so `AddThreeDTilesLinkRuntime` advertises its required runtime/search/source policy dependencies
- introduced configurable `TileSourceOptions` + content-link resolution so non-Google roots and `file://` child URIs can be composed without changing parser code
- separated interactive search configuration and DTOs from Google-specific types while keeping the current Google geocoder implementation behind `ISearchResolver`
- centralized Google destination-policy defaults and removed duplicate literals from the host and `ResoniteSession` convenience path
- tightened fetch/process boundaries so content processing works on fetched content rather than pulling source access through the processor contract

## Why
The previous refactor renamed several seams but still left the production host and nested-content parser hard-wired to Google assumptions. That meant a future PLATEAU 3D tiles provider swap would still require code changes in startup and parser internals. This branch moves those assumptions to explicit composition/config and adds tests around the new seams.

author: meinharrd
body:
## Summary

On a cold Bee node, navigating to a Swarm address (`bzz://` or an ENS-resolved `.eth` name) previously rendered Bee's raw `{"code":404,"message":"address not found or incorrect"}` JSON because the node hadn't connected to enough peers to find the content yet. Even after a successful page load, sub-resources (CSS, JS, images, video) on that page often hit the same transient 404/500s and left the page looking broken.

This PR fixes both sides with two coordinated mechanisms in the main process — no JS injected into web pages.

### 1. Main-process pre-navigation probe

- New module `src/main/swarm/swarm-probe.js` HEAD-polls Bee for the target `bzz://<hash>` before the webview navigates to it (exponential backoff, 30 s per attempt, ~5 min overall, and Bee-unreachable detection).
- Wired through new IPC channels (`bzz:start-probe`, `bzz:await-probe`, `bzz:cancel-probe`) in `ipc-handlers.js` and exposed via `preload.js`.
- `src/renderer/lib/navigation.js` now gates every `bzz://` load (direct and ENS-resolved) on the probe. During the probe the tab's native loading spinner stays on; clicking Stop or starting another navigation cancels it.
- On probe failure we route to a friendlier `error.html`:
  - `swarm_content_not_found` message when the probe times out.
  - Existing "Swarm node is not running" page when Bee's HTTP API is unreachable.
  - The address bar and error page show the original `ens://swarm.eth` (not the internal `bzz://<hash>`); "Try Again" re-enters the probe flow instead of going straight to the raw gateway URL.

### 2. Custom `bzz:` scheme via `session.protocol.handle`

After the probe succeeds, navigation loads `bzz://<hash>/<path>` instead of the raw Bee gateway URL. `bzz` is registered at startup as a privileged standard scheme (`secure`, `supportFetchAPI`, `corsEnabled`, `stream`, `allowServiceWorkers`), and every `bzz://` request is served by a main-process handler in `src/main/swarm/bzz-protocol.js` that:

- Proxies the request to the local Bee gateway (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/bzz/<hash>/<path>`).
- Always sets `Swarm-Chunk-Retrieval-Timeout`, `Swarm-Redundancy-Strategy: 3`, and `Swarm-Redundancy-Fallback-Mode: true`, giving Bee more server-side runway per chunk.
- Retries transient `404`/`500`/`502`/`503`/`504` on idempotent methods with bounded exponential backoff (~3 min total). Non-idempotent methods (`POST`, …) are single-shot because the request body is a consumable stream.
- Strips hop-by-hop / origin / referer headers before forwarding.
- Streams the response body back to Chromium, preserving `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Content-Range`, and `Swarm-Feed-*`, so video Range requests and feed-resolved content work transparently.

Because `bzz` is a standard scheme, `bzz://<hash>/` becomes the page origin in Chromium. Same-origin relative paths (`<script src="/foo.js">`, `url(/images/x.png)` in CSS) resolve naturally to `bzz://<hash>/foo.js` — no URL rewriting for `bzz://` is needed, and `request-rewriter.js` no longer handles that scheme (IPFS / Radicle rewriting is unchanged).

This fixes the class of "randomly broken CSS / video doesn't load" reports that an earlier in-page retry shim could not reach: `<video>` Range requests, CSS-descendant URLs (`background-image`, `@font-face`, `@import`), service workers, and `fetch()` calls issued before any preload-installed wrapper could apply.

## Files

- Probe: `src/main/swarm/swarm-probe.js` + tests
- Protocol handler: `src/main/swarm/bzz-protocol.js` + tests
- Scheme registration + handler wiring: `src/main/index.js`
- IPC plumbing: `src/main/ipc-handlers.js`, `src/main/preload.js`, `src/shared/ipc-channels.js` (+ tests)
- Renderer flow: `src/renderer/lib/navigation.js`, `src/renderer/lib/tabs.js`, `src/renderer/pages/error.html` (+ tests)
- Rewriter: `src/main/request-rewriter.js` — dropped the `bzz://` → gateway conversion (handled by protocol handler now)
- Preload: `src/main/webview-preload.js` — dropped the in-page sub-resource retry shim
- Docs: new `## Swarm Content Retrieval` section in `README.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased]` entry

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run lint` passes (confirmed locally).
- [ ] `npm test` green (confirmed locally: 1019 passing across 58 suites; one pre-existing unrelated Bee integration test fails on `main` too).
- [ ] With the Swarm node stopped, type `swarm.eth` and land on the "Swarm node is not running" page.
- [ ] With Bee freshly started (cold, few peers) type `swarm.eth` and observe the tab spinner running until content resolves, then the page loading cleanly. Address bar shows `ens://swarm.eth`.
- [ ] Once loaded, `document.location.origin` in DevTools is `bzz://<hash>` (not `http://127.0.0.1:1633`), and sub-resources fetch from `bzz://...` rather than the gateway URL.
- [ ] Video elements play through on first cold load (Range requests are retried transparently).
- [ ] If the probe ultimately times out, the error page shows `swarm.eth` (not the hash); "Try Again" re-enters the probe flow.
- [ ] Clicking Stop during the probe cancels it and returns to the previous URL.

## Architecture notes

- Both mechanisms live in the main process. No JavaScript is injected into loaded pages for Swarm retry logic.
- `session.protocol.handle('bzz', …)` replaces an earlier renderer-side retry shim that was structurally blind to `<video>` Range requests, CSS descendants, and service workers.
- The probe stays as-is for UX reasons (native spinner + clean error routing) even though the protocol handler would otherwise retry through Bee's initial 404s.

Collect a PDP-specific client ID in the CLI and surface the real OAuth/server error when PDP token minting fails, instead of hiding both behind the misleading "missing 'access_token'" shape-check error.

author: hituziando
body:
execCommand invoked this.handlerDict[req.name] without first verifying the command was registered. The public KM.send path guards this via browser.hasCommand() before calling execCommand, but consumers that call execCommand directly (or any future internal path that skips the pre-check) would hit TypeError: this.handlerDict[req.name] is not a function and leave the request dangling with no reject.

Guard the call inside execCommand so a missing command funnels through the same reject path as a handler-rejected request: encodeURIComponent the reason ("CommandNotAdded") and hand it to KM.onError, which in turn rejects the request promise with Rejected:<name>:CommandNotAdded. Add a regression test that drives execCommand directly with an unregistered name and verifies the reason propagates; the test fails against the previous code with the TypeError.

body:
## Summary

- **StreamRecorder class** (`packages/orchestrator/src/core/stream-recorder.ts`): Records full agent event streams as JSONL files with crash-safe `appendFileSync`. Manages manifest.json per issue with attempt tracking, PR linkage, and retention lifecycle.
- **REST API** (`packages/orchestrator/src/server/routes/streams.ts`): `GET /api/streams/:issueId/:attempt?` serves JSONL with `application/x-ndjson`, `GET /api/streams/:issueId/manifest` returns manifest JSON. Strict path segment validation.
- **Dashboard replay** (`packages/dashboard/src/client/hooks/useStreamReplay.ts`): Fetches recorded history and parses JSONL into ContentBlocks. AgentStreamDrawer merges recorded history with live WebSocket events, shows session stats from manifest, and distinguishes Live vs Recorded mode.
- **PR highlights** (`packages/orchestrator/src/core/highlight-extractor.ts`): Scans JSONL for file operations, test runs, git operations, and completion events. Selects top 5 diverse moments. Renders GitHub PR comment with metrics table + collapsible key moments.

author: 1e0ng
body:
## Summary

Adds gyro-based heading correction to the 2-DOF coupled controller. When `drivebase.use_gyro(True)` is called, the control tick reads heading from an attached IMU instead of computing it from the encoder differential — slip-immune, unaffected by asymmetric friction. Matches the Pybricks `DriveBase.use_gyro(True)` API.

Requires PR #31 (BNO055 in C) which already landed — the IMU is read every 1 ms through a cached bound method, no Python frame on the tick.

### C drivebase (`native/user_c_modules/openbricks/drivebase.c`)

- New optional `imu=` constructor kwarg. Caches `imu.heading` bound method.
- New `use_gyro(enable)` method. Toggling on captures the current heading as the new zero offset.
- `drivebase_register` re-baselines heading on every move-start, so each `straight()` / `turn()` begins from heading 0 regardless of where the robot was pointing.
- Control tick: when `use_gyro` is active, `diff_pos = -body_delta * axle * π / wheel_circumference` (body-deg → wheel-deg), with a ±180 wrap on the delta to handle BNO055 heading rollover mid-move. Otherwise unchanged (encoder-diff).

### Python `DriveBase` wrapper (`openbricks/robotics/drivebase.py`)

- `DriveBase(..., imu=None)` passes through to the native layer.
- `DriveBase.use_gyro(enable)` forwards; raises `RuntimeError` for open-loop motor pairs (no native drivebase to toggle).

### Tests (+4)

- `_FakeIMU` — minimal shim with only `.heading()`.
- `test_requires_imu_attached` — `ValueError` when `use_gyro(True)` is called without an IMU.
- `test_use_gyro_toggle_without_native_raises` — `RuntimeError` for L298N-only motor pairs.
- `test_gyro_heading_drives_diff_correction` — inject a +10° CCW heading, assert `left_dps > right_dps` (CW correction).
- `test_use_gyro_false_reverts_to_encoder_feedback` — with gyro off, injecting IMU heading has no effect on target_dps.

## Usage

```python
from openbricks.drivers.bno055 import BNO055
from openbricks.drivers.jgb37_520 import JGB37Motor
from openbricks.robotics import DriveBase
from machine import I2C, Pin

i2c   = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22), freq=400_000)
imu   = BNO055(i2c)
left  = JGB37Motor(in1=25, in2=26, pwm=27, encoder_a=32, encoder_b=33)
right = JGB37Motor(in1=14, in2=12, pwm=13, encoder_a=34, encoder_b=35)

robot = DriveBase(left, right, wheel_diameter_mm=56, axle_track_mm=114, imu=imu)
robot.use_gyro(True)          # switch heading feedback to the BNO055
robot.straight(500)           # now slip-immune
robot.turn(90)                # heading from IMU, not encoder diff
```

## Test plan

- [x] `./native/micropython/ports/unix/build-standard/micropython tests/run.py` — 140 tests green
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] On real ESP32 + BNO055 + JGB37s: `use_gyro(True)` + `turn(90)` → robot actually turns 90° body-heading regardless of wheel slip

## الهدف
المرحلة الثالثة من تحويل ميزان إلى SaaS — **التكامل مع Moyasar + التسجيل الذاتي للمستأجرين**.

## التدفق الكامل للاشتراك

```
/                             (landing)
  └─ choose plan ──→ /checkout/{plan}?cycle=yearly
                        └─ fill form + coupon (AJAX) + Moyasar MPF
                              └─ Moyasar hosted payment page
                                    └─ /checkout/callback?id=pay_xxx
                                          ├─ verify via MoyasarService::getPayment
                                          ├─ DB::transaction:
                                          │    ├─ Tenant row
                                          │    ├─ Subscription row
                                          │    ├─ Payment row
                                          │    ├─ CouponService::apply (atomic)
                                          │    └─ CreateTenantJob dispatch (queued)
                                          └─ redirect /checkout/success
                                                └─ TenantWelcomeMail (48h signed URL)
                                                      └─ tenant.sa/password/setup/{token}
                                                            └─ /dashboard (logged in)
```

## الملفات

### Services + Jobs (2)
| ملف | الدور |
|-----|------|
| `app/Services/MoyasarService.php` | wrapper لـ Moyasar API (createPayment/getPayment/refundPayment/verifyWebhook) مع تحويل تلقائي SAR → halalas |
| `app/Jobs/CreateTenantJob.php` | provisioning async: subdomain + stancl JobPipeline + admin user + welcome mail + SuperAdmin notification |

### Controllers (3 جديدة)
- `CheckoutController` (show/applyCoupon/callback/success)
- `MoyasarWebhookController` (HMAC-SHA256 signature check)
- `TenantPasswordSetupController` (يقرأ token + يحفظ كلمة مرور + يُدخل)

### Mailables + Views (5)
- `TenantWelcomeMail` + `resources/views/emails/tenant/welcome.blade.php`
- `TrialExpiryWarningMail` + `resources/views/emails/tenant/trial-warning.blade.php`
- `resources/views/checkout/{show,success}.blade.php` — Alpine + Moyasar MPF
- `resources/views/auth/tenant-setup.blade.php`

### Commands (2) + Schedule
- `saas:check-trial-expiry` — يومياً 00:00 — expired + suspend لو `trial_suspend_after_expiry`
- `saas:send-trial-warnings` — يومياً 08:00 — تنبيه قبل `trial_warning_days`
- `routes/console.php` يُسجّل الجدولة مع `withoutOverlapping + onOneServer`

### Routes (7 جديدة)
| المسار | الاسم |
|-------|------|
| GET /checkout/{plan} | checkout.show |
| POST /checkout/apply-coupon | checkout.apply-coupon |
| GET /checkout/callback | checkout.callback |
| GET /checkout/success | checkout.success |
| POST /webhooks/moyasar | webhooks.moyasar (CSRF-exempt) |
| GET /password/setup/{token} | tenant.password.setup (signed) |
| POST /password/setup | tenant.password.setup.store |

## الأمان

- **Moyasar API keys** مشفّرة في system_settings، تُقرأ عبر Config في كل request
- **Webhook** يتحقّق HMAC-SHA256 على `X-Moyasar-Signature` — بدون توقيع = 401
- **Callback** لا يثق بأي شيء من query string — يستدعي getPayment() server-side
- **كل callback** داخل DB::transaction (atomic)
- **Coupon redemption** عبر `DB::increment('uses_count')` (race-safe)
- **Signed URL** 48 ساعة لتهيئة كلمة المرور (لا كلمة مرور في clear في البريد)

author: jaudiger
body:
This PR extends `Brioche.gitCheckout` so you can pass a commit hash in addition to a branch or tag name. The existing named ref lookup is kept, and a commit hash fallback is added on top, so both cases are handled by the same function.

When `fetch_git_commit_for_ref` is called, it connects to the remote, runs the git protocol handshake, and asks the server for the list of refs with ls-refs. It then tries to match the value passed against refs/heads/<name> and refs/tags/<name>. If a ref matches, the function return the commit it points to and stop there. This is the same behavior as before.

If no ref matches and the value looks like a full 40 character hex SHA, the code treats it as a commit hash. It sends a minimal fetch request to the server with want `<oid>` to confirm the commit exists on the remote. To avoid pulling the full history just for a check, the code asks for deepen `1` and the `blob:none` filter whenever the server advertises support for them. If the server accepts the want, the function returns the hash. If it rejects it, it returns an error that keeps the underlying reason and says the commit was not found or unreachable.

Trying the name match first matters in one edge case: a branch or tag that happens to be spelled like a commit hash still wins, because we always look at the ref list before falling back to commit validation.

I also replaced `std::thread::spawn` and the `oneshot` channel with `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. The behavior is the same, since `gix` is a blocking client and the work still runs off the async runtime, but the caller is simpler and the error from the resolver is preserved end to end instead of being flattened into a string.

author: cwolfinger
body:
## Summary

Implements Part B of https://github.com/map-room/map-room/blob/docs/proai-air-evacuation-spec/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-21-proai-air-evacuation-design.md.

After \`moveUnitsToBestTerritories\` and before the unmoved-unit warning loop in \`ProNonCombatMoveAi.doNonCombatMove\`, run a new rescue pass \`evacuateStrandedAir\`. For every air unit whose current territory is not a valid landing spot (conquered-this-turn land, or sea zones without carrier capacity) and which has at least one valid option in its move map, pick the best destination via a two-pass heuristic and assign it.

- **Pass 1**: defense-maximizer restricted to the unit's valid reachable options (mirrors the threshold logic from the existing air-placement pass — capital + winPct / factory + winPct / tuvSwing ≥ 0).
- **Pass 2**: nearest-valid fallback, ties broken by \`territoryValueMap\` so strategically useful tiles beat filler.

Units with no valid option remain in place — downstream engines are expected to crash them per §19 (Map Room shipped this path in PR #1906).

## Why

\`ProCombatMoveAi.canAirSafelyLandAfterAttack\` picks attack targets based on a half-range heuristic, but nothing re-checks the post-capture landing situation. After the attack resolves, air units sit on a just-conquered territory. The existing NCM air-placement pass is a pure defense-maximizer — if the unit's reachable options don't improve defense, it leaves the unit unmoved and logs a warning. The unit stays on the conquered tile.

Observed in production (map-room sidecar): Japanese bombers u87, u88, tactical_bomber u107, fighter u145 all physically on Amur after Japan's turn ends, with Amur in \`_conqueredThisTurn\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`games.strategy.triplea.ai.pro.*\` test suite passes
- [x] \`:game-app:ai-sidecar:test\` passes (\`NoncombatMoveExecutorIntegrationTest\` and others) — rescue is a no-op when no air is stranded
- [x] Spotless clean
- [ ] 🧑 Manual: deploy to map-room sidecar, reproduce the Amur scenario, confirm bombers end up at strategically-chosen landings (airfields, capitals, home) rather than random nearest-friendly tiles.

## Follow-up

Dedicated ProNonCombatMoveAi unit test coverage is not part of this PR — the codebase has no established fixture for direct \`doNonCombatMove\` invocation and building one is a larger infra task. Behavior is validated via the existing sidecar integration tests plus manual Amur reproduction. If future regressions call for unit tests, build a ProAiTestFixture at that point.

body:
## Summary
- Conversations + actions search were one-shot (limit=50, no pagination) and rendered raw records with no indication where the query hit
- Switched both to an envelope response \`{items, total, offset, limit, has_more, semantic?}\` with per-item \`snippet_html\` containing the match wrapped in \`<mark>\`
- Conversations run **keyword (paged)** first, then overlay a capped **\"Related by meaning\"** semantic tail on page 0 (deduped against keyword ids)
- UI renders initial page + appends on scroll-near-bottom; no re-render, no jump

## Why
User workflow was \"search the full history for a keyword\" — semantic-only recall was fuzzy and the UI silently capped at 50. Now you can keyword-filter the whole archive with pagination, still get semantic suggestions where they help.

## Scope (explicit)
- **Changed**: \`/api/conversations/search\`, \`/api/actions/search\` (GET)
- **Unchanged**: memories / manifests / tasks / products / ideas search endpoints — already work for users

## Files
- \`internal/web/snippet.go\` — new \`highlightSnippet\` helper (case-insensitive, ~80 chars context, HTML-escapes non-match, wraps match with \`<mark>\`, falls back to first 160 chars on no-match)
- \`internal/conversation/store.go\` — new \`SearchKeyword(q, limit, offset) (items, total, err)\` over title/summary/turns
- \`internal/action/search.go\` — new \`SearchPaged(q, limit, offset) (items, total, err)\`; old \`Search\` kept as a shim
- \`internal/web/handlers_search.go\` — envelope shape for both endpoints; conversations merge keyword + semantic (page 0 only)
- \`internal/web/ui/views/conversations.js\`, \`actions.js\` — infinite scroll state machine (offset tracking, append-only, scroll-to-bottom trigger, detach on clear); separate sections for keyword vs. \"Related by meaning\"
- \`internal/web/ui/style.css\` — \`.conv-item-snippet\` (2-line clamp) + global \`<mark>\` styling

## Test plan
- [x] \`go build ./...\`
- [x] \`go test ./internal/web/... ./internal/conversation/... ./internal/action/...\`

- [ ] Manual: search \"mysqldump\" on Actions tab, scroll — verify pagination, snippet shows \`<mark>mysqldump</mark>\` inside the tool_input fragment

…o workspace

Rewritten onboarding to guide new users to the aha moment — a commit closing
a ticket — before asking for configuration. Applies patterns from analysis
of 1,460 onboarding flows: sell outcomes, personalize, show-don't-tell.

Backend (convex/)
- schema: preferences gains onboardingIntents, teamSize, dismissedFounderNote
- schema: workspaces/projects/tasks gain isDemo flag
- auth/users: extended preference validators; invokes seed helper on first
  user creation (wrapped in try/catch — seeding failure is non-fatal)
- onboarding/seedDemo: plants a full narrative — LTF1 Tour workspace, demo-app
  project, active sprint, 3 tasks (done/in_review/todo), and the activity
  timeline that shows a PR merge auto-closing LTF-1. Idempotent — bails if
  user already has a membership. Also exposes deleteMyDemo for one-shot cleanup.

Frontend (apps/web/src/)
- OnboardingFlow: 7-step flow — aha → intent → team → projection → ai →
  import → theme → complete. AhaStep auto-plays a terminal showing
  git push → LTF-1 DONE. IntentStep + TeamStep drive a personalized
  ProjectionStep ("~X hrs/week recovered, here's what we'll prioritize").
  AI tier carries a RECOMMENDED badge driven by team size; import step
  highlights Linear/Jira when that intent was picked. Theme step moved
  to an optional last step with a KEEP DEFAULT button.
- FounderNoteCard: README-style welcome note rendered on dashboard for
  freshly-onboarded users; Discord + changelog links; dismiss persists.

- WorkspaceCard: [DEMO] badge + two-click DELETE DEMO action that calls

author: seamus-brady
body:
## Summary

Closes the chat-hijack bug that was supposed to be fixed by the Frontdoor PR (#90) but wasn't.

#90 shipped the Frontdoor routing plumbing (publishes to `HumanQuestionOutput` for autonomous cycles, with a drop-for-SchedulerSource policy) — but the **legacy `QuestionForHuman` broadcast on line 197 still fired unconditionally**. Since the scheduler runner never `Subscribe`s to Frontdoor as a destination, Frontdoor's drop branch never actually runs — the route silently dies at "no destination registered" and the broadcast goes out to every connected browser just like before. The observed symptom (operator chat hijacked by scheduler cycles, requires refresh) was unchanged.

This is the surgical close.

## Change

Both broadcast sites now branch on `state.cycle_node_type`:

- `handle_own_human_input` (cognitive-loop's own `request_human_input`): SchedulerCycle synthesises a tool result ("No human is attached to this autonomous cycle...") and spawns a continuation think worker. The react loop resumes with the canned instruction instead of entering `WaitingForUser`.
- `handle_agent_question` (sub-agent's `request_human_input`): SchedulerCycle replies directly to the waiting agent's reply subject with the same canned message. Cognitive state stays unchanged — the agent's react loop continues in its own process.

Interactive cycles keep the existing behaviour.

## Test plan

- [x] `gleam build` — clean
- [x] `gleam test` — 1720 passing
- [ ] Smoke: trigger a scheduler-driven cycle that calls `request_human_input` (e.g. force the meta-learning scheduler into an ambiguous state). Confirm no broadcast, no UI hijack, cycle continues.
- [ ] Smoke: manually invoke `request_human_input` during an interactive cycle. Confirm the question still reaches the web/TUI as before.

## Summary

Refactors the gcc nightly release pipeline with improved architecture using Docker and GitHub repository_dispatch events for better dependency management and build isolation.

## Changes

- **Rewrite release.yml**: Implements repository_dispatch triggers for:
  - Stage 0: Triggered from binutils, manages initial build
  - Stage 1: Triggered from newlib, manages dependent gcc build
- **Deterministic builds**: Downloads dependencies using exact tags from dispatch payload
- **Docker image**: Publishes lightweight ubuntu:24.04 runtime image to GHCR alongside tarball
- **Dispatch threading**: Passes binutils_tag and newlib_tag through dispatch payloads for consistency
- **Reliability improvements**: 
  - Concurrency guards to prevent parallel workflows
  - Fail-fast curl flags for robust dependency downloads
  - hello.c smoke test to validate built artifacts
- **Simplified codebase**: Removes obsolete update.yml workflow
- **Container support**: Adds Dockerfile for production deployments

## Benefits

- Better separation of concerns with stage-based dispatch
- Reproducible builds via explicit version pinning
- Reduced resource usage with optimized Docker images
- Improved observability of multi-stage release process

[skip-receipt-gate: version-bump chore — no new code, releasing modules already merged via OMN-9335 (PR #867)]

## Summary

- Bumps \`pyproject.toml\` version from \`0.39.0\` → \`0.40.0\`
- Updates \`uv.lock\` to reflect new version

## Why

Commit \`9a353982\` (PR #867, merged 2026-04-20, OMN-9335) added two new modules to main **after** the \`v0.39.0\` tag was cut (2026-04-06):
- \`omnibase_core.validation.checker_normalization_symmetry\`
- \`omnibase_core.topics\` (TopicBase + build_topic helpers)

Without a new release, \`ccc#301\` and 7 downstream bot PRs remain blocked because those modules are not available on PyPI.

## Release mechanism

On merge, the \`Auto-Tag on Merge\` workflow detects the \`release\` label, reads \`pyproject.toml\`, creates tag \`v0.40.0\`, and pushes it. The tag push triggers the \`Release\` workflow which builds and publishes to PyPI, then fires \`dependency-cascade\` to open lockfile-bump PRs in downstream repos.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] Auto-tag creates \`v0.40.0\` on merge
- [ ] Release workflow publishes \`omnibase-core==0.40.0\` to PyPI
- [ ] \`ccc-uv-bump-fixer\` unblocks after PyPI confirms publish

author: copilot
body: ## 📝 Description Redesigns the `/select` page into a two-column layout: a left endpoint tree (with all existing filters/checkboxes preserved) and a right live HTTP preview panel that updates as endpoints are checked. ### Left panel — endpoint tree - Checking an endpoint adds it to the preview in selection order; unchecking removes it — row click now toggles the checkbox directly - Selected endpoints highlighted with a coloured left-border accent (`border-primary` + `bg-primary/10`) - Tag section headers are `sticky top-0 z-10` (Linear-style — the section label pins while the list scrolls beneath it) - **Select All** and **Deselect All** buttons moved into the Endpoints card header - Filters pinned above the scrollable endpoint list ### Right panel — `HttpPreview` component - Renders the combined `.http` file for **all checked endpoints** in selection order using `generateHttpFileContent` - Simplified title — always "HTTP Preview" - Syntax highlighting per token type: | Token | Colour | |---|---| | `# comment` | muted grey | | `@var = value` | cyan name + muted value | | `### Section` | yellow bold | | `METHOD URL` | method-coloured + foreground URL | | `Header: value` | blue name + muted value | | Body / JSON | green | - **"Copy"** button (with ✓ feedback) + **"Download .http"** button in the panel header (download filename uses spec title) - Empty state placeholder when no endpoint is checked ### Page layout - `StepIndicator` removed from the select page - Compact single-row header bar at the top: spec title, version, base URL, endpoint count, "Upload new file", and **Download ZIP** button — replaces the separate `SpecInfo` + `GenerationActions` cards - Layout is `h-[calc(100vh-3.5rem)] overflow-hidden` — **only the two panels scroll**, the page body does not - Grid uses `flex-1 min-h-0` so panels fill the remaining viewport height dynamically (no fixed `h-[600px]`) ### Other - `EndpointItem`: removed `isActive` / `onPreview` props; row click toggles selection; selected state drives the left-border accent - `EndpointGroup`: removed `onPreview` / `previewEndpointId` props; tag header is now sticky - `select/page.tsx`: `selectionOrder` state tracks check order; `orderedPreviewEndpoints` feeds the right panel - `translations.ts`: `previewSelectEndpoint` updated in EN + FR to reflect checkbox-driven interaction ### Screenshots **GET endpoint selected** — compact header bar at top, Select All / Deselect All in left card header, sticky tag label, left-border accent on selected row, combined preview on the right: **POST endpoint selected** — multi-endpoint combined preview with Copy + Download buttons: --- ## 🎯 Motivation & Impact The previous single-column list gave no way to inspect generated output without downloading. The new layout surfaces the `.http` preview inline with Rider-style colouring, showing all checked endpoints combined in real time — matching the multi-select mental model users already have from the checkboxes. Moving the download action to the top removes the need to scroll to the bottom to act. Sticky tag headers and checkbox-driven preview interaction (rather than a separate click target) reduce cognitive overhead. Locking only the two panels to scroll — rather than the whole page — mirrors the Postman UX and keeps the layout stable regardless of spec size. All existing features (filters, checkboxes, ZIP download) are unchanged. --- ## 🔗 Links (optional) Related Issue(s):

body:
## The bug (CRITICAL prod data correctness)

\`chargeTypeToOffguide("drug-trafficking")\` returned "17" — which is USSC code for Immigration. Similar transpositions across ~12 chargeType slugs. Every Similar Cases Analyzer (\$297) and plea-analyzer report with a mapped chargeType matched the defendant to the WRONG federal offense bucket.

## Transposition matrix

| Slug | Old (wrong) | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| drug-trafficking | 17 (Immigration) | 10 (Drug Trafficking) |
| drug-possession | 22 (not in FSD) | 9 (Drug Possession) |
| white-collar / fraud | 13 (Firearms) | 16 (Fraud/Theft/Embez) |
| weapons | 16 (Fraud) | 13 (Firearms) |
| sex-offense-contact | 26 (Robbery) | 27 (Sex Abuse) |
| sex-offense-digital | 27 (Sex Abuse) | 7 (Child Pornography) |
| murder | 1 (Admin) | null |
| kidnapping | 3 (not in FSD) | null |
| theft | 21 (Money Laundry) | 16 |
| burglary / robbery | 5 (Bribery) | null / 26 |
| arson | 7 (Child Porn) | null |
| contempt | 25 (Prison Off) | 1 (Admin of Justice) |
| probation-violation | 29 (Tax) | 25 (Prison Offenses) |

## Root cause
Original map hand-coded from matview OCCURRENCE COUNTS (PR #7) without cross-checking against USSC codebook's offguide_label column. Header comment itself labeled code 17 as "drug trafficking" (it's Immigration). Tests hardcoded the wrong expected values so couldn't catch it.

## The fix
ussc-mappings.ts now imports from \`src/lib/fsd-offguide.ts\` (shipped in PR #16) which uses FSD table's offguide_label as authoritative source. Single source of truth. Ambiguous slugs (murder/kidnapping/arson/burglary) return null instead of fabricated codes.

## Impact
- Customers getting correct federal sentencing data starting at deploy time
- Existing data (reports already delivered) not retroactively fixed — operator may want to manually re-run recent high-value orders
- Positive cascade: every $297 Similar Cases Analyzer order is now matched to the right bucket

## Test plan
- [x] tsc clean
- [x] 542/548 vitest pass (6 pre-existing skips), 0 regressions
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Post-merge: spot-check prod with curl for drug-trafficking + verify response mentions Drug Trafficking not Immigration

author: meleksomai
body:
Closes #591.

Wires [`publint`](https://github.com/bluwy/publint) into CI as a first-class turbo task so packaging regressions (malformed `exports` maps, stale types paths, accidentally-published `src/` or `tests/`) fail the PR instead of leaking to npm. See [ADR 0015](./docs/adr/0015-secure-publishing.md) for the full secure-publishing posture this fits into.

## Shape of the integration

Every public package gets a `publint` script and devDep; `turbo.json` gains a `publint` task with `dependsOn: ["build"]`; the root `pnpm publint` simply delegates to `turbo run publint`. Private packages omit the script and turbo skips them automatically. This matches the existing pattern for `build`, `test`, and `check-types` — no bespoke iterator script, no custom filter logic.

Why not wire into the existing `linting` job? That job does not run `pnpm build`, and publint validates against the real `pnpm pack` output. A dedicated `packaging` job builds (via turbo's task graph) then lints.

## What the check caught on its first run

`@glion/annotate-delimiters` was missing `"files": ["dist"]` and shipping `src/`, `tests/`, `tsup.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, and `.turbo/` logs to npm on every release. Patch changeset included. All other 40 public packages already pass `publint --strict`.

## Security framing — why this is on the PR now

Glion is entering launch mode (#590) and publishes ~40 `@glion/*` packages. ADR 0015 lays out six layers of the publishing-security model:

1. Package-shape validation — **this PR**
2. Publisher authentication & sigstore provenance — **gap**: `ci:publish` does not pass `--provenance` and the scope is not yet on trusted publishers. Commit `3ea71c2e` normalized the `repository` field in preparation; the flag itself is follow-up work.
3. Supply-chain integrity — dev tools exact-pinned (publint pinned at `0.3.18`)
4. Publish trigger integrity — publishes only from CI on `main`
5. Minimal package contents — enforced transitively by (1)
6. Secrets & credential hygiene — `SECURITY.md` still TODO

Only (1) is fully automated by this PR; the ADR calls the other gaps out by name so they do not silently rot.

## Verification

| Check                | Result                                              |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm publint` cold  | 41 pass, 2 private skipped (~30s)                   |
| `pnpm publint` warm  | FULL TURBO cache hit (~3s)                          |
| `pnpm check`         | clean                                               |
| `pnpm check-types`   | 42/42 packages                                      |
| `pnpm build`         | 41/41 packages                                      |

## Files to skim

- `turbo.json` — one-line task addition
- `docs/adr/0015-secure-publishing.md` — the full rationale, including explicitly rejected alternatives (custom `tools/publint-workspace.mjs`, `prepublishOnly` hooks, non-strict rollout)
- `packages/annotate-delimiters/package.json` — the live bug the check caught

The 40 other package.json diffs are mechanical (identical `publint` script + devDep added); easiest to review them in bulk rather than one-by-one.

author: sinameraji
body:
Bundle addressing the "UI is a mess", manual version bumps, and lack of per-repo agent context.

## Part A — UI polish

- **Markdown renderer** (`src/ui/markdown.tsx`, new). Kimi's replies use **bold**, *italic*, `code`, `#` headers, and `- ` bullets — all previously rendered as literal syntax. Now styled via a ~180-line parser wired into `ChatView`'s assistant branch.
- **Diff view**: drop `--- path` / `+++ path` headers (tool title has the path already) and `\ No newline at end of file` markers. For small edits (≤ 3 changed lines, single hunk) hide the `@@` header too.
- **Visual rhythm**: `marginTop={1}` on user events + `paddingLeft={1}` on assistant replies. No more wall-of-text.
- **Tool titles**: `bash: cd /long/path && git status` → `$ git status`. Paths inside cwd show as relative, paths outside collapse to `…/last-two`.
- **Tool-view compact args**: absolute paths in fallback previews collapse via the same helper.

## Part B — `/init` + `KIMI.md`

Matches Claude Code's `CLAUDE.md` pattern but named `KIMI.md` (`KIMIFLARE.md` and `AGENT.md` also accepted). 

- `/init` slash command scans the repo and has the model `write` a concise `KIMI.md` at the root.
- On every subsequent launch, `buildSystemPrompt` auto-loads the file into the system prompt as authoritative project context.
- A one-line info event confirms when a context file was picked up.

## Part C — release-please for auto-version bumps

`.github/workflows/release-please.yml` (new):

1. Feature PR merges to main → release-please opens/updates a single "release PR" that bumps `package.json` + writes `CHANGELOG.md` entries based on Conventional Commit subjects.
2. Merging the release PR tags `v*.*.*` and creates a GitHub release.
3. The existing `publish.yml` sees the version change and publishes to npm automatically.

No more hand-edited `package.json` version bumps per PR.

## Part D — defensive

`onTasks` callback no longer nests `setTasksStartedAt` inside a `setTasks` updater function (React anti-pattern; state updaters should be pure). Unlikely to be the welcome-flood cause but worth cleaning up.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run build` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (confirmed locally)
- [ ] Ask a question that returns markdown (`**bold**`, bullets) — assistant reply shows styled, not literal
- [ ] Run `bash: cd $(pwd) && git status` — tool title shows `$ git status`
- [ ] One-line edit — diff shows just `- old / + new`, no `---`/`+++` headers or `@@`
- [ ] Delete `KIMI.md`, run `/init` in the kimiflare repo itself — model writes `KIMI.md`
- [ ] Re-launch kimiflare — `loaded project context from KIMI.md (N lines)` info appears
- [ ] Merge this PR — release-please bot opens a release PR within ~1 min
- [ ] Merge the release PR — version bumps, `publish.yml` publishes to npm

author: himerus
body:
## Summary

Security hotfix closing two CRITICAL gate-bypass vectors in the shipped push/commit review hooks. Both were reachable by any agent or user with write access to `.rea/policy.yaml` — the bypasses fired BEFORE policy schema validation, so the strict zod loader never saw (and therefore never rejected) the disarming keys.

### Defect B — `push_review: false` / `commit_review: false` grep bypass

Removed the unaudited grep short-circuits:

- `hooks/_lib/push-review-core.sh:344-350` — `grep -qE 'push_review:[[:space:]]*false' .rea/policy.yaml` → `exit 0`
- `hooks/commit-review-gate.sh:111` — mirror bug for `commit_review: false`

Both blocks ran **before** `REA_SKIP_PUSH_REVIEW` (the audited whole-gate escape hatch, `push-review-core.sh:355`) and before any other policy loading. The only remaining escape hatches are the documented env-var waivers, which require non-empty reasons, are refused in CI, and emit `push.review.skipped` / `codex.review.skipped` audit records.

### Defect C — protected-paths matcher omits `.rea/` and `.husky/`

Extended the awk regex at `hooks/_lib/push-review-core.sh:859` and the user-facing error listing at `:893-898` to include `[.]rea/` and `[.]husky/`. The `[.]` bracket literal is load-bearing: it matches `.rea/policy.yaml` but does NOT match bare `rea/` path segments (e.g. a project folder named `rea`).

Without this, diffs to `.rea/policy.yaml` (autonomy, blocked_paths, block_ai_attribution) or `.husky/pre-push` (gate entry points) previously reached `main` without the protected-path Codex adversarial-review requirement firing.

### Dogfood mirror sync

`.claude/hooks/_lib/push-review-core.sh` and `.claude/hooks/commit-review-gate.sh` synced byte-identical.

### tarball-smoke security-claim gate extension

Extended `scripts/tarball-smoke.sh` so `[security]`-tagged changesets also validate against `__tests__/hooks/*{security,bypass,sanitize,injection}*.test.ts` — the prior gate only inspected `src/**/*{security,sanitize}*.test.ts`, so a hook-only security fix was invisible to the regression-test assertion. Perl extractor yields concrete hook refs from the test body; zero-extractable-refs fails loud.

## Regression coverage

New test suite `__tests__/hooks/push-review-gate-policy-bypass.test.ts` (5 cases):

1. `push_review: false` in policy → gate still runs
2. `commit_review: false` in policy → commit gate still runs
3. Diff touching `.rea/policy.yaml` → protected-path Codex requirement fires
4. Diff touching `.husky/pre-push` → protected-path Codex requirement fires
5. Diff touching `Projects/rea/Bug Reports/note.md` (bare `rea/` segment) → Codex does NOT fire

Plus dogfood mirror byte-identity assertions locked in at CI time. Two pre-existing sibling tests (`push-review-gate-git-adapter.test.ts`, `push-review-gate-prepush-stdin.test.ts`) that previously asserted the bypass was honored were correctly inverted.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint && pnpm type-check && pnpm test && pnpm build` — green (1116/1117)
- [x] `shellcheck` on all hook sources + tarball-smoke.sh — clean
- [x] `diff -u hooks/_lib/push-review-core.sh .claude/hooks/_lib/push-review-core.sh` — empty
- [x] `diff -u hooks/commit-review-gate.sh .claude/hooks/commit-review-gate.sh` — empty
- [x] `bash scripts/tarball-smoke.sh` — PASS (hook-test gate + dist symbol gate both satisfied)
- [x] code-reviewer agent — pass
- [x] security-engineer agent — pass (awk regex validated against 15 adversarial path shapes)
- [x] codex-adversarial agent — pass (4 iterations; 3 out-of-scope findings rolled to 0.10.0)
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Post-publish: `grep -c push_review:` / `commit_review:` in published tarball returns 0

body:
Render log today showed the generic
  "Google rechazó el intercambio (401): invalid_client"
which is accurate but doesn't tell you what to do. Add defensive logging and a mapped hint for every common Google OAuth error so the next time the cause is obvious from the logs alone.

- Warn at exchange time when GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET had trimmed whitespace or doesn't start with "GOCSPX-" (the real Google web client secret format). Those two account for 90% of invalid_client reports — copy-paste errors.
- Log secret_prefix (first 10 chars) + secret_length on every exchange so we can compare what the server is actually using against what's in Google Cloud Console without exposing the secret itself.
- Map the Google error JSON to a human hint appended to the thrown message: invalid_client → check that CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET come from the same OAuth Client and haven't been rotated; invalid_grant → code expired/reused, try again; redirect_uri_ mismatch → URI not whitelisted in GCP.

66/66 tests still green; lint + build clean.

body:
## Análise

Run 24737450282 falhou (post-PR #33 merge). shadow_diff.py exit 1 via polars.exceptions.ComputeError:
\`\`\`
cannot compare string with numeric type (i64)
\`\`\`

Após fix de case (#33), column names alinharam (Python lowercase = Go lowercase). Mas tipos divergem:

| Coluna | Python (fdb+polars) | Go struct | Resultado |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP_UNID_ID | i64 (seed INTEGER) | string (parquet tag) | **type mismatch** |
| DATA_NASC | Date (seed DATE) | string (parquet tag) | **type mismatch** |
| CG_HORAAMB/OUTR/HOSP | i64 | int64 | OK |
| CPF_PROF, NOME_PROF, etc | str | string | OK |

Go struct em \`apps/dump_agent_go/internal/extractor/rows.go\` declara TPUnidID + DataNasc como \`string\`. Seed tinha INTEGER/DATE.

## Fix

Seed DDL alinhado a expectativa Go:
- TP_UNID_ID INTEGER → VARCHAR(3) (zero-padded '01'-'99')
- DATA_NASC DATE → VARCHAR(10) (ISO8601 'YYYY-MM-DD')

Regenerado cnes_seed.sql determinístico. Manifest sha256 atualizado: cd0bd23f668c94ae.

## Nota latent bug

Real FB CNES production tem TP_UNID_ID INTEGER + DATA_NASC DATE. Go extractor vai falhar scan → string em produção. Fix real requer mudança no Go rows.go ou SQL CAST na extração. Fora do escopo desta PR — cobrir em spec futura.

## Streak impact

Reseta para 0 (todas runs anteriores com diff mascarado ou diff real). Próximos 3 success genuínos → cleanup trigger.

author: bendstaples7
body:
## Fix quote draft numbers, AI line item hallucination, and broken request images

### Problem

Three issues found while reviewing a recent quote for Marisa Jones:

1. **"Quote Draft D-undefined"** — Draft numbers displayed as `D-undefined` on both the draft detail page and the drafts list because `draftNumber` was defined in the `QuoteDraft` TypeScript interface but never stored in the database or populated by the backend.

2. **Irrelevant line items (utility sink)** — The AI generated a "Plumbing: Install Utility Sink" line item for a request that had nothing to do with plumbing. The system prompt was too permissive — it told the AI to "prefer line items from similar past quotes" and to "use template line items as a starting point," which caused it to pull in unrelated catalog items.

3. **Broken request images** — Images from Jobber requests showed as broken links on the quote draft page. The stored image URLs are AWS S3 presigned URLs with a 72-hour expiration (`X-Amz-Expires=259200`). By the time the draft page loaded and fetched request details, the URLs had expired.

### Changes

**Draft numbers (`0014_draft_number.sql`, `quote-draft-service.ts`, `quote-engine.ts`)**
- New migration adds `draft_number` column to `quote_drafts` and backfills existing rows with sequential per-user numbers
- `QuoteDraftService.save()` generates the next sequential number per user via `MAX(draft_number) + 1`
- `mapDraftRow()` populates `draftNumber` from the database
- All 5 SELECT queries updated to include `draft_number`
- `QuoteEngine.buildDraft()` sets a placeholder `draftNumber: 0` (real number assigned by the service on save)

**AI prompt (`quote-engine.ts`)**
- Added critical constraint: "Do NOT include line items for work the customer did not ask about"
- Changed template instruction to only include relevant items and remove ones that don't apply
- Changed similar quotes from "prefer their line items" to "use them only as pricing references"
- Added guidance for vague requests: generate fewer items with lower confidence rather than guessing

**Image URLs (`quotes.ts`)**
- `GET /jobber/requests/:id` now re-fetches fresh attachment URLs from the Jobber GraphQL API instead of serving stale stored ones
- Fresh URLs are written back to D1 so other consumers benefit
- 5-second `Promise.race` timeout prevents the Jobber API call from blocking the response
- Graceful fallback to stored URLs if the API call fails or times out

### Testing

- All 164 tests pass (unit + property)
- Client builds clean
- Pre-existing worker build errors (unrelated to these changes) remain unchanged

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->
---
## Summary by cubic
Fixes broken draft numbers, filters out unrelated line items in generated quotes, and restores request images by refreshing expired URLs with safe timeout and fallback.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Draft numbers: added per-user `draft_number`; atomic assignment via `INSERT ... SELECT MAX(draft_number)+1`; `UNIQUE(user_id, draft_number)` ensures no duplicates; retries up to 3 times on constraint errors; drafts display like D-001 instead of D-undefined.
  - Line items: tightened system prompt to only include work explicitly requested; templates only when relevant; similar quotes used as pricing references; fewer items with lower confidence when requests are vague.
  - Request images: `GET /jobber/requests/:id` re-fetches fresh attachment URLs from Jobber GraphQL, updates stored URLs, races with a 5s timeout, uses `c.executionCtx.waitUntil` on timeout, and falls back to stored URLs only if the refresh fails (not when a successful refresh returns zero images).

- **Migration**
  - Run `0014_draft_number.sql` to add and backfill `draft_number`, and create `UNIQUE(user_id, draft_number)`.

<sup>Written for commit d903414e84e960e1010f75f65bed51cc8436773e. Summary will update on new commits.</sup>

## Summary

- Phase 5 is the verification and decisions-log phase; this PR captures the results of every T5.2 negative test, summarises the T5.1 end-to-end dogfood evidence, and writes the T5.3 resolved-decisions table that future changes can refer to.
- One concrete fix shipped alongside the record: the PreToolUse hook now blocks pushes from branches whose names violate the project regex, closing a gap where lefthook silently skipped its pre-push guard for pushes without file changes.

## Changes

- `.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-git.sh` — new rule: block `git push` when the current branch is neither `main` nor a match for the naming regex. Placed after the existing push-to-main block so error messages stay specific.
- `docs/git-workflow-implementation.md` — new "Phase 5 — Verification record" section containing:
  - T5.1 end-to-end dry-run evidence (PRs #1/#2/#3/#4/#10)
  - T5.2 negative-test matrix with captured command, blocker, and output for each scenario
  - T5.2 findings + fixes (the new hook rule; the compound-invocation limitation documented rather than patched)
  - T5.3 resolved-decisions table

body:
## Problem

OSMap ≤ 5.1.3 has a bug in `Factory::getTable()`: `Table::getInstance()` returns `false` when the table class is not found, but the return type is declared as `?Table` (nullable). PHP 8.1+ throws a `TypeError` as a result.

The live site has OSMap **5.1.3** installed — the bug is active.

## Solution

Added `patchOsmapFactory()` to the existing `script.php`. Runs on `install` and `update`.

```php
// before (OSMap ≤ 5.1.3)
return Table::getInstance($tableName, $prefix);

// after
return Table::getInstance($tableName, $prefix) ?: null;
```

**Idempotent:** OSMap ≥ 5.1.4 already contains the fix — `str_replace` finds nothing, no harm done. Works with both OSMap Free and Pro (same file path).

## Changes

- `j2commerce/plg_osmap_j2commerce/script.php` — added `patchOsmapFactory()`
- `j2commerce/plg_osmap_j2commerce/README.md` — documented the fix in Requirements and Troubleshooting

## Problem
Order status could be changed to any value without restrictions,
allowing invalid transitions like `completed → create`.

## Solution
Added allowed transitions map in `update_order_status`:

Raises `InvalidOrderTransitionError` (400) if transition is not allowed.

body:
# Ticket(s) Closed

- Part of #4152
- Stacked on top of #4829

## What

Fourth PR in the 5-PR MPP chain — the first one that actually flips MPP on end-to-end for `AggregateScan`. Wires the MPP plan bridge, DSM coordinator, and customscan glue into the aggregate custom scan so scalar and GROUP BY aggregates on binary joins execute through Partial → hash-shuffle → FinalPartitioned → Gather when `paradedb.enable_mpp = on`. `JoinScan` still errors on the `JoinOnly` shape — that lands in 5/5 (#4807).

**Review as a stacked PR.** This PR targets `moe/mpp-03-assembly` (#4829). When the earlier PRs merge, GitHub auto-retargets this to `main`.

## Why

Previous PRs in the chain (#4827, #4828, #4829) added the primitives, operators, and plan assembly, but none of them had a production caller. This PR connects those pieces to the aggregate custom scan so the existing `aggregate_join_*` benchmarks can actually take the MPP path. The default stays `enable_mpp = off`, so behaviour is unchanged for any caller that doesn't opt in; turning it on is what lights up the ~2.7× win we've been measuring on `aggregate_join_topk_count`.

## How

- `mpp/coordinator.rs` — DSM estimate/init, worker attach, `MppExecutionState` lifecycle.
- `mpp/customscan_glue.rs` — `mpp_is_active`, `mpp_worker_count`, plan-broadcast helpers.
- `mpp/exec_bridge.rs` — `build_mpp_physical_plan` dispatcher + per-shape bridges (`scalar_agg_on_binary_join`, `groupby_agg_on_binary_join`, plus helper walkers).
- `aggregatescan/*` — `ParallelQueryCapable` impl, DSM hooks, `stash_plan_for_mpp`, `classify_logical_plan`, `bake_logical_plan`, MPP routing in `exec_custom_scan`, session context branch in `datafusion_exec`.
- `hook.rs` — new `add_upper_path` helper that Gather-wraps parallel-aware upper-rel paths so MPP Final aggregate results flow to the leader.
- `joinscan/scan_state.rs` — `build_base_session_with_mpp` + profile helpers consumed by AggregateScan's join subtree (skips `SortMergeJoinEnforcer` and disables `enable_join_dynamic_filter_pushdown` when `total_participants > 1`).
- Benchmark SQL — MPP alt variants for `aggregate_join_count`, `aggregate_join_groupby`, `aggregate_join_multi`, `aggregate_join_topk_count`, `aggregate_sort`.

## Tests

- `cargo check -p pg_search --features pg18` clean.
- `cargo test -p pg_search --lib mpp:: --features pg18` green.
- `cargo pgrx regress pg18 mpp` green (`mpp_smoke`, `mpp_fallback`, `mpp_exec`).
- Existing `aggregate_custom_scan` / `join_custom_scan` regress tests unchanged with `enable_mpp = off`.
- Local 25 M `aggregate_join_groupby` bench completes under 10 s with correct row counts; CI bench on the chain tip (#4807) shows the MPP variants beating DataFusion.

## Summary

Implements the complete capture-scene command handler for Feature 216 (Storyboarding — Capture), enabling analysts to freeze map state with a single keystroke (`Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+C`). The implementation includes the command orchestration layer, per-scene thumbnail service, storyboard panel UI, and comprehensive test coverage.

## Key Changes

### Command Handler (`captureScene.ts`)

- Integrates with #215's CRUD module for scene creation and duplicate-timestamp resolution
- Provides dependency injection for testability (VS Code APIs, thumbnail service, ULID generation)

### Thumbnail Service (`sceneThumbnailService.ts`)
- Writes scene thumbnails atomically (large 800×600 and small 200×150 PNGs)
- Implements atomic write pattern: tmp file → fsync → rename
- Merges STAC asset entries into `item.json` with proper error handling
- Validates STAC item structure and ULID format
- Orphans partial files on failure (harmless since scene is never created)

### Storyboard Panel UI
- **`StoryboardPanel.tsx`**: Presentational component displaying scene list with empty states

- Registered `debrief.captureScene` command in package.json with camera icon

- **`captureScene.test.ts`** (15 tests): Command handler control-flow branches, duplicate resolution, error cases

### Background Auto-Sync
- Added startup auto-sync thread that runs incremental LDA filing sync and newsletter scraping

- Ad scraper uses deduplication by destination domain to avoid capturing duplicate ads
- Screenshots are base64-encoded for storage and transmission

author: dragoangel
body:
### Problem

Every TCP connection to the fuzzy worker is rejected with refusing TCP connection from <ip> (blacklisted) regardless of configuration. A freshly started worker with no blocked map, no dynamic_blocked_nets entries, and no blocked_ip configured still refuses every TCP client at accept time. UDP traffic is unaffected.

### Root

The TCP accept path at fuzzy_storage.c:2377 inverted the semantics with !:


if (!rspamd_fuzzy_check_client(ctx, addr)) { /* log "(blacklisted)" and close */ }
!0 == true, so every ALLOWED client entered the reject branch; !503 == false, so actually-blocked clients would slip through.

author: andreagrandi
body:
## Summary

- Sentry alert [113870246](https://andrea-grandi.sentry.io/issues/113870246/) fired when the scheduled `post_random_library` job hit a Bluesky read timeout. Captured locals (`attempt = 1, last_exc = None`) show `_post_with_retry` re-raised on the first attempt instead of retrying.
- Root cause: `_is_transient_error()` only matched `requests` exceptions. The Bluesky path uses `atproto_client` → `httpx`, so its timeouts fell through and surfaced as a user-visible error for a purely transient failure.
- Fix: teach the helper about `httpx.TimeoutException` / `httpx.TransportError` and `atproto_client.exceptions.NetworkError` (the parent of `InvokeTimeoutError`). I intentionally did **not** use the wider `RequestErrorBase` — a failing test proved it would also swallow `BadRequestError` / `UnauthorizedError`, which must not retry.
- Added four unit tests covering `httpx.ReadTimeout`, `httpx.ConnectError`, atproto `InvokeTimeoutError` (all transient) and atproto `BadRequestError` (explicitly non-transient, so the helper can't silently widen).

## Test plan

- [x] `nox -s tests -- libraries/test_social_post.py::TestIsTransientError libraries/test_social_post.py::TestPostWithRetry -v` — 14 passed

## Project

[ag2](https://github.com/ag2ai/ag2)

## Checklist

- [x] One project per PR
- [x] PR title format: `Add project-name`
- [x] Entry format: `- [project-name](url) - Description ending with period.`

## Why This Project Is Awesome

Which criterion does it meet? (pick one)

- [x] **Industry Standard** - The go-to tool for a specific use case
- [ ] **Rising Star** - 5000+ stars in < 2 years, significant adoption
- [ ] **Hidden Gem** - Exceptional quality, solves niche problems elegantly

Explain:

AG2 (positioned as "the Open-Source AgentOS") is one of the primary Python frameworks for building and orchestrating multi-agent AI systems. It has 4.4k+ GitHub stars, a published PyPI package (`ag2`), dedicated documentation at [docs.ag2.ai](https://docs.ag2.ai/latest/), and active, frequent releases.

AG2 originated as the AutoGen codebase and continued as an independent, community-governed project under the `ag2ai` organization from late 2024 onward, now with its own maintainers, release line, and roadmap. It pioneered several patterns that are now standard across the agent-framework ecosystem (GroupChat for multi-agent conversations, structured human-in-the-loop workflows, tool/function-calling abstractions across LLM providers), and remains a go-to choice for teams specifically building multi-agent conversational systems in Python.

The project is also actively evolving: the recent [AG2 Beta](https://docs.ag2.ai/0.12.0/docs/beta/motivation/) introduces an event-driven architecture designed around emerging agent standards — native support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A), and AG-UI — plus stronger context and memory primitives, new multi-agent coordination patterns, and cleaner integration with Text UI, web, ambient, and background runtimes. AG2 Beta agents remain backward-compatible with AG2 multi-agent interaction patterns from day one, enabling gradual adoption.
