author: calnightingale
body: ## What was broken Diffusion-weighted MR series (and other 4D/dynamic studies) with de-identified or otherwise-malformed rescale metadata rendered as a completely black viewport. Scrolling/cine behaved normally, pixel data streamed in fine, but the window/level fell entirely outside the rendered pixel range → all pixels clipped to black. - **Who hit it:** dynamic (4D) volumes that cornerstone splits by a `splittingTag` (e.g. DWI series split by DiffusionBValue, producing N×32 instances with a 1/N dimension-group selector in the cine bar). - **Modalities/modes observed:** MR DWI/ADC series (4D streaming dynamic volume). By extension, any dynamic volume where DICOM metadata says `WindowCenter`/`WindowWidth` exist but `RescaleSlope` is missing or otherwise bogus. - **Viewport types affected:** volume viewports specifically (stack rendering was already covered by DQ-344). ## Root cause Cornerstone's `setDefaultVolumeVOI` prefers metadata `WW`/`WC` when both are present on the series' middle image. For de-identified series the metadata often has `RescaleIntercept=32768` plus a missing `RescaleSlope`, and the de-id tool has already shifted the signed pixel data into unsigned-looking integers. The net effect: - GPU texture ends up with pixel values in the actual rescaled/shifted space (e.g. `Int16Array` whose values happen to read `[-32768, -25327]` or `Uint16Array` `[32768, 42437]`, depending on how the loader typed the buffer). - `voiRange` ends up in the unrelated metadata space (e.g. `[0, 644]`). - No overlap between window and data → fully black. DQ-344's existing stack-viewport auto-windowing didn't cover this path because dynamic volumes go through `setVolumesForViewport`, not the stack path. Cornerstone's own middle-slice pixel-sampling fallback inside `setDefaultVolumeVOI` is _skipped_ when any WC/WW is present, so the volume path doesn't self-heal for this class of bad metadata. ## The fix Targeted auto-windowing for **dynamic volume viewports only**, in `CornerstoneViewportService.setVolumesForViewport`: 1. When a viewport's underlying volume is a dynamic volume (`volume.isDynamicVolume()` is true), attach a one-shot listener for `Events.IMAGE_VOLUME_LOADING_COMPLETED`. 2. When the event fires, sample raw typed-array pixel values from ~8 cached images across the volume, skipping 1 sample per ~10k pixels per image. This gives us `[min, max]` in **exactly the same numeric space as the GPU texture** — including signedness — which is critical because `image.minPixelValue`/`maxPixelValue` can disagree with the underlying `Int16Array`/`Uint16Array`'s actual values for these series. 3. If the viewport's current `voiRange` overlaps the sampled `[min, max]` at all, leave it alone. 4. Otherwise, override `voiRange` to the full sampled span (no percentile-based outlier rejection — simpler, and adequate for making the image visible) and show the same "Auto-Windowing Applied" notification DQ-344 added. Scope choices and why: - **Dynamic-only gate.** Regular volumes self-heal via cornerstone's pixel-sampling fallback. An earlier version of this fix applied to all volume viewports and broke 3D four-up rendering on a series that previously rendered fine — a post-load `setProperties({ voiRange })` on a non-dynamic volume's 3D viewport races cornerstone's opacity/transfer-function setup. Dynamic volumes don't have that post-setup behavior to conflict with. - **Defer to `IMAGE_VOLUME_LOADING_COMPLETED`.** Sampling immediately after `setVolumes` resolves returns no data (streaming is still in flight), causing the override to skip. Waiting for full load completion guarantees enough pixel data is cached. - **Sample raw typed arrays instead of `voxelManager.getRange()`.** We saw cases where `getRange()` returned `[32768, 42437]` (from `image.minPixelValue`/`maxPixelValue`) while the underlying array was `Int16Array` with values `[-32768, -25327]`. Setting `voiRange` in the former space produces black when the GPU reads the latter. - **Only override on zero overlap.** Keeps us out of the way when cornerstone's VOI is already sane. ## Test plan The production links below reproduce the bug and the regression-guard behavior against the hosted atlas. To verify against this branch locally, serve it with any config that exposes the two data sources used below (`thryothor-495511-pacs-deid/v1.0` and `clanga-65737-pacs-deid/v1.0`) and swap the `https://.../atlas/viewer/` prefix for your local equivalent. If your buckets require auth, OHIF accepts a bearer token via `?token=` on the viewer URL (see `platform/app/src/routes/Mode/Mode.tsx`). **proc-1327 — the broken series** All black in current prod: ``` https://gradienthealth.github.io/atlas/viewer/thryothor-495511-pacs-deid/v1.0?StudyInstanceUIDs=1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.86114562220811432313310407692399345798&SeriesInstanceUIDs=1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.90424059860696909766753998803465688785&leftPanelEnabled=false&rightPanelEnabled=false ``` If you try this locally from this branch instead (e.g. `yarn run dev; localhost:3000`), renders properly: **PROC-1353 / DQ-327 — regression guard** Works in prod: ``` https://gradienthealth.github.io/atlas/viewer/clanga-65737-pacs-deid/v1.0?StudyInstanceUIDs=1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.20741711644969544194990188373071960880&SeriesInstanceUIDs=1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.66105338337151112057194521604603724565&leftPanelEnabled=false&rightPanelEnabled=false ``` Still works locally ### Checklist - [ ] proc-1327: default stack view renders; "Auto-Windowing Applied" notification appears. - [ ] proc-1327: switch to 3D four-up — all 4 panels render. - [ ] PROC-1353 / DQ-327: default stack view renders with auto-windowing notification (existing DQ-344 behavior, unchanged). - [ ] PROC-1353 / DQ-327: switch to 3D four-up — renders correctly, **no** new notification fires, no black screen. - [ ] Pick any previously-working series in the atlas with normal metadata — confirm no regression, no spurious notifications. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: rocksbrothers-png
body:
### Motivation

- Ensure Tesseract+pytesseract OCR is present and validated at build/runtime to avoid broken deployments on Render.  
- Support richer/safer QR payloads for stock items (JSON payloads, simple numeric patterns and raw codes) and allow lookup by stock item id.  
- Improve client-side QR scanning UX with clearer feedback, a close-camera control and deterministic payload resolution.

### Description

- Dockerfile: set `OCR_REQUIRED=1`, echo a build marker, install Tesseract and Portuguese language, and run runtime validations (`tesseract --version`, `pip show pytesseract`, `python -m scripts.check_ocr_runtime.py --require`) during build; change `CMD` to run `scripts/check_ocr_runtime.py --require` before starting `server_postgres.py`.
- `render.yaml`: propagate `OCR_REQUIRED` environment variable for Render deployments.
- Add `scripts/check_ocr_runtime.py`: new CLI that queries `get_ocr_runtime_status()`, reports structured diagnostics (plain or `--json`), detects Render vs local env, and can `--require` OCR (exit non-zero) or allow missing OCR locally with `--allow-missing-local`.
- `server_postgres.py`: add `parse_stock_qr_lookup_value()` to normalize and parse stock QR payloads (JSON payloads, `EPIITEM:123` simplified pattern, and raw codes), integrate it into `/api/stock/lookup-qr` to accept either `stock_item_id` or `qr_code` in the query and adjust SQL to match by id or `LOWER(qr_code_value)`; add diagnostic `print()` logs and small signature handling cleanup; import `unicodedata`.
- `static/app.js` and `static/index.html`/`styles.css`: add `resolveStockQrPayload()` to interpret scanned input, send `stock_item_id` and normalized `qr_code` to the lookup API, add console logs/warnings for rejected scans, add a camera-close button and CSS positioning, alter behavior to stop camera only when a session was applied, and change QR label print to embed JSON payload in the QR image source.

### Testing

- Ran backend test suite with `pytest`; all tests passed.  
- Verified the OCR runtime checker by running `python scripts/check_ocr_runtime.py --json` locally and in a simulated Render env, which produced expected structured diagnostics.  
- Performed frontend build/check (static assets) and exercised the delivery QR lookup flow in a local dev server to confirm QR parsing, API lookup by id/code, and UI camera close behavior succeeded.

author: upetit
body:
## Summary
- Subagents run in isolated pydantic-ai contexts, so the primary's `get_current_time` tool result doesn't propagate. In a live session this caused `deep_research` to issue web searches without the current year, returning stale-dated results.
- Add `current_time_fragment()` helper and register it on each agent (`primary`, `deep_research`, `draft_longform`) via `agent.system_prompt(...)`. pydantic-ai recomputes dynamic system-prompt callables on every `agent.run()`, so long-lived agent instances can't drift and subagents no longer need a `get_current_time` round-trip before time-sensitive work.
- Doc commit captures two operational notes from a v1→v2 deployment migration: runtime config location (`~/.kore/config.json` + docker volume) and the `get_tools(["*"])` wildcard gotcha.

- [x] `pytest tests/test_system_prompts.py -v` — 4/4 pass (helper + one injection test per agent)

author: kdelemme
body:
Resolves https://github.com/elastic/rna-program/issues/412

## Summary

Records each dispatcher decision as an `event_log` entry instead, so we reuse the shared bulk writer, ILM, REST API, and saved-object-based authz.

- Adds `kibana.alerting_v2.*` fields to the event_log schema (`scripts/mappings.js` + regenerated `generated/mappings.json` / `generated/schemas.ts`).
- Registers a new `alerting_v2` provider with actions `dispatched` / `throttled` / `unmatched` (outcome lives in `event.action`, not a custom field).
- New `StoreExecutionHistoryStep` (step 11) writes one event per `(rule × policy × episode)` via `IEventLogger`. Each event carries rule + action_policy saved-object refs as `rel: primary`, so searching by either SO returns the event. Unmatched episodes get just the rule ref.
- `Rule.kind` ('alert' | 'signal') is now hydrated by `FetchRulesStep` and used as `kibana.saved_objects[].type_id` on rule refs, matching the existing alerting plugin convention.


## Testing

Create a rule, create an action policy with a workflow, check the logs after a while:

```
FROM .kibana-event-log* | WHERE event.provider == "alerting_v2" | STATS count_action = count(*) BY event.action
```

author: ronfed
body:
The detector's `TrackProcesses` function can be called before the eBPF probes are fully loaded.
This caused a panic in
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x8 pc=0x4f65f8]

goroutine 73 [running]:
github.com/odigos-io/runtime-detector/internal/probe.(*Probe).TrackPIDs(0x786408335ba8?, {0x786408676b60, 0x2, 0x786408676b60?})
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/odigos-io/runtime-detector@v0.0.24/internal/probe/probe.go:413 +0x28
github.com/odigos-io/runtime-detector.(*Detector).TrackProcesses(0x7864082625e8?, {0x786408676b60?, 0x2b10d48?, 0x7864078bd900?})
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/odigos-io/runtime-detector@v0.0.24/detector.go:364 +0x28
```

This PR adds support for this case by checking if the probes are loaded or not, and if they are not - save the tracked processes passed by the called in a pending slice - which will be added to the eBPF maps once the probes are loaded.

CORE-930

author: copilot
body:
The medication interaction warning flow was not surfacing alerts because seeded interactions were missing in empty/dev environments. The diagnosis flow also forced doctors to recreate ICD entries instead of reusing a shared catalog, and there was no management UI for diagnosis/interactions.

- **Diagnosis catalog reuse**
  - Search now resolves against reusable catalog diagnoses by **code or description** instead of only ad hoc consult-linked records.
  - Creating a diagnosis returns an existing catalog match when one already exists, avoiding duplicate ICD entries.
  - Consultation finalization now **copies** the selected catalog diagnosis into the consultation record, preserving per-consult history without consuming the shared catalog entry.

- **Medication interaction seeding**
  - Added an incremental Liquibase changelog to seed common drug interactions idempotently in `faker` environments.
  - Matching is tolerant of medication display names that include dosage suffixes (`Amoxicilina 500mg`, `Ibuprofeno 400mg`, etc.), so alerts can populate from existing sample data.
  - Interaction creation/update now rejects self-pairs and duplicate A/B or B/A combinations.

- **New management surfaces**
  - Added a **Diagnósticos** catalog view for both **Administrador** and **Médico** to create, edit, search, and reuse shared diagnosis definitions.
  - Added an **Interacciones** management view for **Administrador** only to register and remove medication interaction rules.
  - Updated routes and sidebar navigation to expose the new modules under the correct role boundaries.

- **Frontend diagnosis integration**
  - Unified diagnosis mapping in the frontend service layer so both search and create flows use the same `codigoCIE`/`descripcion` model.
  - The doctor consultation screen now consumes the shared catalog directly, so selecting or creating a diagnosis behaves consistently across consultations.

Example of the new consultation persistence behavior:

```java
Diagnostico diagnosticoConsulta = new Diagnostico();
diagnosticoConsulta.setCodigoCIE(diag.getCodigoCIE());
diagnosticoConsulta.setDescripcion(diag.getDescripcion());
diagnosticoConsulta.setConsulta(consulta);
diagnosticoRepository.save(diagnosticoConsulta);
```

This keeps the catalog reusable while still attaching a diagnosis snapshot to each completed consultation.

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a `Build APK` GitHub Actions workflow to `EldritchPortals`, mirroring the existing EldritchPortal pipeline so APK builds can be triggered consistently in this repository. The previous workflow file was effectively empty.

- **Workflow added (`.github/workflows/build-apk.yml`)**
  - Configures triggers for:
    - pushes to `main`
    - manual dispatch with `clean_build` input (`true|false`)
  - Sets `contents: write` to allow release publishing.

- **Android build environment setup**
  - Uses Python 3.9 + OpenJDK 17.
  - Installs required system packages.
  - Rebuilds and installs `libtool 2.4.6` (matching the reference workflow).
  - Installs `buildozer` and `cython<3.0`.

- **Build, cache, and distribution**
  - Adds cache for `~/.buildozer` keyed by `buildozer.spec` and `clean_build`.
  - Supports optional clean rebuild by removing `~/.buildozer`.
  - Builds debug APK via Buildozer.
  - Uploads `bin/*.apk` as an artifact.
  - Creates a prerelease using version from `buildozer.spec` and workflow run number.

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      clean_build:
        type: choice
        options: ["true", "false"]
```

author: yorickyeng
body:
## 🚨 Выявленные Антипаттерны

### 1. **God Class (Божественный класс)**
Класс нарушает **Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)**, выполняя 7 различных ответственностей:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│          GodDiscountCalculator                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. Хранение состояния расчёта (9 полей-переменных)      │
│ 2. Получение данных из репозиториев                     │
│ 3. Расчёт скидок по категориям товаров                  │
│ 4. Расчёт объёмных скидок по порогу                     │
│ 5. Расчёт налогов                                       │
│ 6. Расчёт стоимости доставки                            │
│ 7. Расчёт комиссий платежных методов                    │
│ 8. Форматирование и вывод отчёта в консоль              │
│ 9. Быстрая оценка стоимости (quickEstimate)             │
│ 10. Экспорт в строку (exportToString)                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 2. **Feature Envy**
Метод `calculateAndPrint` чрезмерно использует данные из `ProductRepository` и `CartRepository`, но логика принадлежит доменной области, а не презентации.

### 3. **Primitive Obsession**
Использование примитивных типов (`Double`, `String`) вместо доменных объектов:
```kotlin
private val TAX_RATE = 0.13                    // Должно быть Money/TaxRate
private val DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD_1 = 5000.0      // Должно быть Money
private val SHIPPING_BASE = 300.0              // Должно быть Money
```

### 4. **Magic Numbers**
Числовые литералы без пояснений:
```kotlin
private val TAX_RATE = 0.13           // Почему 13%?
private val CARD_COMMISSION = 0.02    // Откуда 2%?
private val WEIGHT_PER_ITEM = 0.5     // Почему 0.5 кг?
```

### 5. **Data Clump**
Группы связанных полей, которые должны быть объектом:
```kotlin
// Эти 7 полей должны быть классом CalculationResult:
private var subtotal = 0.0
private var categoryDiscount = 0.0
private var volumeDiscount = 0.0
private var tax = 0.0
private var shipping = 0.0
private var commission = 0.0
private var finalTotal = 0.0
```

### 6. **Temporal Coupling**
Методы зависят от порядка вызова:
```kotlin
fun calculateAndPrint(paymentMethod: String) {  // Должен вызываться первым
    // ... устанавливает все поля
}

fun exportToString(): String {  // Требует предварительного вызова calculateAndPrint
    return "SUBTOTAL:${subtotal};..."  // Использует поля, установленные выше
}
```

### 7. **Inappropriate Intimacy**
Класс знает слишком много о внутренней структуре `CartItem` и `Product`:
```kotlin
val cartItems = cart.getItems().map { cartItem ->
    val product = productMap[cartItem.product.id] ?: cartItem.product
    Pair(product, cartItem.amount)  // Прямой доступ к внутренностям
}
```

### 8. **Switch Statements (When-выражения)**
Длинные when-выражения, которые должны быть полиморфизмом:
```kotlin
val catDiscount = when (product.category) {
    Category.SNOWBOARDS -> SNOWBOARDS_DISCOUNT
    Category.BINDINGS -> BINDINGS_DISCOUNT
    Category.BOOTS -> BOOTS_DISCOUNT
    // ... 7 случаев
}
```

### 9. **Hardcoded Values**
Жестко закодированные значения конфигурации:
```kotlin
private val SNOWBOARDS_DISCOUNT = 0.10
private val BINDINGS_DISCOUNT = 0.05
private val BOOTS_DISCOUNT = 0.07
// ... должны быть в конфигурации
```

### 10. **Mixed Concerns (Смешение ответственностей)**
Класс находится в пакете `presentation.console`, но содержит бизнес-логику:
```
presentation.console.GodDiscountCalculator
    ├── Репозитории (domain layer)
    ├── Бизнес-правила расчёта (domain layer)
    └── Вывод в консоль (presentation layer)
```

### 11. **Mutable State**
Изменяемое состояние приводит к ошибкам:
```kotlin
private var subtotal = 0.0    // Может быть изменено
private var tax = 0.0         // Зависит от порядка вызовов
```

### 12. **Poor Naming**
- `GodDiscountCalculator` — имя само признаёт проблему
- `calculateAndPrint` — нарушает Single Responsibility
- `quickEstimate` — неясное назначение

---

## 📊 Метрики класса

| Метрика | Значение | Порог | Статус |
|---------|----------|-------|--------|
| Lines of Code (LOC) | 120 | < 50 | ❌ |
| Number of Fields | 22 | < 10 | ❌ |
| Number of Methods | 4 | < 5 | ⚠️ |
| Coupling (CBO) | 2 репозитория + Category | < 3 | ⚠️ |
| Responsibility Count | 7+ | < 3 | ❌ |

---

## 🛠️ Рекомендации по Рефакторингу

### Стратегия разделения:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    После рефакторинга                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │

author: pierrci
body:
we had an internal cron (`inference-providers-validate-mappings`) stuck for 5 days due to it waiting indefinitely for a fetch to complete

according to codex, this wouldn't have happened if the abort signal was passed downstream properly - this is what this PR is trying to do

[traces (internal)](https://traces.com/s/jn7b42b1herx47tt7nkfcrpfex858ttk)

---

[![Compound Engineering](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built_with-Compound_Engineering-6366f1)](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin)
![Codex](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPT_5-000000)


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches many provider `getResponse`/polling code paths and the shared `delay` utility to add abort support; changes are mostly additive but could affect request cancellation behavior and type signatures across providers.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds end-to-end **AbortSignal propagation** across inference tasks so cancellations stop provider polling loops and downstream asset downloads.
> 
> This threads an optional `signal` through `TaskProviderHelper.getResponse` and relevant task helper interfaces, updates multiple providers (e.g. Fal.ai, Black Forest Labs, Replicate, WaveSpeed, Novita, ZAI, HF-Inference, etc.) to pass `signal` into `fetch` and polling `delay` calls, and makes `delay(ms, signal)` abort-aware.
> 
> Updates task entrypoints (e.g. `textToImage`, `textToVideo`, `imageToImage`, `textToSpeech`, `automaticSpeechRecognition`, `imageToText`) to forward `options.signal`, and adds a Vitest suite (`provider-abort-signal.spec.ts`) to verify aborts prevent/interrupt polling fetches and input downloads.

body:
## Summary
Closes #777 (ASQ-004). Part of the Quality Program.

Phase 1 (#1158) landed measurement tooling and micro-wins. Phase 2 delivers the real target: **p95 of `build_monthly_grid` down 69% on synthetic production-scale data, blowing past the ticket's ≥40% ask.**

## Numbers (bench_monthly_grid, 30 formadores × 210 events × 50 blocks, April 2026)

|                 | before phase 2 | after phase 2 | delta |
|-----------------|---------------:|--------------:|------:|
| min             |     33.4 ms   |    21.4 ms   |  −36% |
| p50             |     34.0 ms   |    22.2 ms   |  **−35%** |
| p95             |     88.2 ms   |    27.2 ms   |  **−69%** |
| p99             |     91.8 ms   |    60.8 ms   |  −34% |
| mean            |     39.7 ms   |    24.7 ms   |  −38% |
| queries/call    |          6    |         6    |    — |

Generated via `python manage.py bench_monthly_grid --year 2026 --month 4 --role FORMADOR --iterations 20 --warmup 3 --json` (command landed in phase 1).

## What changed in `services/monthly_grid_service.py`

1. **Dropped `prefetch_related(Prefetch("participations", …))` on events.** The RelatedManager materialization + `.all()` iteration per event was the dominant cost — Django was building ORM objects for every participant. Replaced with a single `Participation.objects.filter(...).values_list("solicitacao_id", "usuario_id")` that feeds a flat `event_to_users: dict[int, list[int]]` index. Query count stays at 6.

2. **Flattened the nested accumulator.** `user_data[uid]["events_by_day"][day_num]` became three flat dicts keyed by `(uid, day_num)`: `events_by_user_day`, `blocks_by_user_day`, `desloc_by_user_day`, plus `ch_month_by_user` / `ch_year_by_user`. Three dict lookups per write become one.

3. **Clamped the day loops** to the month boundary (`first_day` / `last_day`) before iterating, eliminating the per-iteration `if current.month == month and current.year == year` check.

4. **Replaced `Usuario.objects.filter(id__in=…)` with `.values("id", "first_name", …)`** — the grid only reads name/email/username, so the full ORM model wasn't paying for itself.

5. **Removed** the now-unused `_init_user_data()` helper and the `Prefetch` import.

## Contract preserved
The 10 monthly-grid tests (`test_availability_monthly_api.py`, `test_monthly_with_deslocamento.py`) all pass unchanged. Response JSON shape (`days`, `legend`, `people[]`, `cells[][]`, `details_index{}`) is byte-compatible.

Speed up `findMatch` by caching per-key metadata (patternIndex,
wildcardPrefix / wildcardSuffix, `isPattern`, `isSubpathMapping`,

author: johnelliott
body:
Hey there, love the app thus far, just using the robots to fix an issue one of my machines and one of my friends machines ran into. I'm presenting this is a potential issue, but of course feel free to use it, copy it, throw it out and redo it yourself if that's your preference.

Problem: Whisper v3 large downloads seem to succeed, but they're not usable.

Fixes #130

  ## Summary
  - HuggingFace appends a `_NNNMB` size suffix to some WhisperKit model directories (e.g. `openai_whisper-large-v3-v20240930_626MB`).
  - Hex's exact-string matching treated the renamed directory as a missing download, so Whisper Large v3 kept retriggering downloads and showing as
  not-installed.
  - Fix adds a tolerant matcher that strips a trailing `_\d+MB` suffix, and updates `models.json` to the current HuggingFace name.

  ## Why
  Currently unreachable for users who already had Whisper Large v3 downloaded — after the HF rename, the app believes the model is gone and re-downloads
  every launch. The fix preserves existing on-disk models and keeps existing glob patterns working by only falling back to suffix-stripping when exact
  match fails.

  ## Changes
  - `HexCore/Sources/HexCore/Logic/ModelPatternMatcher.swift` — add `matchesFlexible` and `stripSizeSuffix`.
  - `Hex/Clients/TranscriptionClient.swift` — add `effectiveModelPath(for:)`; `resolveVariant` now cascades exact -> glob -> size-suffix variant.
  - `Hex/Features/Settings/ModelDownload/ModelDownloadFeature.swift` — route `selectedModelIsDownloaded`, curated-model hydration, and the download-success
   handler through `matchesFlexible`.
  - `Hex/Resources/Data/models.json` — update Whisper Large v3 `internalName` to the current HuggingFace name.

  ## Validation
  - `cd HexCore && swift test`
  - `xcodebuild -scheme Hex -configuration Release CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build`
  - Manual: relaunch with an existing `openai_whisper-large-v3-v20240930_626MB` directory on disk - UI shows "downloaded" and model loads.

  Happy to split this into an issue first if you'd prefer - didn't file one since it's a contained bug fix, but happy to follow the usual flow.

From the commit: 
> HuggingFace appends _NNNMB (e.g. _626MB) to Whisper Large v3's repo name, which broke exact string matching: already-downloaded models appeared missing and the curated entry kept retriggering downloads.
> 
> Add ModelPatternMatcher.matchesFlexible / stripSizeSuffix to treat foo and foo_626MB as the same model, and use flexible matching in ModelDownloadFeature's selected/curated/download-complete paths. Add TranscriptionClient.effectiveModelPath so on-disk lookups fall back to the stripped directory when the exact path is absent, preserving existing downloads. Update models.json to the current HuggingFace name.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * More reliable detection and offline resolution of downloaded models, improved tokenizer discovery, and handling of size-suffixed on-disk folders.
  * Improved variant resolution for exact, stale, and globbed model names.

* **Updates**
  * Whisper Large v3 model identifier updated.

* **New Features**
  * Flexible model-name matching to align catalog, available, and curated entries.

* **Tests**
  * New tests covering flexible matching and size-suffix behavior.

### Description Broken off from #1042 , this PR contains only Vespa-specific changes Adds support for Vespa in OSB. Ingest and query data on other search engines outside of OpenSearch using a new `--database-type` flag

Each engine is a Python module under osbenchmark/engine/<name>/ exposing 5 functions:

Function | Purpose -- | -- create_client_factory | Builds engine-native HTTP/gRPC client create_async_client | Creates async client for worker processes register_runners | Registers engine-specific operation runners wait_for_client | Health-check polling before benchmark starts on_execute_error | Translates engine exceptions to OSB metrics

A lightweight registry (osbenchmark/engine/__init__.py) dispatches --database-type=vespa to the correct module. OpenSearch remains the default and delegates to the existing osbenchmark/client.py and osbenchmark/worker_coordinator/runner.py, those files are untouched.

**Vespa** (`osbenchmark/engine/vespa/`): - Client: pyvespa `httpr` (Rust HTTP) for search, `aiohttp` for document feed - Search: pre-translated YQL required (runners raise `BenchmarkError` if `body["yql"]` missing) - Feed: `feed_batch()` with HTTP/2 multiplexing, configurable `max_concurrent` - HNSW: `hnsw_ef_search` mapped to `targetHits` + `hnsw.exploreAdditionalHits` ## Usage ### Vespa ```bash opensearch-benchmark run \ --pipeline=benchmark-only \ --workload-path= \ --workload-params=params_vespa.json \ --test-procedure=vespa-search-only \ --target-hosts=:8080 \ --database-type=vespa \ --client-options="hnsw_ef_search:256" ``` ### Example params file (works for all engines — adjust `target_index_name` per engine) ```json { "target_index_name": "target_index", "target_field_name": "embedding", "target_index_body": "indices/faiss-index.json", "target_index_primary_shards": 1, "target_index_replica_shards": 0, "target_index_dimension": 768, "target_index_space_type": "innerproduct", "target_index_bulk_size": 500, "target_index_bulk_index_data_set_format": "hdf5", "target_index_bulk_index_data_set_corpus": "cohere-1m", "target_index_bulk_indexing_clients": 10, "target_index_max_num_segments": 1, "hnsw_ef_construction": 200, "hnsw_ef_search": 256, "query_k": 100, "query_data_set_format": "hdf5", "query_data_set_corpus": "cohere-1m", "query_count": 10000, "search_clients": 1, "neighbors_data_set_corpus": "cohere-1m", "neighbors_data_set_format": "hdf5" } ``` ## New Dependencies - **pyvespa** (`pip install pyvespa`) — optional, for Vespa engine - is not required for OpenSearch-only usage (lazy imports, graceful degradation) ### Issues Resolved #1000 ### Testing - [x] New functionality includes testing Unit tests + full E2E test against live Vespa + Milvus nodes. author: tanguille
body:
## Summary

Migrate llama-server to ik_llama.cpp and retune both MoE models for its recommended hybrid CPU/GPU inference pattern. No pod memory bump required.

### Image swap

`ghcr.io/mostlygeek/llama-swap:cuda` → `ghcr.io/ikawrakow/ik-llama-cpp:cu13-swap-4417`

Upstream ships a llama-swap-bundled variant so this is drop-in with no entrypoint changes. The fork specifically targets hybrid CPU+GPU MoE workloads (fused FFN ops, better auto-fit tensor offload).

### MoE tuning (gemma-4 and qwen-3.6)

Both entries switch to the explicit expert-offload pattern:

```
--n-gpu-layers 99
--override-tensor exps=CPU
```

Expert FFN weights stay on CPU; attention, router, embeddings, and KV cache live on the 4070. Per-token hot path is small matmuls in VRAM; experts stream from the OS page cache. Beats auto-fit layer slicing on ≤16 GB GPUs for MoE.

Dropping `--no-mmap` lets the kernel page cache handle expert residency adaptively — MoE access is sparse and clustered so most pages fault once and stay warm. Cold start is faster, the 20 GiB pod memory limit holds, and unload releases pages immediately.

### Per-model changes

- **`gemma-4`**: UD-Q3_K_XL → **UD-Q4_K_M** (ik_llama.cpp refuses the _XL variant's f16 tensors; Q4_K_M matches or exceeds Q3_K_XL quality at similar size)
- **`qwen-3.6`** (new): `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M` with `--top-p 0.95` per Unsloth's Qwen sampling guide
- **Both**: `--threads 6 --threads-batch 6` (experts now on CPU, threading is the bottleneck; matches the 6-CPU cgroup); `--ctx-size 131072` (auto-fit conflicts with explicit tensor placement); `-fmoe` + `-rtr` (ik_llama.cpp-specific fused MoE FFN + runtime repack)
- **`qwen-3.5`**: intentionally untouched — dense 9B, fully GPU-offloaded, different optimization profile. Its `_XL` quant may break on ik_llama.cpp; if reload fails, follow-up PR.

## Test plan

- [ ] Flux reconciles the HelmRelease cleanly; pod restarts with new image
- [ ] `curl http://llama-server/health` reports healthy after cold start
- [ ] `qwen-3.6` loads and completes a chat request (`curl -X POST /v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"qwen-3.6",...}'`)
- [ ] `gemma-4` reloads on first request after image swap (quant changed, expect fresh download of Q4_K_M)
- [ ] `nvidia-smi` during inference shows ~3–5 GB VRAM for weights + KV cache, not the full 12 GB
- [ ] `kubectl top pod` stays under the 20 GiB memory limit with experts mmap'd in page cache
- [ ] `qwen-3.5` still reloads (watch for f16-tensor load error on its `_XL` quant; if so, follow-up)

## Summary
This PR implements the complete chat interface for Phase 2, including real-time messaging via WebSocket (STOMP), message display, chat list management, and user search functionality. The implementation integrates with the existing authentication and state management systems.

## Key Changes

### New Components
- **ChatWindow**: Main chat interface with message display, infinite scroll pagination, and message input with auto-expanding textarea
- **ChatList**: Sidebar showing all chats with search, unread badges, and last message preview
- **NewChatModal**: User search and private chat creation modal with debounced search
- **MessageBubble**: Individual message rendering with sender info, timestamps, edit indicators, and read status placeholders

### Core Features
- **Real-time messaging**: WebSocket subscription per chat using STOMP protocol with automatic message injection into store
- **Cursor-based pagination**: Load older messages with IntersectionObserver sentinel at top of reversed message list
- **Message state management**: Extended `chatStore` with `addMessage` and `prependMessages` actions for real-time and paginated updates
- **User search API**: New `userApi.searchUsers()` endpoint with 300ms debounce in modal
- **Chat creation**: Mutation-based private chat creation with automatic navigation and cache invalidation

### UI/UX Details
- **Flex-col-reverse layout**: Messages container uses reverse flex direction to anchor newest messages at bottom while supporting infinite scroll
- **Auto-expanding textarea**: Input grows up to 128px with smooth height transitions
- **Avatar system**: Deterministic color assignment based on first character of name
- **Time formatting**: Smart relative timestamps (HH:MM for today, "Ayer" for yesterday, weekday/date for older)
- **Loading states**: Skeleton loaders for chat list and spinner indicators for message loading
- **Dark mode support**: Full dark mode styling throughout all components

### Integration Points
- Connected `MainLayout` to use `ChatList` and `ChatWindow` components
- Integrated `useSocket()` hook for WebSocket lifecycle management
- Added `useChatSubscription()` hook for per-chat STOMP topic subscriptions
- Extended `chatStore` with message management actions and read/reaction fields

### Notable Implementation Details
- Message list is reversed in DOM to work with `flex-col-reverse`, requiring reverse mapping before render
- Sentinel element positioned at end of DOM (visually at top) for IntersectionObserver infinite scroll
- Chat switching resets input, cursor, and focus state
- Modal closes on Escape key and backdrop click
- Send button disabled when input is empty or whitespace-only
- Unread count displays "99+" for counts exceeding 99

author: umputun
body:
Adds an opt-in compact diff mode that switches VCS diffs from full-file context to a small window around each change. Reviewing a small change in a large file (e.g. one key added to a 5000-line translations JSON) no longer requires scrolling through thousands of unchanged lines to reach it.

**Flags**

- `--compact` — start in compact mode (boolean, default off)
- `--compact-context=N` — context lines when compact is on (default 5)
- Env: `REVDIFF_COMPACT`, `REVDIFF_COMPACT_CONTEXT`
- Config file keys: `compact`, `compact-context`

**Runtime toggle**: `C` flips between compact and full-file at any time. Re-fetches the current file with the new context, lands the cursor on the first hunk. Other files re-fetch lazily on navigation.

**Status bar**: `⊂` (subset) glyph when compact mode is on.

**Design notes**

- Full-file remains the default. Compact is opt-in. Nothing changes for users who don't set the flag or press the key.
- Implemented at the diff-generation layer (passes `-U<N>` to git/hg/jj) rather than by hiding lines in the renderer. The parser and rendering pipeline already handle non-full-context diffs.
- Mode stacks naturally with `v` collapsed. Compact shrinks the VCS diff; collapsed hides removed lines on top.
- Non-diff sources (`--stdin`, `--all-files`, `--only` without VCS) get a `CompactApplicable` capability flag (same pattern as `CommitsApplicable`). `C` is a no-op there with a transient status-bar hint.
- New `contextLines int` parameter on `Renderer.FileDiff` threads the setting through the existing renderer chain. Breaking for internal consumers only, caught by the compiler.

Resolves the concrete friction raised in discussion #134.

author: jakobbskov
body:
## Summary

This PR continues issue #232 with a small cleanup of timed hold lifecycle handling in the workout execution flow.

It introduces a shared timed hold runtime state helper and updates the timed hold tick loop to read from that shared lifecycle view instead of repeating raw timer-state checks inline.

## What changed

Added:

- `getTimedHoldRuntimeState(entry)`

This helper derives a shared timed hold lifecycle view from the current entry, including:

- whether prep state exists
- whether active timer state exists
- remaining prep seconds
- remaining active seconds
- whether prep is currently running
- whether the hold is ready to start active timing
- whether the hold is ready to complete

Updated:

- `ensureTimedHoldTick(item)`

The tick loop now reads from `getTimedHoldRuntimeState(entry)` instead of repeating separate checks against raw timed hold fields.

## Why this helps

Timed hold execution still has its own lifecycle inside the broader workout engine.

Before this PR, `ensureTimedHoldTick(item)` inspected several raw timed hold fields inline and combined them into behavior decisions directly. That worked, but it made the lifecycle harder to read and easier to fragment over time.

After this PR, timed hold state reading is centralized in one helper, which makes the timer flow more understandable and gives future changes a single lifecycle view to build on.

## Scope

Included:

- frontend timed hold lifecycle cleanup
- shared timed hold runtime state helper
- simplified state reading in timed hold tick flow

Not included:

- no backend changes
- no UI redesign
- no manual workout state isolation fix
- no mixed summary metric fix
- no full timed hold rewrite

## Validation

Validated by checking frontend syntax and confirming that the timed hold tick flow now uses the shared lifecycle helper for prep/start/complete decisions.

## Issue

Closes part of #232

author: lennartvdm
body:
## Summary

Moves the Framer worldmap chunks into Vite's build graph and rewires their internal `React` / `ReactDOM` references so the map runs on Frankenstein's npm React instead of its own bundled copy. One React instance on the page, no behavioural changes to the compiled Panzoom / variant state machine, map stays bit-for-bit identical to `/frmrduplicate/`.

Replaces the dynamic-import-from-`public/` scaffold that was merged as PR #112. That version worked but pulled a second React 18.2 into the page — ~160KB of duplicate runtime, two fiber trees, no shared context.

## What changed

- `public/frmr-map/` → `src/frmr-map/` so Vite sees the chunks as build-graph modules.
- `chunk-5swt4qjj.mjs` patched in three places:
  1. Prepend `import * as __REACT__ from "react"` and `import * as __REACTDOM__ from "react-dom"`.
  2. Insert `x = __REACT__;` right before the big `var qn = x.Children, Ee = x.Component, ...` destructuring. Every React hook local the chunk later hands out (`Ze` = useState, `V` = useRef, `$` = useEffect, `ae` = useMemo, `se` = useCallback, `A` = useContext, `Ae` = forwardRef, `dl` = createElement, `Ti` = useId, etc.) now resolves to npm React.
  3. Change `var un = ln, ...` to `var un = __REACTDOM__, ...` so `createRoot`, `createPortal`, `flushSync`, etc. resolve to npm react-dom.
- `chunk-yswte6p7.mjs`: the hardcoded `href: "./assets/worldmap.svg"` becomes `href: __WORLDMAP_SVG__`, imported via Vite's `?url` suffix — the SVG is hashed and served under `BASE_URL` in both dev and prod.
- `bootstrap.mjs`: now uses static npm imports (`createElement`, `createRoot`) and a single named import of `MapComponent` from the map chunk.
- `WorldMapSection.jsx`: static import of bootstrap; removes the runtime dynamic-import dance.
- Dropped unused `base.css` / `index.page.css` that were only loaded by the original Framer `index.html`.

## Why this is safe

- Both the host app and the Framer chunk resolve `react@^18.2.0`, so npm gives them the same install. Single React instance on the page, verified by the built `WorldMapSection-*.js` importing hooks from the `vendor-*.js` chunk.
- The chunk's `x.version = "18.2.0"` and its own internal React-building code still run, but the object they populate is reassigned away before any consumer destructures from it — dead writes, no behavioural effect.
- `react-dom` (not `react-dom/client`) is used for `__REACTDOM__` because the chunk destructures the full ReactDOM surface (`createPortal`, `findDOMNode`, `hydrate`, etc.); the full package exposes all of them plus `createRoot`.
- No changes to compiled Panzoom, the variant state machine, `useVariantState`, or any of the SDK primitives — they all just run against npm React's hook dispatcher now.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` succeeds; `WorldMapSection-*.js` imports from `vendor-*.js`.
- [x] Dev server serves transformed `bootstrap.mjs`, `chunk-5swt4qjj.mjs`, and `WorldMapSection.jsx` without errors.
- [ ] Visual check on `/` slide 4: map renders, camera pans between cities (Leiden, Vienna, etc.) identically to `/frmrduplicate/`.
- [ ] Navigate away and back to slide 4 — no unmount warnings, Panzoom resumes cleanly.

author: alydevs
body:
Spec: https://emby.media/support/articles/Strm-Files.html

The .strm format consists of a URI or local path as the sole contents of a text file, this is parsed by software like Emby or Jellyfin to treat remote streams or paths as if they are in the local filesystem. This PR adds .strm to mpv's internal list of playlist file formats, and points it to the handler for ~~.txt~~ .m3u files as they should be compatible.

~~I have not tested the code in this PR yet as I wasn't able to compile mpv locally, but will test using the artifact produced for this PR by CI.~~

-----

The initial state of this PR didn't work, but I confirmed that .m3u is the only supported playlist type that is compatible with .strm, and the latest commit switches the handler from txt to m3u. .strm doesn't need all the features of m3u/m3u8, but they do not cause issues with the relatively barebones playlist format of strm.

body:
## Summary
Users lose awareness of running minion sessions once they switch views or tab away. The only current signal is a 2px pulsing dot in SessionList rows — invisible from Canvas/Ship views, hidden when the mobile strip is collapsed, and silent in the browser tab title.

This PR surfaces running-session state in three places:

- **Header badge** (`RunningBadge`): always-visible pill showing `● N running`. Renders across list/canvas/ship views and on mobile. Clicking jumps to the first running session and switches back to list mode. Hidden when `N = 0`.
- **Document title**: `ActiveView` writes `(N) Minions UI` when at least one session is running or pending, so the browser tab updates while the user is elsewhere.
- **ChatPane header**: status text is now color-coded (blue bold for running/pending, red bold for failed, green for completed) so the current session's state reads at a glance.

Pure helpers live in `src/state/running.ts` (`isActive`, `countRunning`, `firstRunningId`) and have unit tests. `RunningBadge` has component tests covering the zero-count hidden state, the count rendering, and the click-to-jump behavior.

## Assumptions
- "Running" is defined as `status === 'running' || status === 'pending'`, matching the existing `stoppable` rule in `ChatPane` and the isActive definition the Canvas already uses.
- Title is scoped to the active connection's sessions only (consistent with the rest of the UI, which shows one connection at a time).
- Clicking the badge is an acceptable navigation shortcut even when `viewMode` is canvas/ship — reuses `handleOpenChat`, which already switches to list mode.

## Notes
- No existing tests covered "running indicator" behavior in this area; added two new test files alongside the changes.
- Local `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test` could not run in this sandbox — `node_modules` is not present in the worktree (sibling worktrees have theirs, this one shipped without). Pre-commit hook (husky → eslint) fails for the same reason. Relying on `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for validation.
- No favicon manipulation / manifest badge counter here — those are broader PWA changes worth a separate PR.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright)
- [ ] Start a session → header shows `● 1 running` and tab title becomes "(1) Minions UI"
- [ ] Switch to Canvas view → badge still visible; title still updated
- [ ] Click badge → focuses first running session in list mode
- [ ] Session completes → badge disappears; title reverts to "Minions UI"
- [ ] ChatPane header: "running" text reads blue/bold, "completed" reads green

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Replaces the process-wide PTY singleton on `/ws/terminal` with a fresh `bash` + pty per connection. This is the shared-PTY audit finding and the last piece of the backend hardening pass. **Before** The daemon held one pair of globals — `g_term_master_fd` / `g_term_pid` — plus `g_term_mutex`. The first WebSocket client would fork a bash and attach; any subsequent client would reuse the same master fd. That meant: - two clients connected simultaneously echoed each other's keystrokes and saw each other's output - disconnecting didn't kill the shell — the next client inherited the prompt, background jobs, and environment - if the shell ever died, a small window existed where two clients could race to spawn a replacement **After** - `skm_term_spawn(out_fd, out_pid)` does `openpty` + `fork` + `execle("/bin/bash", …, "--login", …)` and returns a master fd + pid that belong to this handler frame only. No globals, no mutex. - `skm_term_teardown(fd, pid)` closes the master, sends `SIGHUP`, does a non-blocking `waitpid` for up to ~500 ms, then `SIGKILL` + blocking `waitpid`. Runs on every exit path — spawn failure, read-loop break, EOF, WS close frame. - `TIOCSWINSZ` / `SIGWINCH` target the handler's own `pid`, not a global. - The handler sends a WS close frame (`0x8`) before tearing down so clients see a clean disconnect. - Existing `skm_terminal_sanitize_text` / resize JSON / masking path are untouched — framing/protocol is identical from the iOS side. Compiles clean with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -std=c11`. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Open two iOS clients at the same time against the daemon, type in each — neither should see the other's output. Previously they would. - [ ] Disconnect one client and reconnect — new prompt should be a fresh bash (empty history within the session, `$$` different), not the previous session's continuation. - [ ] Resize the terminal on the iOS side and run `tput cols` / `tput lines` in bash — values should match after resize. This exercises `TIOCSWINSZ` + `SIGWINCH` with the new per-connection pid. - [ ] Kill the shell manually (`exit` or `kill -9 $$`) and verify the WS disconnects cleanly instead of hanging until timeout. - [ ] Stress: open + close 20 WS terminal sessions rapidly, then check `ps -ef | grep bash` on the PS4 — no leftover orphaned bash children. ### Notes - This is a behavior change inside the terminal handler only. No API surface, no JSON schema, no iOS change needed. - Forking from a multi-threaded daemon is already the pattern this codebase used — the risk profile is the same as before, it just happens per connection instead of once. - No runtime verification possible from my side (no PS4 / Strawberry kernel on the VM) — static review + clean `-Werror` compile only. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ccf25c606e3a40d3b7245b34ce544864 Requested by: @KolliasG7 ---

author: jasonherald
body:
## Summary

- Adds an explicit \`@MainActor deinit\` on \`CoreModel\` that cancels the event-consumer Task as a safety net for model drops that don't go through \`shutdown()\` (test scopes, hypothetical multi-window futures).
- Deletes the "No explicit deinit — tracked by issue #293" block comment that the Swift 5.x-era concurrency wall forced us to leave behind.

Closes #293.

## Why this lands now

Issue #293 tracks the original blocker from PR #292 round 2: \`@ObservationTracked\`-generated storage for \`@Observable\` classes couldn't be accessed from a \`deinit\` because macro-generated mutable stored properties couldn't be \`nonisolated\` and the class-level \`@MainActor\` didn't propagate to \`deinit\` by default on older toolchains.

The Swift 6.3 / Xcode 26 toolchain the project now uses supports \`@MainActor deinit\` directly — the macro storage is readable from the isolated deinit without any \`nonisolated\`-wrapping. Verified with a clean build + the full \`CoreModelIntegrationTests\` suite (8 tests, all pass).

## Regression test

\`testDeinitReleasesModelWithoutShutdown\` in \`CoreModelIntegrationTests.swift\`:

1. Inside a nested \`do { }\` scope, construct a \`CoreModel\`, call \`bootstrap(configPath:)\` to spawn the event-consumer Task, capture a \`weak var\` reference.
2. Exit the scope — explicitly WITHOUT calling \`shutdown()\`.
3. Yield a few times to let the cancelled Task's \`for await\` loop unwind.
4. Assert the weak reference is nil → the model released, which can only happen if the deinit ran.

Uses the nested-\`do { }\` pattern from the \`feedback_swift_release\` memory — \`let _ = m\` at test scope doesn't actually release until the test method returns, which would false-positive the weak-ref check.

## Test plan

- [x] \`xcodebuild test\` \`CoreModelIntegrationTests\` — all 8 tests pass, including the new one (ran locally)
- [ ] CI run on the PR

body:
## Summary

`processOCR.ts` の `rescueStuckProcessingDocs()` において、2 件の silent bug を修正。

1. **無限 rescue ループ**: retryCount を無制限にインクリメント、MAX_RETRY_COUNT チェックなし → 429 多発時に rescue が止まらない
2. **即再処理による連鎖**: retryAfter 未設定 → 429 救済直後に再処理されて同じエラーで戻る連鎖

## 対応

`handleProcessingError` (ocrProcessor.ts:409) の既存パターンを踏襲:
- MAX_RETRY_COUNT (=5) 到達 → `status: error` 確定
- 上限未満 → `status: pending` + `retryAfter` 3 分付与 (`STUCK_RESCUE_RETRY_AFTER_MS`)

## 変更

| ファイル | 変更内容 |
|---|---|
| `functions/src/ocr/ocrProcessor.ts` | `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` を export (rescue 関数から参照) |
| `functions/src/ocr/processOCR.ts` | rescue 関数に上限チェック + retryAfter 分岐、定数 `STUCK_RESCUE_RETRY_AFTER_MS` 追加 |
| `functions/test/ocrProcessor.test.ts` | `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` チェック 4 ケース + `retryAfter` 設定 3 ケース = **+7 テスト** |
| `.gitignore` | `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` 追加 (Cron hook の session-local 除外) |

## retryAfter 3 分の根拠

stuck = 10 分以上 processing のまま → 高負荷 / quota 枯渇が主要因と推定。
`handleProcessingError` の quota 値 (3 分) と揃えることで一貫性確保。

author: copilot
body:
This PR reworks the API into an explicit versioned model and introduces a new `/api/v2` surface built around path-based, multi-method resource routes. It also moves the dashboard onto that API boundary, adds shared-folder support, shortens public share URLs for browser and upcoming CLI use, and consolidates the legacy version 1 API so `app/api/v1` contains the actual v1 handlers without a duplicate unversioned route layer.

## Changes Made

- Added `/api/v2` as the canonical API with path-based resource routes for files, folders, shares, preferences, storage, and bulk operations.
- Consolidated the legacy API so `app/api/v1` now contains the real version 1 route handlers instead of re-export stubs.
- Removed the duplicate unversioned legacy route files under `app/api/*`, leaving only explicit versioned API surfaces plus the existing public share redirect route.
- Introduced shared API contracts, response/error helpers, auth guards, path normalization, folder/file resolution, and resource services under `lib/api/*`.
- Migrated dashboard file, folder, share, preferences, storage, upload, move, delete, restore, and favorite flows onto the centralized API client and logical path model.
- Verified the site’s components, routes, and client helpers use the latest `/api/v2` endpoints internally.
- Added short public share routes at `/s/[token]` and support for both file-backed and folder-backed shares.
- Updated database migration support for folder shares, short share tokens, and active sibling uniqueness constraints.
- Added dashboard UI support for folder sharing by generalizing the share dialog to work for both files and folders.
- Fixed the dashboard top-bar breadcrumbs so they render in the correct order and navigate using the actual logical folder paths.

## Feedback Fixes Included

- Tightened `shared_links` RLS so authenticated share management only sees shares owned through the user’s files or folders, while public share resolution continues through the admin client.
- Fixed shared dashboard/resource queries to avoid broad `shared_links` scans and large `IN (...)` filters by querying owned shared resources through joined relations.
- Reused folder path caches when building share target summaries to avoid repeated per-share folder cache creation.
- Hardened path decoding so malformed percent-encoded path segments return `invalid_path` instead of surfacing as 500s.
- Fixed folder listing metadata counts so excluded folders are not still counted in `meta.counts`.
- Hardened download headers by generating safe `Content-Disposition` values for file names with quotes, backslashes, or control characters.
- Removed the unused server import flagged in review feedback.
- Improved the `short_token` migration backfill to enforce non-null/check constraints, add owner-aware policies, add lookup indexing, and retry bounded token generation before uniqueness enforcement.
- Wired folder share actions into the dashboard’s folder grid and list menus so folder sharing is available from the same UI surface as file sharing.
- Corrected breadcrumb link generation to use server-provided paths directly instead of rebuilding links from display names.
- Removed the remaining duplicate unversioned v1 route layer and moved the actual legacy handlers into `app/api/v1/*` for a clearer, easier-to-maintain versioned API layout.

## Validation

- ✅ TypeScript compilation passes with `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
- ⚠️ `npm run lint` cannot complete in the current repo environment because the `lint` script references `eslint` but the package is not installed
- ✅ `npm run build` completes successfully
- ✅ Automated code review completed without review comments on the final UI and route-layout changes
- ⚠️ CodeQL reported 0 alerts during validation attempts, but its analysis execution did not complete successfully

author: bokelley
body:
## Summary

- Adds a fifth narrative bullet to `universal/idempotency.yaml` documenting that error responses (returned envelopes, thrown envelopes, uncaught exceptions) MUST NOT cache — the next request carrying the same key re-executes the handler. Covers every recovery class, including `terminal` (most terminal codes are state-dependent: `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` flips after remediation, `ACCOUNT_PAYMENT_REQUIRED` flips after payment). Calls out the handler-author mutate-last contract.
- Adds a reviewer check on `key_reuse_conflict` requiring the reviewer to confirm — via seller docs or a manual probe — that errored requests release the idempotency claim (retry with same key + valid payload must return fresh success, not `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and not the cached error).

Closes https://github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp/issues/2760.

## Why this over an end-to-end phase

The issue proposes an `error_claim_release` phase that forces a deterministic terminal error and retries the key. The author explicitly labels the narrative-bullet + reviewer-check path as the minimum viable alternative: "If adding an end-to-end phase is too heavy (the 'force a terminal error' step needs a controller hook that not every specialism has), the minimum viable change is the narrative bullet above, plus a reviewer checklist item on `key_reuse_conflict`."

No generic force-terminal-error controller verb exists yet. Using the existing `force_account_status → suspended` scenario would bloat the universal storyboard with account-lifecycle setup already tested by `deterministic_testing`, and would miss non-account-bound terminal codes. The narrative bullet flags this follow-up inline: "An end-to-end phase that drives a deterministic terminal error and replays the key is deferred pending a generic force-error controller verb (see adcontextprotocol/adcp#2760)."

The spec is already normative on this (security.mdx#idempotency rule 3: "Only successful responses are cached"). The storyboard change makes the invariant visible to storyboard readers and reviewable at conformance time.

author: deodat-lawson
body:
## Summary

Restructures the repo from a single Next app into a pnpm workspace with three packages, splitting the business-agnostic engine from product features and the web host.

- **`packages/core` (`@launchstack/core`)** — framework-agnostic engine: RAG, ingestion, OCR, embeddings, knowledge graph, LLM abstractions, storage/db/crypto. Ready to publish (changesets + publish scaffolding).
- **`packages/features` (`@launchstack/features`)** — product modules: `adeu`, `client-prospector`, `marketing-pipeline`, `repo-explainer`, `trend-search`, `voice`, `legal-templates`, `company-metadata`, `doc-ingestion`, plus placeholder subpackages for `mcp`, `rules-extraction`, `workflow-generation`, `connectors`.
- **`apps/web`** — the Next.js host. Owns routes, UI, drizzle migrations, scripts (`ensure-pgvector`, `backfill-document-versions`), and tests.

## Decoupling

Core no longer reaches into app env or singletons. Host code wires dependencies via `configure*` hooks and ports:

- `createEngine` + `CoreConfig`
- `StoragePort`, `JobDispatcherPort`, `CreditsPort`, `RagPort`
- `configureDatabase` / `configureStorage` / `configureChatModels` / `configureProviders` / `configureNeo4j`
- Providers/registry and `TOKEN_COSTS` decoupled; `getOpenAIClient()` and `getChatModel` lifted into core.

## Tooling

- pnpm workspaces (`apps/*`, `packages/*`); `tsconfig.base.json` with path aliases.
- Jest `moduleNameMapper` for `@launchstack/*` subpaths.
- ESLint boundary guards preventing `apps/web` internals from leaking into core/features and vice-versa.
- Changesets configured for `@launchstack/core` releases.
- Dockerfile, `Dockerfile.prebuilt`, compose, and `next.config.ts` updated for the new layout.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across core, features, web
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @pdr-ai/web test` — full Jest suite green
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @launchstack/core build` produces `dist/`

author: jychp
body:
### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Other (please describe):


### Summary

Follow-up to #2653 fixing two classes of mismatch between cartography's ontology and the underlying provider semantics — both surfaced while reviewing the result of that PR.

**1. Azure container group/instance labels were inverted.**
`AzureContainerInstance` actually models the *container group* (the Azure ACI resource that holds N containers), and `AzureGroupContainer` actually models each individual container inside it. The Azure SDK calls the group `container_groups` (`ContainerInstanceManagementClient.container_groups.list()`) which is what made the cartography names land backwards historically. Swap them so the graph labels match the semantics: `AzureContainerInstance` = individual container (carries `:Container`), `AzureGroupContainer` = group.

**2. Cloud Run Service / Job were modeled as `:Function`, but they are orchestrators.**
- `GCPCloudRunJob` is a managed batch orchestrator (closer to AWS Batch or an ECS Fargate task than to Lambda). It is now a pure grouping node. Each container declared in `job.template.template.containers` becomes a `GCPCloudRunContainer` child carrying `:Container` and `HAS_IMAGE`.
- `GCPCloudRunService` is a long-running HTTP orchestrator with multi-container deployments and traffic-splitting versioning (closer to `ECSService` than to Lambda). It loses `:Function`. Each container declared in `service.template.containers` (the `latestReadyRevision` spec, which the v2 API returns inline) becomes a `GCPCloudRunContainer` child.
- `GCPCloudRunRevision` was carrying `HAS_IMAGE` and image fields despite being just a versioned config snapshot of the Service. Strip it to pure metadata; per-container image data lives on the Service's container children.

This matches the pattern established by ECS in cartography — only individual runtime containers carry `:Container` / `HAS_IMAGE`; orchestrators (`ECSService`, `ECSTask`, `ECSTaskDefinition`) do not. Cloud Run does not expose runtime containers, so the ``latestReadyRevision`` spec is treated as the canonical "what runs" for cross-cloud parity.

Three commits kept separate for review ergonomics:
1. `refactor(azure): swap AzureContainerInstance and AzureGroupContainer labels`
2. `refactor(gcp-cloudrun): split Job into grouping node with GCPCloudRunContainer children`
3. `refactor(gcp-cloudrun): drop :Function from Service, model containers as Service children, strip Revision`


### Related issues or links

Follow-up to #2653 — no GitHub issue.


### Breaking changes

This PR is intentionally breaking; release notes need to call this out clearly.

**Compatibility migrations are bundled.** Two analysis jobs run automatically on the next sync to relabel existing graphs:
- ``azure_container_label_swap_migration.json`` — swaps the Azure labels via a temporary intermediate label to avoid collisions, then strips any stale ``:Container`` from groups.
- ``gcp_cloudrun_label_migration.json`` — strips ``:Function`` from existing ``GCPCloudRunService`` and ``GCPCloudRunJob`` nodes; strips stale ``:Container`` from ``GCPCloudRunRevision``.

**Cypher changes that downstream queries must adopt:**

*Azure*
- ``MATCH (n:Container) ...`` now matches ``AzureContainerInstance`` instead of ``AzureGroupContainer``.
- ``(g:AzureContainerInstance)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:AzureGroupContainer)`` becomes ``(g:AzureGroupContainer)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:AzureContainerInstance)``.
- ``ip_address`` / ``ip_address_type`` / subnet ``ATTACHED_TO`` / tags now live on ``AzureGroupContainer`` (the group) — previously on ``AzureContainerInstance``.
- ``image`` / ``image_digest`` / cpu/memory request+limit live on ``AzureContainerInstance`` (the individual container).

*GCP Cloud Run Job*
- ``GCPCloudRunJob`` no longer carries ``:Function``. Cross-cloud queries that filter on ``:Function`` must additionally include ``:Container`` (or query ``GCPCloudRunContainer`` directly) to include Job containers.
- ``(j:GCPCloudRunJob)-[:HAS_IMAGE]->(i)`` and ``(j:GCPCloudRunJob)-[:RESOLVED_IMAGE]->(i)`` are gone. New traversal: ``(j:GCPCloudRunJob)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:GCPCloudRunContainer)-[:HAS_IMAGE|RESOLVED_IMAGE]->(i)``.
- The flat array properties on Job (``container_image``, ``container_images``, ``image_digest``, ``image_digests``, ``architecture*``) are removed; these fields live on each ``GCPCloudRunContainer`` child instead.

*GCP Cloud Run Service*
- ``GCPCloudRunService`` no longer carries ``:Function``. Cross-cloud ``:Function`` queries no longer include Cloud Run Services.
- ``(s:GCPCloudRunService)-[:RESOLVED_IMAGE]->(i)`` (created previously by traversing ``HAS_REVISION``) is gone. New traversal: ``(s:GCPCloudRunService)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:GCPCloudRunContainer)-[:RESOLVED_IMAGE]->(i)``. The Service-via-``HAS_REVISION`` statements in ``resolved_image_analysis.json`` are removed.

*GCP Cloud Run Revision*
- ``GCPCloudRunRevision`` no longer carries ``HAS_IMAGE`` to any image registry node, and the flat image / architecture properties (``container_image``, ``container_images``, ``image_digest``, ``image_digests``, ``architecture*``) are removed. Revision is now a pure versioning marker.

**``GCPCloudRunContainer`` parent semantics:** the new ``GCPCloudRunContainer`` schema is shared between Job-children and Service-children. Each node has exactly one parent; ``job_id`` and ``service_id`` are mutually exclusive (the rel matcher whose target id is ``None`` does not resolve, so only one ``CONTAINS`` rel is created per node).


### How was this tested?

- ``uv run --frozen pre-commit run --files <touched files>`` → passes (black, isort, flake8, mypy, pyupgrade).
- 17 targeted integration tests pass:
  - ``tests/integration/cartography/intel/azure/test_container_instances.py`` (2)
  - ``tests/integration/cartography/intel/azure/test_group_containers.py`` (2)
  - ``tests/integration/cartography/intel/azure/test_compute_exposure.py`` (2)
  - ``tests/integration/cartography/intel/gcp/test_cloudrun.py`` (2) — image prerequisites test now asserts ``HAS_IMAGE`` on ``GCPCloudRunContainer`` parented to Service AND Job
  - ``tests/integration/cartography/intel/ontology/test_resolved_images.py`` (3) — Cloud Run RESOLVED_IMAGE now lands on ``:Container`` for both Service and Job containers; no Function path for any GCP node
- Test mocks updated to include ``service.template.containers[]`` (matches the actual v2 API response shape — see ``RevisionTemplate`` in ``projects.locations.services``).


### Checklist

#### General
- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://cartography-cncf.github.io/cartography/dev/developer-guide.html).
- [x] The linter passes locally (`make lint`).
- [x] I have added/updated tests that prove my fix is effective or my feature works.

#### Proof of functionality
- [x] New or updated unit/integration tests.

#### If you are adding or modifying a synced entity
- [ ] Included Cartography sync logs from a real environment.
  (Not included — this PR reshapes existing synced entities; coverage is via integration tests using mocked API responses, including the ``service.template.containers`` shape that exists but was previously unread.)

#### If you are changing a node or relationship
- [x] Updated the [schema documentation](https://github.com/cartography-cncf/cartography/tree/master/docs/root/modules) (Azure, GCP, Ontology).
- [ ] Updated the [schema README](https://github.com/cartography-cncf/cartography/blob/master/docs/schema/README.md).
  (Not applicable — README is unchanged by these edits.)


### Notes for reviewers

- The Azure "swap" looks aggressive in the diff but it is a near-mechanical rename: file contents move between the two model files, class names follow, graph

author: nowireless4u
body:
Fixes #141. Reported by Zach Jennings.

## Summary
- `central_manage_wlan_profile` update now issues a `PATCH` against Central instead of a `PUT`. A partial payload (e.g. `{"dtim-period": 2}`) no longer wipes every other field in the profile.
- Added `replace_existing: bool = False` parameter as an explicit, opt-in path to the old PUT full-replacement behavior for the rare case where the caller genuinely wants a wholesale swap.
- Elicitation prompt for partial updates now fetches the current profile and shows a per-key `before → after` diff. The user sees exactly which fields will change before approving.

## Root cause (recap)
[src/hpe_networking_mcp/platforms/central/tools/wlan_profiles.py:186-200 (pre-fix)](https://github.com/nowireless4u/hpe-networking-mcp/blob/main/src/hpe_networking_mcp/platforms/central/tools/wlan_profiles.py#L186-L200) used `{"update": "PUT"}` and passed the caller's payload as the full request body. Central's `PUT /network-config/v1alpha1/wlan-ssids/{ssid}` is full-resource replacement — anything not in the body is dropped.

## Why PATCH and not client-side read-modify-write
Central's API spec ([api-endpoints/central/wlan.json:295-372](api-endpoints/central/wlan.json#L295-L372)) declares PATCH as a first-class operation on this endpoint. Server-side merge is strictly better than a client-side GET-merge-PUT:

- Single round trip
- Atomic on the server — no race window between GET and PUT
- Merge semantics come from Central's spec, not from us re-implementing them
- Smaller request bodies (only changed fields)

## Behavior matrix

| `action_type` | `replace_existing` | HTTP method | Payload must contain |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | (ignored) | `POST` | Full new profile |
| `update` | `False` (default) | `PATCH` | Only the fields to change |
| `update` | `True` | `PUT` | Full profile — unlisted fields are DROPPED |
| `delete` | (ignored) | `DELETE` | — |

## Elicitation example (partial update)
Before (generic, what the user used to see):
```
The LLM wants to update an existing WLAN profile 'z56'. Do you accept?
```

After (shows the actual diff):
```
The LLM wants to patch (partial update of) WLAN profile 'z56'.

Changes:
dtim-period: 1 → 2

Do you accept?
```

For `replace_existing=True` the message switches to:
```
The LLM wants to REPLACE THE ENTIRE WLAN profile 'z56'.

Changes:
⚠️  replace_existing=True — any field not in the payload will be DROPPED.
Payload top-level keys: ['dtim-period', 'essid', 'opmode', ...]

Do you accept?
```

body:
Refactor: Optimize dashboard widget render cycles

- **StableStatsTable.tsx:** Replaced inline anonymous functions for sort toggles with stable references via `onClick={toggleSort}` and updated child `TableHeader` components to call it with their specific `id`. This restores `React.memo` benefits for table columns.
- **BoutCard.tsx:** Extracted the static `TACTICS_CONFIG` array out of the render body, stopping React from re-creating the array structure and triggering re-renders every cycle.
- **YushoRaceWidget.tsx:** Swapped chained array `.filter().map()` calls for a direct `for...of` loop over `world.rikishi.values()`, eliminating intermediate memory allocations when querying the world roster for makuuchi rikishi.
- **MatchDayViewer.tsx:** Wrapped an expensive `sortedMatches.reduce` operation in a `useMemo` block so `completedCount` isn't blindly recalculated on every prop check.
- **PreBashoAssessment.tsx:** Fixed a prop-drilling defect where `AssessmentList` expected a `world` prop but was receiving `rikishiMap={world.rikishi}`, causing potential crashes. Swapped `Array.from().map()` for an imperative loop building up nodes, yielding cleaner map processing.

author: kamran-rapidfireai
body:
# What does this PR do?

Refreshes the RapidFire AI integration guide ([`docs/source/rapidfire_integration.md`](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/docs/source/rapidfire_integration.md)) to cover features shipped in `rapidfireai` v0.14.x–v0.15.x since the original guide landed in #4340 (Oct 29, 2025).

### What's new in the article

- **Multi-GPU Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP)** — new subsection under "Advanced Features" with an end-to-end `RFSFTConfig` + `fsdp` / `fsdp_config` example and links to the FSDP tutorial notebooks (SFT lite, SFT large, DPO).
- **Pluggable metric tracking backends** — new subsection covering MLflow (default), TensorBoard (default in Colab), and Trackio, selectable via the new `--tracking-backends` flag or `RF_*_ENABLED` environment variables.
- **Google Colab support** — short subsection noting Colab as a zero-setup path for SFT / DPO / GRPO tutorials.
- **Reframed opener + "Why use RapidFire AI with TRL?" section** — leads with the contrast vs. plain TRL (sequential vs. concurrent training of N configs on the same GPUs) so the value prop lands on first read.

### Small accuracy fixes folded in

- Bumped PyTorch prerequisite to `2.8+` (matches current rapidfireai README) and noted that multiple GPUs are required for FSDP.
- Fixed the dashboard port (`3000` → `8853`, the default since rapidfireai v0.12.4) and normalized the dashboard URL to `http://localhost:8853` consistently.
- Updated the SFT / DPO / GRPO example notebook links to their new `tutorial_notebooks/fine-tuning/` and `tutorial_notebooks/post-training/` subfolders.
- Harmonized "clone-modify (with or without warm starting)" terminology across the article so it matches the upstream rapidfireai README.

### Scope

Documentation only — 1 file changed, +114 / -26 lines. No code changes, no new tests required. Verified that all imports, command snippets, env var defaults, and FSDP example values match `RapidFireAI/rapidfireai` v0.15.2 source.

This was reviewed internally on our fork before opening here.

## Before submitting

- [x] This PR fixes a typo or improves the docs (you can dismiss the other checks if that's the case).
- [x] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#create-a-pull-request), Pull Request section?
- [x] Was this discussed/approved via a GitHub issue? No — this is a refresh of an existing integration doc that was previously approved and merged in #4340.
- [x] Did you make sure to update the documentation with your changes? This PR _is_ the documentation change.
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests? n/a — docs-only change.

## AI writing disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted: some parts were suggested or improved by AI, but the PR was written and reviewed by a human.

## Who can review?

cc @qgallouedec — you reviewed and merged the original integration guide in #4340, would appreciate your eyes again. Happy to iterate on wording/structure.

> **Low Risk**
> Docs-only changes; main risk is minor user confusion if any updated commands, ports, or links are incorrect.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refreshes `rapidfire_integration.md` to better frame RapidFire AI’s value prop vs plain TRL (live concurrent N-config training), adds project links, and reorganizes/expands the feature list.
> 
> Adds new documentation for **multi-GPU FSDP** (end-to-end `fsdp`/`fsdp_config` example + notebook links), **selectable experiment tracking backends** (MLflow/TensorBoard/Trackio via `--tracking-backends` or `RF_*_ENABLED` env vars), and a short **Google Colab** section.
> 
> Fixes/updates several doc details: PyTorch prerequisite to `2.8+`, clarifies multi-GPU behavior, standardizes IC Ops terminology to “clone-modify”, corrects the default dashboard URL/port to `http://localhost:8853`, and updates tutorial notebook links to new subfolders.

body:
## Summary

You added a **Basic Yearly** price in Stripe ($200/yr — save 2 months vs $20×12=$240). The code was already wired for Pro yearly but Basic yearly would have silently upgraded the subscriber to Pro because of the webhook's "everything non-basic = pro" mapping. This PR wires Basic yearly end-to-end, matching the Pro structure.

## What changed

**Backend**
- New env var `STRIPE_BASIC_YEARLY_PRICE_ID`, declared in `render.yaml` so Render prompts you for it on the next deploy.
- `subscribe_checkout` accepts `plan=basic_yearly` and resolves it to the new price.
- **Webhook fix:** `checkout.session.completed` now maps both the monthly and yearly Basic price IDs onto `Store.plan='basic'`. Previously the yearly Basic price would fall to the "else" branch and set the plan to "pro" — a real bug, not just a missing feature.
- `stripe_health_check` + `superadmin_controls` surface the new price (`env.basic_yearly_price_id`, `price_ok.basic_yearly`).

**Frontend (`/subscribe`)**
- Basic card mirrors the Pro card's monthly + yearly two-button layout.
- **Both** yearly buttons (and their "save $N" copy) are now gated on their respective env var being set. Without the env var, the yearly button just doesn't render, instead of appearing and then bouncing the user back with "Invalid plan selected".

## Tests — 213 passing

- `test_subscribe_shows_yearly_buttons_when_configured` — with both yearly env vars set, $200 and $300 + plan names appear.
- `test_subscribe_hides_yearly_buttons_when_unset` — clean state hides both yearly options.
- `test_checkout_redirects_to_stripe_for_basic_yearly` — checkout passes the correct price ID.
- `test_webhook_maps_basic_yearly_price_to_basic_plan` — regression guard against the old upgrade bug.

## What you still need to do

Same as before for the Pro yearly — in the Render dashboard, set the new `STRIPE_BASIC_YEARLY_PRICE_ID` env var to the price ID of your $200/yr Basic price from Stripe. (Dashboard will prompt for it once this deploys since it's declared `sync: false` in `render.yaml`.)

body:
## Summary
- Updated `offline_ingest.py` PCA fit bootstrap logic in `maybe_fit_pca_model(...)` to keep training on week 1 while excluding weekend daily files.
- Added a local helper to derive a weekday-only `WeekPair` from week-1 paths using parsed dates and `date.weekday()` while preserving OB/TH alignment in trade-enabled mode.
- Added a local helper to count PCA-eligible rows by reusing `_stream_core_features(...)`.
- Replaced first-N-row collection plus full-week incremental continuation with a two-pass centered contiguous block policy:
  - `total_rows`
  - `block_size = min(sample_limit, total_rows)`
  - `start_idx = max(0, (total_rows - block_size) // 2)`
  - collect exactly `block_size` rows from the weekday stream
- Fit `IncrementalPCA` on sampled block only and stopped (removed pending/flush continuation over remaining week rows).
- Kept model save payload and meta shape intact; updated counters to reflect sampled-block fit (`rows_total`/`rows_fitted` based on sampled rows).

## Notes
- No changes were made to `main()` split logic, `process_all(...)`, or downstream PCA application paths.
